verdict.summary: In tipc_crypto_key_rcv, the untrusted message-derived key length skey->keylen is copied into skey->key before the only sanity check, enabling an out-of-bounds heap write.

evidence.reason: The copy length skey->keylen is attacker-controlled: it is read from the message at line 24 (skey->keylen = ntohl(*((__be32 *)(data + TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME)))), a u32 with full range 0..0xFFFFFFFF and no shown minimum or maximum. skey is allocated at line 17 as kmalloc(size, GFP_ATOMIC) where size = msg_data_sz(hdr) (u16, line 6), so the key flexible array starts at offset sizeof(u32)+TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME within a buffer of at most 65535 bytes. The only candidate guard, line 30 (if (unlikely(size != tipc_aead_key_size(skey)))), executes AFTER this memcpy and therefore cannot constrain skey->keylen before the copy (Phase 2 guard-after-use; Phase 4 reach/identity failure). A witness such as keylen=0xFFFFFFFF survives the BLOCK test: no shown statement before line 26 bounds keylen, and the memcpy writes that many bytes past the heap allocation. The absent one-statement fix is a bound check on skey->keylen (e.g., against the remaining allocated capacity) placed before line 26.

assumptions: struct tipc_aead_key has layout u32 keylen; char alg_name[TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME]; char key[]; with flexible array key at offset sizeof(u32)+TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME, so keylen bytes written at line 26-27 must fit within the kmalloc(size) allocation.
tipc_aead_key_size(skey) expands to sizeof(*skey) + skey->keylen.
limitations: The message read at data + TIPC_AEAD_ALG_NAME + sizeof(__be32) may also read past the message buffer, but the primary confirmed finding is the heap out-of-bounds write into skey->key.
The line 30 sanity check would be sufficient if it ran before the copy, but it is placed after it and provides no protection to the sink.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in FindEmptyObjectSlot are protected: the s_objects[i] access is bounded by the loop condition i < MAX_LOADED_OBJECTS, the *handle write is guarded by if(handle), and MemorySet zeroes a validated in-range slot with a matching size. No entry-point value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: The pointer write *handle is the only potentially dangerous dereference; the NULL check if(handle) on the same value on every reaching path excludes NULL, so its admitted set (non-NULL) has an empty intersection with the failure set. This guard passes the BREAK test (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach).

The s_objects[i] read is bounded by the loop guard i < MAX_LOADED_OBJECTS, admitting only i in [0, MAX_LOADED_OBJECTS-1], which is within the capacity of s_objects. The subsequent MemorySet(object, 0, sizeof(*object)) operates on this validated in-range slot with a matching size, so no OOB read/write is reachable.

object->attributes.occupied is readable before any initialization and CLEAR is the intended free-slot marker.
limitations: The NULL returned by return NULL (line 17) is dereferenced only by an unshown caller; no in-fragment dereference exists, so no NULL-deref finding is made here.

The whole-object initialization via MemorySet is a defensive-hardening step, but the verdict rests only on the guards shown (loop bound and if(handle)), not on whether the fragment is the fixed or vulnerable member.

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read of cp950_pua_tbl[] when the linear search loop (line 47) exhausts without finding a match: the post-loop code dereferences cp950_pua_tbl[k] with k equal to the table element count.

evidence.reason: After the search loop at line 47 (for k=0; k < N; k++ with N = sizeof(cp950_pua_tbl)/(sizeof(unsigned short)*4)), if no entry satisfies line 48 the loop exits with k == N. The code at lines 53-57 then reads cp950_pua_tbl[k][2], cp950_pua_tbl[k][0], and cp950_pua_tbl[k][2]>>8 with k == N, which is one past the N-element table — an OOB read (CWE-125). The only guards on the path are is_in_cp950_pua(c1,c) at line 45 (an unshown predicate that does not bound k) and the loop condition at line 47, which admits k == N after termination; neither constrains k < N before the access, so no protective statement survives the BREAK test. The absent one-statement fix is a post-loop bound check such as `if (k < N)` before line 53. c1 and c are attacker-controlled (c1 = filter->cache from a prior input byte at line 20, c from the current input), and c2 = (c1<<8)|c at line 46, so an attacker can reach the PUA branch and drive the search to miss.

assumptions: cp950_pua_tbl is an array whose element count equals sizeof(cp950_pua_tbl)/(sizeof(unsigned short)*4), so the index bound N is the element count (line 47).
c1 = filter->cache (line 30) originates from a prior input byte stored at line 20, making it attacker-controllable entry-point data.
limitations: The exact witness value requires is_in_cp950_pua(c1,c) (line 45) to return true for a c1/c pair that the table at line 48 does not contain; is_in_cp950_pua's body is not shown, so the concrete byte pair is not derivable from the fragment alone, capping confidence.
The big5_ucs_table[w] access (line 38) is fully guarded by line 37 (w >= 0 && w < big5_ucs_table_size) and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: The u32 multiplication elem_size * smap->map.max_entries in bpf_map_area_alloc can overflow, producing an undersized allocation that pcpu_freelist_populate then overflows with elem_size * max_entries bytes, yielding a heap out-of-bounds write.

evidence.reason: elem_size (line 3) and smap->map.max_entries are both u32, attacker-controlled BPF map-creation values with no shown upper bound, so their product is computed in u32 and wraps modulo 2^32 (CWE-190). No overflow guard precedes the allocation; the only checks are the allocation-failure NULL test (line 8) and freelist-init err test (line 12), neither of which constrains elem_size or max_entries. A witness such as elem_size = 0x10000 with max_entries = 0x10000 makes the product wrap to 0, the allocation succeeds small/non-NULL, and pcpu_freelist_populate (lines 15-16) writes max_entries * elem_size bytes into the undersized buffer, a heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787). The absent one-statement fix is an overflow check such as if (smap->map.max_entries > U32_MAX / elem_size) return -E2BIG; before the allocation.

Under standard semantics pcpu_freelist_populate writes max_entries elements each of elem_size bytes into smap->elems, whose allocation (line 6) may be smaller than that total when the u32 product wraps. The NULL/err guards do not prevent this overflow, so the write exceeds the allocated region.

assumptions: smap->map.value_size and smap->map.max_entries are u32 fields derived from BPF map-creation parameters (entry-point input) with no shown bound in this fragment.
bpf_map_area_alloc of a wrapped-small (e.g. 0) size can return a non-NULL pointer, so the line 8 NULL check passes.
limitations: The actual out-of-bounds write occurs inside pcpu_freelist_populate (body not shown); the failure is demonstrated by the standard semantics of that callee combined with the shown undersized allocation.
If the map-creation layer elsewhere bounds max_entries or value_size, that invariant is not visible in this fragment and is not relied upon here.

With a short skb (e.g. skb->len=3, data[0]=AID tag, aid_len=32) the L22-23 && guard does not return (true && false = false), so data[aid_len+2]=data[34] is read far beyond the 3-byte skb. OOB read (CWE-125): the memcpy source &skb->data[2] copies aid_len bytes (up to 32, admitted by the L33 check) but skb->len is unconstrained below 2+aid_len; a 3-byte skb with aid_len=32 copies 30 bytes past the end of the skb. No skb->len bound relative to aid_len exists; the missing fix is a skb->len < aid_len + N length check before the copy.

assumptions: skb->data and skb->len are derived from externally supplied NFC frames (entry-point input) and are attacker-controlled.
sizeof(transaction->aid) is the 32-byte NFC_MAX_AID_LENGTH, giving the L33 guard an admitted aid_len range of 0..32.

limitations: The spec comment (L15-21) stating AID length 5..16 is documentation, not executable protection, and is not credited.
The params memcpy destination write is bounded by the L47 allocation-size check, so the destination is not flagged; only the OOB skb->data source reads are confirmed.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds write in qtm_decompress: the wrap-branch match copy (line 108) writes match_length bytes starting at window[window_posn] with no bound against the remaining window space, so attacker-controlled match_length (length_base[sym]+extra+5, line 80) can exceed window_size - window_posn and overflow the window buffer.

The only guard on this path, line 98, bounds j = match_offset - window_posn, not i (wrong-target drift), leaving the write unconstrained. The missing one-statement fix is a cap equivalent to the else branch's line 112-113 (if (i > (int)(window_size - window_posn)) i = window_size - window_posn;).

A macro definition prefix of MAXSTRING non-newline characters reaches linelen == MAXSTRING (last in-bounds write at index MAXSTRING-1 via line 164), and the first argument character then writes index MAXSTRING past the MAXSTRING-element tmpFile.line; longer arguments write further. The absent one-statement fix is a linelen + arg.length > MAXSTRING bound check before this copy loop, and the guard at line 157 fails the guard-identity audit (check-then-use drift) because linelen is not re-verified before or during these writes.

assumptions: tmpFile.line has capacity MAXSTRING widechars, evidenced by the guard at line 157 combined with the same array/index write at line 164.
CharsString token/argument length is capped at MAXSTRING by getToken's standard semantics, so arg.length <= MAXSTRING.
Macro fields (definition, substitutions, argument_count) originate from the attacker-controlled table file via compileMacro at line 37.
limitations: The argument index arguments[m->substitutions[2 * subst + 1] - 1] at line 168 could be out of bounds only if compileMacro fails to validate substitution indices; compileMacro's body is not shown, so this is not confirmed.
char *s = malloc(sizeof(char) * (emphClass.length + 1)) is dereferenced without a NULL check; failure requires allocator exhaustion on a small allocation, so it is demoted.
The CTO_SeqAfterExpression write has no visible capacity for seqAfterExpression, so its bounds cannot be confirmed from the fragment.
The CTO_MultInd ruleChars append relies on getToken token granularity and line length limits, so it is not asserted as a finding.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in TIFFReadDirEntryArrayWithLimit are guarded: typesize==0 is rejected before the division, the two 2GB sanity checks bound count*typesize so datasize cannot overflow uint32, the mapped-file check bounds datasize by tif_size, and each inline _TIFFmemcpy is bounded (datasize<=4 for classic, datasize<=8 for bigtiff) to both the allocated buffer and the inline tdir_offset union, with data guaranteed allocated on those paths.

evidence.reason: Classic-TIFF inline copy is fully constrained: datasize (uint32, count*typesize with count*typesize<=2147483647 from L25) is at most 4, matching both the 4-byte tdir_offset union and the datasize-byte buffer allocated at L45; the L37-42 NULL branch requires datasize>4, so data is allocated and NULL-checked on this path. BREAK test passes on identity, boundary (4<=4), degenerate (1..4), and reach.

BigTIFF inline copy is fully constrained: datasize<=8 matches the 8-byte tdir_offset.toff_long8 union and the datasize-byte allocated buffer; the NULL branch requires datasize>8, so data is always allocated here. BREAK test passes on all four checks.

Rejects typesize==0 before the L25 division 2147483647/typesize and target_count64==0 before *count/datasize computation, so the only in-fragment zero-producer for the division sinks is excluded on every reaching path.

assumptions: TIFFDirEntry.tdir_count is uint32, so target_count64=min(tdir_count,maxcount) is at most UINT32_MAX and the cast at L30 is exact.
The tdir_offset union is 4 bytes in classic TIFF (toff_long) and 8 bytes in BigTIFF (toff_long8), matching the datasize<=4/datasize<=8 copy guards.
TIFFDataWidth returns the element width (1,2,4,8) for known types and 0 for unsupported ones, with the 0 case handled at L14.
limitations: desttypesize has no shown producer of 0 and no shown call site, so the L27 division-by-zero hazard is not derivable from the fragment (Phase 1c limitation), not a finding.

Bounds of the read at L60/L62 and L81/L83 (offset+datasize vs file size) are enforced inside the unshown callees TIFFReadDirEntryData/TIFFReadDirEntryDataAndRealloc; the L34 mapped datasize<=tif->tif_size check and tmsize_t cast of datasize (<=2GB from L25) are the fragment-visible constraints.
The L32 assert is debug-only and was not credited as protective; datasize>0 is actually guaranteed by L14 (count>=1, typesize>=1).

verdict.summary: Out-of-bounds read of the protobuf repeated field 'args' indexed by attacker-controlled edge src_output; the only guard is a debug-only DCHECK that is compiled out under NDEBUG.

evidence.reason: node_t.args(ix) indexes the repeated field without a runtime bounds check; ix is set from attacker-controlled edge->src_output() at line 17 with no shown upper bound. The sole guard, DCHECK(ix < node_t.args_size()) at line 41, is an assertion compiled out under NDEBUG and does not execute, so an admitted value ix >= node_t.args_size() reaches the unchecked protobuf operator[] and performs an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). assumptions: node_t.args() is protobuf RepeatedPtrField operator[], which does not bounds-check; the presence of the DCHECK implies out-of-range indices are expected unless guarded.
in_edges_ edge fields (dst_input, src_output) are derived from externally supplied graph data and are attacker-controlled.
limitations: DCHECK is debug-only and does not protect release builds; it is not credited as a protective statement.
input_nodes.at(i)/input_idx.at(i) at lines 16-17 use bounds-checked .at() and are not flagged.
If the caller's graph always produced src_output < args_size this would not trigger, but no such invariant is shown in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Unsigned underflow in the FLX frame-chunk size computation: attacker-controlled flxfh.size below FlxFrameChunkSize passes the only guard (avail >= flxfh.size) and underflows 'flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize' to a huge size fed to gst_adapter_take, whose NULL return is then dereferenced.

evidence.reason: flxfh.size is attacker-controlled (copied from adapter data at line 98, no validation). The only guard, line 105 'if (avail < flxfh.size)', bounds size only from above by avail (while avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize at line 90) and imposes no minimum, so any flxfh.size in [0, FlxFrameChunkSize-1] is admitted. For such values 'flxfh.size - FlxFrameChunkSize' underflows (CWE-191) to a huge unsigned size passed to gst_adapter_take, which per standard semantics returns NULL for an oversized request; chunk=NULL is then dereferenced at lines 113/114/128. The absent one-statement fix is a lower-bound check such as 'if (flxfh.size < FlxFrameChunkSize) goto need_more_data;' before the subtraction.

assumptions: FlxFrameChunkSize is the fixed size of the frame-chunk header (id+size fields), and avail >= FlxFrameChunkSize holds inside the while loop (line 90).
flxfh.size is a guint32 read from file data; unsigned subtraction wraps on underflow.
limitations: gst_adapter_take's return is not checked in the fragment; the NULL-deref consequence relies on its standard semantics of returning NULL for oversized requests.

Potential integer overflow in 'flxdec->size * 4' (line 124) and a possibly-NULL converter when depth > 8 (lines 67-69, 140) are secondary candidates not needed for the verdict and not independently confirmed from the shown code.
FlxFrameChunkSize's numeric value is a symbolic constant not defined in the fragment; the analysis uses it symbolically.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected by a verbatim statement that survives the BREAK test: fread's count argument caps n at sizeof(buf)-1 so buf[n]=0 reaches at most index 511 of the 512-byte buffer; fopen's NULL result is checked before use; log content is HTML-escaped before emission; the endpoint is gated by the is_readonly authorization check; and all StringBuffer_append calls use literal format strings.

evidence.reason: The fread count argument sizeof(buf) - 1 bounds n to at most 511 in the 512-element buf, so the write buf[n] = 0 on line 14 can never index past 511; BREAK boundary: failure set is index >= 512, maximum admitted value is 511, degenerate n=0 is excluded by the > 0 condition, and the same n (size_t, unmodified) is what the sink consumes — the guard is sufficient.

File-derived content is HTML-escaped by escapeHTML before it reaches the response body's textarea, neutralizing tag/metacharacter breakout (CWE-79 class); the sanitizing transformation executes on every iteration of the read loop before any content emission.

The authorization decision fails closed: a read-only session is rejected with SC_FORBIDDEN and an early return before do_head or any output, so no path admits an unauthorized caller to the log-viewing operation.

The NULL result of fopen is checked before any fread/fclose use, and the NULL path is handled separately in the else branch at line 20, so no NULL-dereference witness survives the reverse protection scan.

assumptions: buf is declared as char buf[512] with valid indices 0..511 (line 11).
fread returns at most its nmemb argument per standard library semantics.
escapeHTML has the standard semantics of escaping HTML metacharacters at the output consumer.
is_readonly returns true for sessions lacking write privileges, failing closed.
Run.files.log is a configured internal path; no attacker-controlled path construction is shown in this fragment.
limitations: The bodies of escapeHTML, StringBuffer_append, send_error, and do_head are not shown; analysis relies only on the call sites and standard semantics.
TOCTOU/symlink concerns on the configured log path are not demonstrable from the fragment (no attacker-controlled path derivation).
No callers of do_viewlog are shown, so req/resp invariants beyond the shown is_readonly gate are out of scope.

The L33 clamp guards iOctetsRemain, not iMsg (wrong-target drift), and the L64 reset executes only after these writes. Missing fix: guard the write with if(pThis->iMsg < iMaxLine) or reset iMsg at octet-count entry. This is an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787).

assumptions: pMsg's write bound is iMaxLine as established by the fragment's own guards: writes are allowed only for iMsg < iMaxLine (L102) and the buffer is treated as full at iMsg >= iMaxLine (L70).
Octet-counted framing must be enabled (pThis->bSuppOctetFram true) for the eInOctetCnt digit path, including L42, to be reachable.
iMaxLine is the configured maximum message size compared against iMsg in every pMsg guard on this path.
limitations: The exact allocation size of pMsg is not declared inside the fragment; the finding rests on iMaxLine being the pMsg write bound per the fragment's own guard convention, so the first overflow position is iMaxLine (and iMaxLine+1+ for multi-digit counts).
The memcpy negative-size candidate at L118 was demoted: copy mode is only reached after the terminator reset iMsg = 0 (L64), so iMsg > iMaxLine cannot reach the memcpy.
A potential OOB read through doSubmitMsg (pMsg[0..iMsg-1] with iMsg > iMaxLine) depends on that helper's unshown semantics and was not counted.
Reading **buff with buffLen == 0 at L10 depends on the unshown caller and was not counted.

The only in-fragment NULL producer is line 71 when qf_next is NULL, and lines 72-73 break unconditionally before the loop can re-enter, so no path carries a NULL qfp to this sink. verdict.summary: A high-bit byte in an attacker-supplied cgroup v1 name is loaded into a signed char and passed to isalnum(), which indexes the kernel ctype table with the negative value, causing an out-of-bounds read before _ctype[].

evidence.reason: c at line 72 comes from param->string[i] (line 71), an entry-point fsconfig/mount string whose bytes are unconstrained by the shown guards: lines 65 and 67 only cap param->size to [1, 254] and line 70 only bounds i, so a byte 0x80-0xFF is admitted. Because c is declared as plain char (line 71), it sign-extends to a negative value on the kernel ABI and the kernel isalnum() ctype macro reads _ctype[(int)(c)] at a negative index - an out-of-bounds read before the table. The absent one-statement fix is 'unsigned char c = param->string[i];'; the post-read character checks at lines 74-76 cannot prevent the read that already occurred.

assumptions: On all Linux kernel target ABIs, plain 'char' is signed, so bytes 0x80-0xFF become negative in line 71.

The kernel's isalnum() (linux/ctype.h) is a ctype-table lookup _ctype[(int)(x)] and is defined only for unsigned-char-representable arguments (EOF deliberately unsupported), making negative arguments an out-of-bounds read before _ctype[].
param->string/param->size arrive from the fs_parameter machinery; on the Opt_name path size is bounded to [1, 254] by lines 65 and 67.
limitations: The downstream consumers of ctx->name, ctx->release_agent, and fc->source are outside the fragment, so no write/OOB on those pointers is asserted here.
The read param->string[i] itself is bounded by i < param->size with size <= 254 and is not independently flagged.
No NULL producer for ss->legacy_name is visible in the fragment, so the strcmp at line 20 is not a finding.
The impact of the confirmed read is bounded to rodata bytes immediately preceding _ctype[] and is treated as low severity.

verdict.summary: reg_match_visual re-acquires rex.line via reg_getline() after getvvcol() and recomputes rex.input = rex.line + col, so the subsequent win_linetabsize(wp, rex.line, col) and rex.input arithmetic operate on a valid, current line pointer rather than a stale/freed one; no dangerous operation remains unguarded.

This is a benign logic/robustness edge case with no memory-safety or demonstrated exploit impact in this fragment; it is not the pair's distinguishing fix and is demoted rather than reported.

No NULL-deref finding: a NULL result from reg_getline would require an out-of-range rex.lnum, which is excluded by the line 48 bound; the reverse protection scan found no NULL producer on a reaching path.

verdict.summary: nft_flow_rule_create sizes the flow action array to the count of NFT_OFFLOAD_F_ACTION expressions (L10-12, L20) but the second loop (L34-44) invokes expr->ops->offload() on every expression with no check bounding appended actions to that capacity, so an action-producing offload can write past the allocated entry array (heap out-of-bounds write).

assumptions: nft_flow_rule_alloc(num_actions) allocates exactly num_actions flow_action_entry slots (standard semantics of the named allocator).
An offload callback on an action-capable expression appends one action at entries[flow->num_actions++] (flow->num_actions == number of emitted actions).
num_actions is attacker-influenced via the nftables rule expression list passed in as rule.
limitations: The exact set of expression ops whose ->offload emits more actions than are counted by the NFT_OFFLOAD_F_ACTION flag lives outside the fragment; confidence reflects the reliance on the unshown callee callbacks emitting beyond the counted size (the known CVE-2022-25636 failure mode).
Null/status checks present in the fragment (L21, L27, L35, L40) are not findings here; they are correctly handled.

set_limit/global_parameters callee semantics are not analyzed because their bodies are unshown and no failure is demonstrable from the shown arguments.
limitations: No numeric length or index derived from attacker input exists in the fragment, so no OOB/wraparound class applies.
Potential NULL from unshown callers or callees (e.g., first_select(), global_parameters()) is out of scope and demoted.
The redundant res re-check at line 104 is dead code but not a security defect.

verdict.summary: The COPY_BUF macro bounds every write into nbuf with the pre-write check at line 18 (dst == buf + UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND -1), confining writes to indices 0..UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND-2 and keeping the dst[-1] = 0 NUL write in bounds; archive reads are bounded by the src == endp rollover with a !b FATAL_ERROR, and all decode_num results are status-checked, so no dangerous operation admits an unconstrained residual-range value.

It survives the BREAK test, making the COPY_BUF sink resolve PRESENT.

assumptions: nbuf's capacity is UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND (line 6), and buf + UINTMAX_STRSIZE_BOUND - 1 is the address of its last element.
xcalloc has its standard semantics (never returns NULL, aborts on allocation failure), so the sparse_map assignment at lines 53-54 cannot produce a NULL dereference.

A huge decoded sparse_map_size can make calloc fail and abort the process (resource-exhaustion DoS), but no memory-safety, injection, or NULL-deref failure is demonstrable from the shown fragment.
Bodies of decode_num and sparse_add_map are not shown; they are analyzed only through their call sites and standard semantics, and all decode_num return statuses are checked (lines 46/61/69).

The comment at lines 41-46 documents the intentional long-standing failure to return an error when an RLIMIT_CPU request is effectively ignored; this is a designed behavioral quirk, not an unchecked security-relevant status.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in chacha20_poly1305_ctrl is guarded by a protective statement that survives the BREAK test: all arg-driven sizes are bounded before use, and the TLS1_AAD decrypt path guards against unsigned underflow before len -= POLY1305_BLOCK_SIZE.

BREAK test: identity (same arg, no intervening modification), boundary (16 <= 16), degenerate (arg in 1..16, no 0/negative), reach (guard executes on every path before the sink). Resolves PRESENT.

BREAK test: identity (same len value, no intervening change), boundary (admitted len >= 16, subtract 16 stays >= 0), degenerate (len = 15 or 0 rejected), reach (guard on every reaching path). Move of a nullable getter result; resolved PRESENT by `if (zeroRttHeaderCipher)` at line 25, which excludes the null value on every reaching path before the sink consumes it.

Dereference of *clientParams; resolved PRESENT by the `if (!clientParams) throw` statement at lines 48-52, which excludes the null value on every path reaching the dereference, and the guard tests the exact value dereferenced.

Moves of nullable handshake ciphers; resolved PRESENT by the combined guard at lines 67-68 (`if (handshakeReadCipher)` and runtime `CHECK(handshakeReadHeaderCipher)`), which excludes a null header cipher and admits only the non-null handshake cipher on every reaching path.

assumptions: The nullable getter results (getZeroRttReadCipher, getZeroRttReadHeaderCipher, getOneRttWriteCipher, getOneRttReadCipher, getOneRttWriteHeaderCipher, getOneRttReadHeaderCipher, getClientTransportParams, getHandshakeReadCipher, getHandshakeReadHeaderCipher) are treated as potentially null, so each use receives a null guard.
glog-style CHECK (lines 40, 68, 74) is a runtime abort in normal builds, not a debug-only assertion, and is therefore counted as an executing protective statement.
limitations: A NULL conn.readCodec or conn.serverHandshakeLayer supplied by an unshown caller would dereferenced, but no statement in the fragment can produce such a NULL, so this is a demoted candidate, not a finding.
No loops, indexing, arithmetic, or input-length processing exist in the fragment, so no OOB, integer-wraparound, or resource-exhaustion candidate is derivable from the shown code.

verdict.summary: send_control_msg discards iov_from_buf's return value and reports the full requested len to the guest via virtqueue_push even when the guest-provided in_sg buffers are smaller than len, so a short guest buffer makes the device claim a complete write; the required return-status check (ret != len) before the push is absent.

evidence.reason: iov_from_buf at line 15 copies at most the total guest-controlled in_sg capacity and its returned byte count is discarded; when the guest advertises an in_sg smaller than len, virtqueue_push still reports len as the used length to the guest, so an unconstrained entry-point sg capacity reaches this sink (CWE-754 unchecked status); the absent one-statement fix is checking the iov_from_buf return for equality with len before pushing.

assumptions: iov_from_buf is bounded by iov_cnt and per-entry iov_len per its standard semantics, so the host-side write itself does not overflow; the failure is the discarded return and the length subsequently reported to the guest via virtqueue_push.
elem.in_sg and elem.in_num are filled by virtqueue_pop from the guest-side virtqueue, making the buffer capacity guest-controlled entry-point data with no shown minimum.
limitations: No host-side out-of-bounds write is demonstrated because iov_from_buf is bounded; the guest-visible consequence (reading unwritten/stale bytes) is outside this fragment.
The TODO comment at line 14 documents the missing check but is not an executable protective statement and is not credited.

verdict.summary: xQueueGenericCreate multiplies the entry-point values uxQueueLength and uxItemSize in 32-bit UBaseType_t arithmetic with only a configASSERT overflow check, which does not execute in normal builds; a wrapped (too-small) xQueueSizeInBytes then sizes the allocation while prvInitialiseNewQueue still lays out the full uxQueueLength*uxItemSize bytes, enabling a heap overflow.

evidence.snippet: xQueueSizeInBytes = ( size_t ) ( uxQueueLength * uxItemSize ); /*lint !e961 MISRA exception as the casts are only redundant for some ports. */
evidence.reason: The multiplication of the two entry-point UBaseType_t parameters wraps modulo 2^32 for any pair with product >= 2^32 (witness: uxQueueLength=65536, uxItemSize=65536 gives xQueueSizeInBytes=0), and the only check, configASSERT at line 17, is an assertion that does not execute in the analyzed configuration, leaving the wrapped value to size pvPortMalloc at line 28 while prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 46 initializes uxQueueLength*uxItemSize bytes of that storage (CWE-190 integer overflow as the root cause of a heap overflow); the absent one-statement fix is an unconditional runtime check such as uxItemSize == 0 || uxQueueLength <= ( ( size_t ) -1 ) / uxItemSize before the allocation.

evidence.snippet: pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ); /*lint !e9087 !e9079 see comment above. */
evidence.reason: This allocation is sized from the wrapped xQueueSizeInBytes produced at line 14 (e.g., 0 bytes for uxQueueLength=65536, uxItemSize=65536), so the queue storage region is smaller than the uxQueueLength*uxItemSize bytes that prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 46 will write through pucQueueStorage, an undersized allocation with no cap or validation of the size reaching it; absent fix: reject the overflowing pair before malloc.

assumptions: UBaseType_t is a 32-bit unsigned type, so the product wraps at 2^32 before the cast to size_t; the same witness holds for 64-bit size_t because the arithmetic occurs in UBaseType_t.
pvPortMalloc returns a NULL-able pointer and its result is checked at line 30, so no NULL-deref finding.
configASSERT is an assertion macro and is treated as non-executing in normal builds per the do-not-credit rule.
limitations: The downstream heap overflow occurs in the unshown prvInitialiseNewQueue, attributed to its standard queue-initialization semantics (writing uxQueueLength*uxItemSize bytes of item storage); the in-fragment confirmed failure is the unconstrained overflow at line 14.
Callers that keep uxQueueLength*uxItemSize below 2^32 are safe in practice; the finding requires an entry-point caller supplying the large pair.

verdict.summary: Stack buffer overflow in gf_text_get_utf8_line: the UTF8 conversion loop writes to the fixed 1024-byte buffer szLineConv without bounding the output index j against its capacity, so a long input line (admitted because lineSize is unconstrained) overflows szLineConv.

evidence.reason: szLineConv is declared fixed-size 1024 (line 5), but the conversion loop writes to szLineConv[j] with no bound on j or on len. len = strlen(szLine) (line 13) is bounded only by lineSize-1 from gf_fgets (line 9), and lineSize is an unconstrained u32 parameter, so a line of len>=513 is admitted. The first branch (line 18) emits 2 output bytes per input byte and advances i by only 1, so a line of all-0xC0 bytes drives j to ~2*len and writes past szLineConv's 1024-byte capacity. The only guard on the path is 'i<len' (line 14), which constrains i (input index), not j (output index) — wrong-target drift — so it does not protect this sink. No bound check on j or len exists; the absent fix is a j<1024 (or j>=sizeof-1 break) guard. OOB stack write of attacker-controlled file content is CWE-787.

assumptions: szLineConv has a fixed 1024-byte capacity (declared line 5).
gf_fgets reads up to lineSize-1 bytes into szLine, so len <= lineSize-1.
lineSize is not constrained by any shown statement, so lineSize >= 514 is within its residual range.
limitations: The overflow requires the caller to pass lineSize >= 514; a caller with a small lineSize would not trigger it, but no such bound is visible in the fragment.
The second path's szLineConv[i]=0 (line 82) would be OOB only if gf_utf8_wcstombs fills all 1024 slots; its exact return semantics are unshown, so it is not asserted as a separate finding.
strcpy(szLine, szLineConv) (lines 60/83) could overrun szLine only when the converted content exceeds lineSize; this is downstream of the primary szLineConv overflow and not independently confirmed.

A comparison variant using >= or <= instead of == would be unsafe, but is not present in this fragment.

verdict.summary: parse_query copies the query type and class from the packet with pj_memcpy at p = start + name_part_len without verifying that 4 bytes remain before max, so a truncated DNS response whose name ends at the buffer boundary triggers an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: p is derived at line 23 as start + name_part_len, where name_part_len comes from get_name_len (line 10) parsing attacker-controlled packet bytes with residual range [1, max-start]; the only guards on the path (lines 11 and 20) merely ensure the name itself fits in [start, max), so p can equal max or max-1. The absent fix is a remaining-bytes guard such as 'if (p + 4 > max) return ...' placed before line 26; the witness (name wire length == max-start) passes the BLOCK test because no shown statement excludes it.

The same missing bounds check admits the same truncated-packet witness: after line 28 advances p by 2, the pointer is already at or past max, and this second 2-byte memcpy reads further out of bounds (CWE-125). Both reads share the single absent protective statement (verify at least 4 remaining bytes before the type/class reads).

assumptions: The packet buffer is delimited by [pkt, max), with max one past the last valid byte; pointer arithmetic is confined to this region on the name-parse path.
get_name_len/get_name standard semantics: on PJ_SUCCESS, the on-wire name (name_part_len bytes) lies wholly within [start, max), providing no guarantee about trailing type/class bytes.
pj_pool_alloc never returns NULL and the name allocation name_len+4 is sufficient for the name plus NUL, so the allocation write is not a sink.
limitations: The bodies of get_name_len and get_name are not shown; their standard semantics (bounded name parse within [start, max)) are sufficient for the demonstrated overrun and no stronger tail guarantee is attributed to them.
Downstream memory corruption or disclosure is not demonstrated; the confirmed failure is the unguarded out-of-bounds read itself.
Caller-side packet construction is unshown, but a truncated DNS question whose name fills the received datagram is directly derivable from entry-point packet data and the shown pointer arithmetic.

verdict.summary: The entry-point tensor value num_streams (int64) is read at line 15 with no validation and passed unconstrained to the QuantileStreamResource constructor at line 18, so zero or negative stream counts reach a security-relevant resource-construction sink; the required positivity check is absent.

GeneratePoolingSequence (standard semantics of its name/call site) returns a cumulative sequence of output_size+1 non-decreasing entries with last entry equal to the input size, making hs/ws and in_offset reads in-bounds.
pooling_ratio_ is an op attribute (user-config entry-point value) with no constraint shown in the fragment.
limitations: If an unshown caller/constructor enforces pooling_ratio_[0]==1.0 and pooling_ratio_[3]==1.0, the batch and depth mismatches would be suppressed; such an invariant is not derivable from the fragment and is not credited.

verdict.summary: triggeredTopics is a 64-element array (per the numTriggeredTopics == 64 drain check and comment), but the drain check runs only once at function entry; numTriggeredTopics is incremented without any per-write bounds check inside the loop and at the tail, so a single publish can write past index 63.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787): triggeredTopics capacity is 64, established by the drain check `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64)` at line 3 and the comment at line 2. The only protective statement is that entry-time drain check, which tests numTriggeredTopics before any writes in this call and is therefore a check-then-use drift (the value at line 29 has been mutated by prior increments). A single call can increment numTriggeredTopics multiple times: once per segment with an untriggered terminatingWildcardChild plus the final add at line 53. Witness: entry numTriggeredTopics == 62 (reachable, since drain only fires at exactly 64 and no other constraint bounds it below 64), with a 3-segment topic where each segment's terminatingWildcardChild is untriggered: the loop writes indices 62, 63, then 64, overflowing the 64-element array. The absent fix is a drain/bounds check (e.g. `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) drain();`) executed before each `numTriggeredTopics++` write, not just at entry.

Same out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) for the tail add. With entry numTriggeredTopics == 63 and a topic whose loop iteration also adds an untriggered terminatingWildcardChild at line 29, that write bumps numTriggeredTopics to 64 and this final write then indexes 64, past the 64-element capacity implied by line 3. The entry-only drain check does not protect this write (check-then-use drift), and no per-write bounds check is present.

assumptions: triggeredTopics is a 64-element array, inferred from `if (numTriggeredTopics == 64) drain();` at line 3 and the comment 'If we already have 64 triggered topics' at line 2.
drain() clears the triggered set so that after it runs numTriggeredTopics is below 64 (standard semantics of a drain helper).

topic.substr(start, stop - start) at line 10 is in-bounds because stop is recomputed as topic.find('/', start), which returns a position >= start (or npos); npos - start is clamped by substr, and start never exceeds topic.size() along the shown recursion path.
limitations: The array capacity is not declared as a literal array size in the fragment; it is derived from the `== 64` drain check, which is an inference rather than a declaration.

The top-level (outermost) caller's start/stop values are not shown; the analysis relies on the shown recursive call site, whose arguments were verified to keep substr in bounds.

verdict.summary: SSL_new()'s return value is never NULL-checked and the resulting ssl pointer is dereferenced immediately, giving a NULL-pointer dereference on allocation failure; separately, SSL_connect()'s status check (rc < 0) treats the failure return 0 as success, failing open with a non-established TLS session.

evidence.reason: ssl is assigned the result of SSL_new(ctx) at line 87 without any NULL check; OpenSSL's standard semantics return NULL on allocation failure, and the reverse protection scan finds no excluding statement (no if (ssl == NULL), no early return, no reassignment) on any path between line 87 and this first dereference. The ctx==NULL check at line 14 guards a different object (wrong-target drift) and does not protect ssl. The absent one-statement fix is an if (ssl == NULL) cleanup-and-return immediately after line 87; the NULL witness survives the BLOCK test, so this is a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476).

The guard admits rc==0 (its admitted set is rc >= 0), but SSL_connect() in blocking mode (per the comment at line 92) returns 0 for a controlled-shutdown handshake failure and 1 only for success; rc==0 therefore falls through to isssl = true at line 115 and return 0, treating a failed handshake as success. The value rc is not modified between the check and the fall-through, so the guard constrains the right value but only part of its failure set. The absent fix is a full status check such as if (rc != 1) or if (rc <= 0); the rc==0 witness survives the BLOCK test (CWE-754).

assumptions: OpenSSL standard semantics, applied per the fragment's call sites: SSL_new() returns NULL on allocation failure; SSL_connect() returns 1 on success, 0 on controlled-shutdown failure, and <0 on error; SSL_CTX_new() creates a context with default verify mode SSL_VERIFY_NONE.
ctx is guaranteed non-NULL at line 87 by the checks at lines 14, 23, 32/42, 57, 66, and 75.
String::c_str() returns a NUL-terminated buffer, so the hostname argument to SSL_set_tlsext_host_name at line 94 has no out-of-bounds read.
limitations: SSL_CTX_set_verify is never called, so with OpenSSL's SSL_VERIFY_NONE default the fragment accepts any server certificate (MITM gap, certificate-validation class); this independent cryptographic-validation gap is documented here but not counted in the CWE list.
The CWE-476 witness requires SSL_new to fail (allocation failure), which is not directly attacker-controlled; it remains an unchecked in-fragment allocation failure path per the NULL-deref rules.
An embedded NUL in hostname would only truncate the SNI value; no memory-safety impact, so no finding.
No call sites of startSslClient are shown, so no caller-side preconditions (e.g., guaranteed non-empty certificate_path) can be assumed in either direction.

verdict.summary: parse() mmaps the attacker-supplied file with capacity st.st_size (L23) and then consumes ELF header/table fields (e_shoff, e_shnum, e_shstrndx, sh_offset, sh_size) with no bounds validation, allowing out-of-bounds reads; additionally, dynamic/dynstr are used uninitialized as shdr indices when the .dynamic/.dynstr sections are absent, and name strings are scanned without a bound.

evidence.reason: Out-of-bounds read: elf_map's only capacity is st.st_size (L23), and e_shoff (base of shdr, L176) plus e_shstrndx are attacker-controlled ELF fields with no check between L33 and L178 (only the fd/fstat/mmap status guards at L13/18/24); witness: e_shoff=0, e_shstrndx=0xFFFF over a small file reads shdr[0xFFFF] at offset ~2.6MB past the mapping; absent fix: a pre-use validation such as e_shoff + e_shnum*sizeof(Elf32_Shdr) <= st.st_size && e_shstrndx < e_shnum; CWE-125.

Uninitialized read: dynamic (L331) is assigned only inside if (!strcmp(name, ".dynamic")) at L338-339, so when the attacker omits that section or sets e_shnum==0 (L333 loop runs zero times) the value is indeterminate and then used as an index into shdr with no intervening test; absent fix: int dynamic = -1; plus a found-check before use; CWE-457.

Out-of-bounds read: name (L183) is elf_map + shstrtab.sh_offset + shdr[i].sh_name with all offsets attacker-controlled and unvalidated against st.st_size (L23); the L254 guard is evaluated at the sink itself and cannot bound the strlen scan that precedes it, which runs past the mapping when no NUL exists inside the buffer (guard-identity drift classes 1/4); absent fix: validate shstrtab.sh_offset/sh_name and cap the string read length; CWE-125.

assumptions: The mapped object's capacity is st.st_size as shown at L23; no other capacity or invariant is derivable from the fragment.

Elf32/Elf64 header fields retain their standard ELF declared widths (e_shnum/e_shstrndx are 16-bit unsigned, offsets/sizes 32/64-bit unsigned), and mmap/strlen/strcmp/snprintf have their standard semantics.
The 64-bit branch (L824, L991-992, L1008-1009) duplicates the identical unguarded patterns with the same residual ranges.
limitations: The strcpy at L255 writes only when strlen(name)>15 with the NUL inside the map, so the write stays within the map; it is not credited as a separate OOB write.
Reading ehdr fields at L36 without a minimum file-size check (e.g., st.st_size >= sizeof(Elf32_Ehdr)) is the same OOB-read class as the cited sinks and is subsumed by them.

Unshown PRINT_*/INFO/flag2str* helpers are assumed only to display the attacker-derived values already analyzed; any additional interpretive use is outside the fragment.

verdict.summary: xQueueGenericCreate guards its queue-size arithmetic only with configASSERT (an assertion macro, not executable protection in normal builds), so uxQueueLength*uxItemSize and sizeof(Queue_t)+xQueueSizeInBytes can wrap. A supplied pair such as uxQueueLength=65537, uxItemSize=65535 (32-bit UBaseType_t/size_t) yields xQueueSizeInBytes=0xFFFFFFFF and an allocation of sizeof(Queue_t)-1 bytes while pucQueueStorage is offset sizeof(Queue_t), producing an undersized heap allocation and out-of-bounds queue-storage writes; the absent fix is a runtime overflow/divisibility check that fails creation instead of an assert.

evidence.snippet: pxNewQueue = ( Queue_t * ) pvPortMalloc( sizeof( Queue_t ) + xQueueSizeInBytes ); /*lint !e9087 !e9079 see comment above. */
evidence.reason: uxQueueLength/uxItemSize retain their full UBaseType_t domain because configASSERT (lines 17 and 20) is an assertion macro whose expansion is unshown and does not execute in normal builds, so it is not credited. With 32-bit types, uxQueueLength=65537 and uxItemSize=65535 reach line 14 with a product of 0xFFFFFFFF (no wrap, so the line-17 check would even pass), then the line-31 addition sizeof(Queue_t)+0xFFFFFFFF wraps to sizeof(Queue_t)-1, making pvPortMalloc allocate an undersized block; the missing runtime check (e.g., if ((sizeof(Queue_t)+xQueueSizeInBytes) < xQueueSizeInBytes) return NULL) is absent, enabling the undersized heap allocation whose storage is later written out of bounds (CWE-190 root cause; CWE-787 heap overwrite).

evidence.reason: The multiplication uxQueueLength*uxItemSize is performed in UBaseType_t arithmetic with no executable bound: uxQueueLength=65536, uxItemSize=65537 wraps the product to 0x10000 while the queue storage actually requires 0x100000000 bytes. The only guard is configASSERT at line 17, which is an assertion macro (unshown expansion; no-op/abort semantics) and per the do-not-credit rule never constrains the value reaching this arithmetic. The absent fix is a runtime divisibility/size-cap check that fails queue creation instead of an assert, so the wrapped size feeds the line-31 allocation (CWE-190).

evidence.snippet: pucQueueStorage += sizeof( Queue_t ); /*lint !e9016 Pointer arithmetic allowed on char types, especially when it assists conveying intent. */
evidence.reason: For the addition-wrap witness (uxQueueLength=65537, uxItemSize=65535, 32-bit size_t), pxNewQueue is a sizeof(Queue_t)-1 byte block (line 31) and pucQueueStorage is advanced by sizeof(Queue_t) bytes, landing exactly one byte past the allocated object; this out-of-bounds storage pointer is passed to prvInitialiseNewQueue at line 48, which initializes storage for uxQueueLength items of uxItemSize bytes and writes beyond the block (CWE-787 heap overwrite). There is no shown runtime statement between line 33's NULL check (which constrains only non-NULL) and this offset that bounds the pointer to the allocation.

assumptions: UBaseType_t and size_t are 32-bit on the analyzed ports; the fragment itself asserts overflow is possible in the multiplication and the addition (lines 16-20), which is the in-fragment evidence that these operations can wrap at the shown boundaries.
configASSERT's expansion is not shown and, per the do-not-credit rule, assertion macros never count as protective statements in the analyzed (normal/release) configuration.
prvInitialiseNewQueue has standard queue-initialization semantics: it sets up and uses a storage region sized uxQueueLength * uxItemSize starting at pucQueueStorage.
limitations: uxQueueLength/uxItemSize have no shown call site, so provenance is analyzed as internal-helper parameters (class c) using only in-fragment arithmetic consequences; the ability of a caller to supply the witness values is api-level, not shown.

The exact widths of UBaseType_t/size_t are port-dependent and not literally declared in the fragment; on a 64-bit size_t configuration the addition-wrap witness does not fire, though the multiplication-wrap witness still produces an undersized allocation if UBaseType_t is 32-bit.

The actual out-of-bounds storage write occurs inside the unshown prvInitialiseNewQueue/queue-send path; the in-fragment confirmed failure is the integer wraparound and the resulting out-of-bounds storage pointer.
In configurations where configASSERT aborts, the overflow would stop execution, but that is still assert behavior (crash, not input handling) and is not credited as a protective statement.

assumptions: mmap at line 23 establishes the only demonstrated capacity, st.st_size bytes at elf_map, with MAP_FAILED handled at line 24.

limitations: The 8-byte scratch write at line 139 (memcpy(ctx->hdr_store + ctx->bytes_in_header, start, 8 - ctx->bytes_in_header)) is a candidate, but hdr_store's capacity on that exact cross-call path is not derivable from the shown statements, so no confirmed overflow witness was established.

The 'assert(size >= 3); size -= 3;' underflow candidates at lines 197 and 437 depend on gf_m4v_parse_frame returning GF_EOS with size < 3, which is not demonstrated by the fragment, so they are demoted.
If assertions are enabled in the build, line 94 aborts on the witness instead of overflowing (a DoS), but asserts are not credited as protective statements for release builds.

verdict.summary: EvalGatherNd validates only that indices are non-negative; index components are not bounded against the params tensor dimensions before being passed to GatherNd, so an index value equal to or larger than a params dimension reaches the callee's standard gather indexing and performs an out-of-bounds read of params.

evidence.reason: The indices tensor is an entry-point input whose values retain the residual range [0, MAX(IndicesT)] after the only shown guard, the non-negativity check at line 7; no statement bounds them against the capacities of params, so a component v equal to a params dimension (e.g., dim 3, v = 3) passes `indices_values[i] < 0` (false), keeps indices_has_only_positive_elements true through TF_LITE_ENSURE (line 12), and reaches this GatherNd dispatch, whose standard gather semantics index params[v] out of bounds — an OOB read (CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is a per-axis upper-bound check (indices component < corresponding params dimension) placed after the sign check and before the dispatch.

assumptions: TFLite tensor contract: the data buffer reachable via GetTensorData is at least tensor->bytes long, so the validation loop read at line 7 stays in bounds (bounded by `i < num_indices` with num_indices = bytes / sizeof(IndicesT)).
params is a finite tensor whose dimensions exist (their numeric values are not shown in this fragment).
limitations: The params tensor's dimension capacities are not declared in the fragment; the failing boundary is inferred from the standard semantics of the gather operation rather than a quoted capacity line, which caps confidence at the stated band.

The body of GatherNd/GatherNdString is not shown; per the rules it is analyzed via the shown arguments and the standard indexing semantics of a gather op, and no internal bounds-checking behavior is attributed to it.
A non-negative but too-large index value is a confirmed reachable witness; the loop itself (read of indices_values[i]) is safe and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: In the decryption branch, ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd subtracts the AES-GCM tag size from an unvalidated src_len without checking src_len >= authsize, wrapping the unsigned length to ~4GB and feeding that length to scatterwalk_ffwd and ccp_init_data, causing out-of-bounds DMA access.

evidence.reason: Decryption computes `ilen = aes->src_len - authsize;` (line 61) with no check that `aes->src_len >= authsize`; for entry-point `src_len = 0` and the switch-admitted `authsize = 16` (lines 34-45), the unsigned subtraction wraps to 0xFFFFFFF0, and this wrapped length reaches this scatterlist walk, advancing past the input buffer (whose capacity is only AAD + `src_len` bytes), so the resulting `p_tag` is out-of-bounds or NULL and is later consumed at line 249; the only guard on the path (authsize switch, lines 34-45) constrains a different value (Guard-Identity drift class 3: wrong target), and the absent one-statement fix is `if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;` before line 61, making this an out-of-bounds access (CWE-787).

evidence.snippet:
ret = ccp_init_data(&src, cmd_q, p_inp, ilen,
				    AES_BLOCK_SIZE,
				    in_place ? DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL
					     : DMA_TO_DEVICE);
evidence.reason: The same wrapped `ilen` (0xFFFFFFF0 from `src_len = 0`, `authsize = 16`) passes the `ilen > 0` test at line 144 and is used here as the DMA length; `ccp_init_data` maps and processes `ilen` bytes against a source buffer that only holds `aes->src_len` plus AAD bytes, producing an out-of-bounds DMA read/write, so the missing `src_len >= authsize` lower-bound check makes this sink unsafe (CWE-787).

assumptions: AES_BLOCK_SIZE is 16; `final_wa` is allocated with AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes at line 211, which exactly fits the two `__be64` writes at lines 216-217.
The input scatterlist capacity is the AAD (aes->aad_len) plus ciphertext (aes->src_len) bytes, so a decryption ilen larger than src_len - authsize exceeds the mapped buffer.
limitations: `aes->iv_len` (line 103) is not validated in the fragment; `dm_offset = CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES - aes->iv_len` could underflow if iv_len exceeded the workarea size, but no in-fragment producer drives iv_len, so this candidate is demoted and not used for the verdict.
`aes->aad_len` vs. the source SG capacity at lines 54-55 could also overrun `scatterwalk_ffwd`, but the comment at lines 47-52 declares SG validity as a caller expectation (demoted candidate).
The encrypt-path `p_tag` write at line 242 relies on the caller providing a destination of src_len + authsize bytes; that contract is not shown and is out of scope.

verdict.summary: thousand_sep.size()/dec_point.size() are unconstrained entry-point String lengths; their 64-bit size_t products are narrowed into the 32-bit int reslen after an overflow check that only tests unsigned-64-bit wraparound, so a large separator string truncates the allocated size and the copy loop performs a multi-gigabyte heap write beyond resbuf.

evidence.reason: thousand_sep.size() (Phase 1 provenance (a): unbounded entry-point String parameter, residual range [0, SIZE_MAX]) is factored into the int reslen at line 67 through a size_t product that is narrowed to int, and the guard at line 62 only detects unsigned-64-bit wraparound, admitting every product below 2^64. With d=DBL_MAX (integral=309, sep_count=102) and thousand_sep of length 42,107,523, the product 102*42,107,523 = 2^32-50 passes the line 62 check, line 67 truncates integral to 259, line 88 allocates a 259-byte resbuf, yet this memcpy plus the loop writes 309 bytes and 102*42,107,523 separator bytes, overflowing the heap buffer by ~4.29 GB; no shown statement on the path bounds the size, and the absent fix is a truncation-safe size check (CWE-787 heap buffer overflow caused by CWE-197 numeric truncation).

dec_point.size() is likewise an unconstrained entry-point length added into the int reslen at line 80 after the line 76 check that tests only unsigned wraparound, so a dec_point of length >= 2^32 truncates reslen while this memcpy writes dec_point.size() bytes, causing an oversized heap write past resbuf (CWE-787, with CWE-197 truncation as the root cause).

assumptions: 64-bit size_t and 32-bit int (standard on the analyzed x86_64/arm64 targets).
ReserveString(n) provides n payload bytes plus a NUL slot, consistent with the comment at lines 20-21 and snprintf sizes 64 / tmplen+1.
dec_point and thousand_sep originate from userland string arguments to number_format, so their lengths are attacker-controlled with no shown cap.
snprintf returns the would-be length per the quoted man-page semantics.
limitations: For separator strings below ~41.7 MB the byte accounting (integral digits + (integral-1)/3 separators + dec fractional digits + dec_point + sign) is exact and no OOB was found on ordinary inputs.
The dec_point-based variant of the truncation requires a >= 4 GB string and is secondary; the thousand_sep variant is the primary witness.

The negative-tmplen guards (lines 28, 38), the digit-first check (29/39), the resize for tmplen>=64, and the no-trailing-separator guard s>=tmpbuf (line 125) are all present and effective for their own failure sets; they do not constrain String sizes.
Huge dec values are likely stopped by snprintf returning < 0 (glibc EOVERFLOW) before the size arithmetic, so that path is not asserted.
On 32-bit platforms size_t is 32-bit and the line 62 unsigned comparison may itself wrap and trigger raise_error, changing the failure mode; the analysis targets 64-bit builds.

verdict.summary: An attacker-controlled fcTL chunk shorter than its fixed 26-byte format is read at offsets 12-33 without any size check, causing an out-of-bounds heap read in the APNG decoder.

evidence.reason: The fcTL chunk fields at chunk.p+12..chunk.p+33 are read with no preceding check that the chunk actually contains them; chunk.p and chunk.size both derive from the attacker-controlled chunk length field read by read_chunk (line 64), whose size is only constrained to be at least 12 (header + empty payload + CRC) per the chunk-size accounting visible at line 181. A length-0 fcTL yields chunk.size == 12, is admitted by `if (!id) break;` (line 65) and the fcTL branch (lines 73-74), and reaches `png_get_uint_32(chunk.p + 12)` reading 4 bytes beyond the 12-byte allocation; the only nearby guard (lines 153-158) validates w0/h0/x0/y0 after the reads and cannot protect them. The absent one-statement fix is a minimum chunk-size check (payload >= 26 bytes / chunk.size >= 34) before line 142, so this is an out-of-bounds heap read (CWE-125).

assumptions: read_chunk allocates chunk.p to hold exactly chunk.size bytes and imposes no minimum payload size; its standard PNG semantics are used since the body is not shown.
CHUNK.size includes the 4-byte length header, 4-byte type, payload, and 4-byte CRC, as evidenced by the fdAT arithmetic `chunk.size - 16` at line 181.
A chunk length field of zero yields a valid small chunk (chunk.size back to 12) that read_chunk accepts, so the loop reaches the fcTL fixed-format reads.
limitations: Multiplication overflow in `rowbytes = w * 4` / `imagesize = h * rowbytes` (lines 53-54) and any consequent undersized frameRaw allocation cannot be confirmed because the numeric value of cMaxPNGSize is not shown.
The `x0 + w0 > w` sum (line 154) could wrap only if cMaxPNGSize >= 2^31, which is not derivable from the fragment, so that path is not asserted.
JXL_ASSERT(chunk.p != nullptr) (line 66) is debug-only and was not credited as a protective statement; NULL is not the failure mode here regardless.
Downstream decode-size behavior inside the unshown processing_start/processing_data bodies was not relied on for the verdict.

verdict.summary: gf_hinter_finalize passes the stack struct slc to gf_isom_set_extraction_slc without having initialized it whenever the OD branch does not execute (no OD track, or OD sample count != 1 / sample not embeddable), reading uninitialized GF_SLConfig fields on the ISMA scene-only path.

assumptions: gf_base64_encode honors its outSize argument (2000), so size64 <= 2000 and all buf64/sdpLine sprintf/strcpy sinks stay in bounds (cap 5000/5100, exact-size malloc).

char buf64[5000] and sdpLine[5100] are the declared sink capacities.
limitations: esd possibly NULL from gf_isom_get_esd (lines 66/105, derefs at 84/98/134) has no NULL producer shown inside the fragment, so it is demoted to a limitation, not a finding.
A potential buf64[size64] OOB would require attributing nonstandard behavior (ignoring outSize) to gf_base64_encode, which is not credited per callee-semantics rules.
Copyright/version strings (lines 20/22) are internal, not attacker-controlled.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation demonstrable in the fragment is constrained: the only array write (m_ppUpsampler[i]) is bounded by the loop guard `i < m_ucCount` against the m_ucCount-element allocation at line 15, and the m_pLargestScale dereference is NULL-guarded at line 32. NULL-return behavior of AllocMem/ComponentOf/TablesOf is not shown inside the fragment, so those candidates are limitations rather than confirmed findings.

evidence.reason: The write to m_ppUpsampler at index i is fully protected by the line 18 loop condition `i < m_ucCount`: admitted i in [0, m_ucCount-1] never reaches the m_ucCount-element capacity allocated at line 15. The guard survives the BREAK test (identity: same m_ucCount with no intervening modification; boundary: max index m_ucCount-1 < capacity m_ucCount; degenerate: counts 0 and 255; reach: the condition executes before every store), so no OOB write is derivable.

The dereference of m_pLargestScale is preceded on every reaching path by the verbatim NULL guard at line 32 (`if (m_pLargestScale)`), which excludes NULL before the call; no unguarded dereference of this value exists in the fragment.

assumptions: m_ucCount is a member whose type is not shown; its name (m_uc prefix) and its comparison with the UBYTE variable i at line 18 imply an unsigned 8-bit count (max 255), which also keeps the size expressions at lines 10-11 and 15-16 free of integer overflow.

Capacities are exactly what the same branch allocates: m_ppDecodingMCU has m_ucCount*8 elements (line 10) and m_ppUpsampler has m_ucCount elements (line 15); the memset byte counts at lines 11 and 16 match their allocations.
limitations: NULL-return semantics of m_pEnviron->AllocMem are not shown in the fragment; a NULL result would NULL-deref at memsets lines 11/16, but the NULL-producing behavior is not demonstrated inside the fragment, so it is a limitation, not a finding.
