If m_ucCount exceeded 255, the UBYTE loop variable i would wrap at line 18 causing non-termination, but the fragment shows no type or producer establishing such a value, so this is unconfirmable.
Allocation failure (OOM) is an environmental condition rather than a value the fragment can be shown to derive from input, so it is not used as a witness.

verdict.summary: In the AES-GCM decryption branch, aes->src_len is subtracted from authsize without a src_len >= authsize check; the unsigned underflow yields a huge ilen passed to scatterwalk_ffwd()/ccp_init_data(), walking the scatterlist past its end (kernel OOB read/write). A second unvalidated subtraction, CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES - aes->iv_len, wraps when iv_len exceeds the ctx workarea and ccp_set_dm_area() writes out of bounds.

evidence.reason: aes->src_len is unsigned with no shown minimum (only authsize is validated at 33-44), so for any src_len in [0, authsize-1] the 32-bit subtraction wraps, e.g. src_len=0, authsize=16 gives ilen=0xFFFFFFF0; no guard constrains src_len (the 144 if (ilen > 0) admits the wrapped value), and the wrapped ilen is consumed at line 62 by scatterwalk_ffwd(sg_tag, p_inp, ilen) and at lines 148/158 by ccp_init_data, which walk the source SG list past its end — an out-of-bounds kernel access. Absent fix: 'if (aes->src_len < authsize) return -EINVAL;' before line 61; the primary mechanism is the CWE-191 integer underflow corrupting a size used for the scatterlist/DMA access (CWE-787 secondary).

aes->iv_len is never validated (only aes->iv non-NULL at line 21); the ctx workarea capacity is CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES (lines 97-99). Line 103 computes dm_offset = capacity - aes->iv_len, which wraps to a near-UINT_MAX offset for any iv_len larger than the capacity, and this copy then writes iv_len bytes at that offset into the bounded ctx buffer — an out-of-bounds write. Absent fix: 'if (aes->iv_len > CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES) return -EINVAL;'; the same failure repeats at line 197, with CWE-191 underflow feeding a CWE-787 OOB DMA copy.

assumptions: cmd->u.aes fields (src_len, iv_len, aad_len, authsize, key_len) are set by the unshown crypto-request caller; per fragment-only rules their unconstrained domains are analyzed for consequences demonstrable inside the fragment, and in the real ccp-crypto path they derive from request-supplied lengths.
scatterwalk_ffwd() is analyzed by its standard semantics: it walks the source SG list by 'len' bytes via sg_next and builds the offset entry; an oversized len advances past the list terminator.
ccp_init_dm_workarea(&ctx, ..., CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES, ...) at lines 97-99 documents the ctx buffer capacity used in the line 103 subtraction.
limitations: The scatterlist walk failure at line 62 (and line 148/158) is stated as an OOB read/walk via standard scatterwalk semantics; the exact manifestation (NULL sg_next vs OOB entry read) depends on the unshown scatterwalk_ffwd implementation, not on the underflow itself.

The iv_len-underflow sink at line 104 assumes any iv_len greater than CCP_AES_CTX_SB_COUNT * CCP_SB_BYTES is representable; the constants' numeric values are not shown, but the capacity expression is a small positive constant product, so such values exist in the unsigned domain.
The aad_len-driven scatterwalk_ffwd at lines 54-55 has no shown bound either; it is subsumed by the same missing-length-validation class and not counted as a separate finding.
The wrapped ilen also corrupts final[1] = cpu_to_be64(ilen * 8) at line 217 via a 32-bit multiply — an integrity-side effect of the same underflow, not counted separately.

verdict.summary: mpgviddmx_process applies the cross-packet ctx->resume_from offset to a new packet's s32 remain guarded only by debug asserts (lines 94/90), wrapping remain negative on a smaller packet and driving an oversized memcpy (line 129); independently, the start-code store copy (line 139) reads 8 - bytes_in_header bytes from a packet window of only 5 bytes when bytes_in_header is 1 or 2.

evidence.reason: ctx->resume_from is a u32 produced at line 393 as an offset into a previous packet's buffer and persists across calls; on a subsequent call with hdr_store_size==0 the only bound on it is the debug-only assert at line 94, so line 96 (s32 remain -= u32 resume_from) wraps (e.g. 10 - 1000 -> -990), which passes the `if (remain<5)` gate at line 128 and is sign-extended to a huge size_t at this memcpy, writing beyond ctx->hdr_store's shown allocation (hdr_store_alloc, lines 68-70) and reading past start — CWE-787 (signed/unsigned subtraction root, CWE-195). The absent fix is a runtime check such as `if (!ctx->hdr_store_size && ((s32) ctx->resume_from > remain)) { ctx->resume_from = 0; return GF_OK; }` before line 95.

ctx->bytes_in_header is set from a previous packet's tail at line 130 (values 1..4) and at line 199 (=3); when it is 1 or 2 and the new packet's remain is 5 (or 6), this copy reads 8 - bytes_in_header (up to 7) bytes from start, exceeding the packet window [data, data+pck_size) declared at line 31 by 1-2 bytes — CWE-125 out-of-bounds read. The loop-top gate `if (remain<5)` at line 128 only constrains remain >= 5 and does not constrain the copy length against remain (wrong-target drift); the absent fix is capping the copy at remain, e.g. `GF_MIN(8 - ctx->bytes_in_header, remain)`.

assumptions: pck_size (line 31) is the exact number of valid bytes of the packet buffer returned by gf_filter_pck_get_data; bytes beyond it are out of bounds.
ctx->hdr_store capacity comes only from the shown gf_realloc sites (lines 70, 299, 343) into ctx->hdr_store_alloc.
assert() statements do not execute in release (NDEBUG) builds and are not counted as protective statements.
ctx->resume_from and ctx->bytes_in_header persist across filter calls and are only modified at the shown lines (393/98 and 130/199/163/170).
limitations: The resume_from witness requires ctx->is_playing == GF_FALSE on the producing call (line 392), an external filter state that the fragment explicitly handles; if that state is never entered the path is dead.

The write side of lines 129/139 further depends on hdr_store's initial allocation, which is not shown; the confirmed violations are the huge-size copy at line 129 and the read past the packet window at line 139.
gf_realloc at lines 70/299/343 is unchecked; on OOM a NULL ctx->hdr_store would be dereferenced at lines 72/301/345 (CWE-476) — demoted as an environmental OOM-only path.

`assert(size >= 3)` (lines 197/430) and `assert(remain >= size)` (line 527) guard size underflows only in debug builds; exploiting them requires unshown gf_m4v_parse_frame size semantics, so they are demoted to limitations.

verdict.summary: The scalar validation for input_requested_max checks input_requested_min instead, so an empty input_requested_max tensor (NumElements()==0) passes validation and input_requested_max.flat<float>()(0) performs an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.reason: input_requested_max is an entry-point tensor whose element count is never constrained: the only intended guard, OP_REQUIRES at line 31, tests input_requested_min.NumElements()==1 (wrong-target drift, guard-identity class 3), so any input_requested_max shape including NumElements()==0 is admitted; a 0-element tensor reaches input_requested_max.flat<float>()(0) at line 34, dereferencing element 0 of empty/null storage (out-of-bounds read, CWE-125). The absent one-statement fix is OP_REQUIRES(ctx, input_requested_max.NumElements() == 1, ...) applied to the correct tensor; the witness (empty input_requested_max) survives the BLOCK test because every guard on the path tests input_requested_min only.

assumptions: ctx->input(...) tensors are user/attacker-suppliable (entry-point provenance); a tensor with NumElements()==0 is supplyable for any input whose shape the fragment fails to validate.
Tensor::flat<float>()(0) on a 0-element tensor dereferences invalid (null or zero-size) storage.
limitations: Float division by requested_min_max (lines 45-47, 56) can yield inf/NaN for DT_QUINT8 when both requested outputs are 0.0f (CWE-369 candidate); demoted because IEEE-754 float division is defined behavior, downstream oneDNN behavior is unshown, and mkldnn::error is caught at line 112.

int i vs size_t depth comparison at line 53 could overflow past INT_MAX, but requires an input_min_vec with more than 2^31 elements (~8 GiB); no shown statement establishes such a tensor is feasible, so it is not counted.
Membership identity (which member of the pair this fragment is) was not used in the verdict.

verdict.summary: The fragment is a type-dispatch wrapper: it selects a GatherNd kernel by params->type and propagates the kernel's status, with an error default for unsupported types. No shown statement performs arithmetic, indexing, copying, or formatting on an unconstrained value; the only data-consuming operations are calls to unshown kernel bodies whose failure sets cannot be derived from the shown code, and the ReportError call uses a literal format string.

evidence.reason: Closest candidate: entry-point tensors (params, indices, output) are forwarded to the unshown GatherNd kernel. No shown statement derives an index, size, capacity, or pointer in this fragment, so no failing value is demonstrated to reach a dangerous operation here; any bounds/type-validation defect inside the unshown callee (e.g., unvalidated indices values) is not attributable from the call site and is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.

ReportError consumes a compile-time literal format string, so the only substituted value, TfLiteTypeGetName(params->type), is format data rather than a format string; no format-string injection (CWE-134) is possible. The default branch is reached exactly for params->type values not matched by the switch and returns kTfLiteError without further consumption of tensor data.

assumptions: params, indices, output, and context are non-NULL per the TFLite kernel entry contract; no shown statement can make them NULL.
params->type is read as a TfLiteType enum value; any value not among the seven listed cases reaches the default and is rejected with kTfLiteError.
limitations: The bodies of GatherNd<T, IndicesT> and GatherNdString<IndicesT> are not shown; any internal bounds-checking defect or its absence cannot be established from standard semantics and the shown pointer-only call site, so it is out of scope.
The IndicesT template parameter is chosen by an unshown caller; a mismatch between indices->type and IndicesT would be a caller-side concern not visible in this fragment.
NULL params or context supplied by an out-of-contract caller would be dereferenced at lines 3 and 19, but the fragment contains no NULL producer, so no witness survives the reverse protection scan.

verdict.summary: In gen_assignment's NODE_CALL/NODE_SCALL handling, the argument count n returned by gen_values is used as the OP_SEND/OP_SSEND operand without any upper bound. For a call with more than 15 positional arguments, n stays above 15 while the packing branch (single OP_ARYPUSH) does not account for the extra values, so the emitted argument count does not match the stack arrangement, causing an out-of-bounds read/write in the VM.

evidence.snippet: genop_3(s, noself ? OP_SSEND : OP_SEND, cursp(), new_sym(s, attrsym(s, mid)), n);
evidence.reason: n originates from gen_values at line 106 and is never bounded above; the only guards (n<0, n==13||14, n<14, n<15 at lines 107/113/120/140) are all false for n>15 and their else branches at lines 147-150 perform a single pop()/OP_ARYPUSH(cursp(),1) without reducing n. A call with more than 15 positional arguments therefore reaches this OP_SEND/OP_SSEND emission with an operand count that exceeds the properly packed argument slots, yielding a heap out-of-bounds access (CWE-787) in the VM. The absent fix is an upper-bound/equality check on n (or complete packing of every extra argument) before this emission.

assumptions: gen_values returns the positional-argument count (or -1 for splat) and its return is not shown to be capped at the limit 13/14 passed at line 106.
n flows from line 106 unchanged (apart from the small-n special cases) to the OP_SEND operand at line 156.
limitations: The exact VM-level OOB depends on mruby's OP_ARRAY/OP_SEND stack semantics outside the shown fragment.

If an unshown implementation of gen_values provably caps its return at 14 (or always returns -1 for large lists), the large-n witness would not be producible; this is the fragile assumption behind the moderate confidence.

verdict.summary: The inner loop bounds i by relative_offset_set.size() (small_stride*big_stride elements) but indexes flat_segment_id, which holds only small_stride elements, causing a heap out-of-bounds read; the read segment id then drives output_index into output_flat without a bounds check, enabling an out-of-bounds heap write (and flat_input is also read out of bounds via offset).

evidence.reason: The inner loop admits i in [0, relative_offset_set.size()) = [0, small_stride*big_stride-1], but flat_segment_id has capacity flat_segment_id.size() == small_stride (segment_id.NumElements() via GetStrides semantics), so any i >= small_stride, e.g. i == 2 with input shape [2,2] and segment_id shape [2], performs a heap out-of-bounds read at this statement; the only prior guard (lines 40-47) validates id values only for indices below flat_segment_id.size() and never constrains this inner-loop index, and no shown check ties i to flat_segment_id.size(), so the missing one-statement fix is a bound on i before flat_segment_id(i) — CWE-125.

output_index = start_offset + flat_segment_id(i) * big_stride is used to index output_flat with no bounds check, and its segment-id term comes from the unvalidated out-of-bounds read at line 57, so an admitted index can exceed output_flat's capacity (num_segments*big_stride) and write out of bounds; additionally offset = start_offset + relative_offset_set[i] deterministically reaches flat_input.size() (e.g., offset 4 for input [2,2] at start_offset 1, i 3), so flat_input is read out of bounds on the same statement — the absent fixes are bounds checks on output_index and offset before use — CWE-787.

assumptions: GetStrides returns (big_stride, small_stride) with small_stride equal to the product of the segment dims (segment_id.NumElements()) and big_stride equal to the product of the remaining input dims, per the shown call site and dim-equality checks at lines 20-26.
GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets(small_stride, big_stride) returns one flattened offset per [small_stride x big_stride] element, i.e., size small_stride*big_stride, per its name and call-site arguments.
allocate_output at lines 32-33 succeeded, so output_shape (num_segments x big_stride) is a valid tensor shape.
limitations: If the callee GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets were given different semantics (a different element count), the exact indices would shift, but the fragment still contains no shown statement bounding the inner-loop index against flat_segment_id.size(), so the OOB read class would remain.

The OOB write through output_flat depends on the indeterminate value read out of bounds at line 57; the deterministic part of the fragment is the flat_segment_id and flat_input out-of-bounds reads, while the write is a direct unvalidated consequence of the same missing bound.

verdict.summary: Unbounded sprintf calls write into the fixed 32-byte stack buffer id in FurnaceGUI::patternRow. The int operands i, j, k are admitted to range up to INT_MAX by comparisons against song-file fields (patLen, chans, effectRows) that have no in-fragment upper bound, so a formatted expansion such as "..##PE%d_%d_%d" reaches 32+ chars plus NUL and overflows id[32].

evidence.reason: Stack-buffer overflow (CWE-121): the sink is an unbounded sprintf into id whose 32-byte capacity is declared at line 2. k is admitted by `k<e->song.pat[j].effectRows` (line 186), i by `i<e->song.patLen` (line 15), j by `j<chans` (line 63); patLen, chans, and effectRows are entry-point song fields with no shown cap, so each operand's residual range includes 10^7 (8 digits). The expansion "..##PE"+k+"_"+i+"_"+j is then 32 characters plus NUL = 33 bytes into id[32]. The guards are wrong-target drift: they bound pattern dimensions, not the string length against the buffer capacity, and admit the failing values. Absent fix: snprintf(id, sizeof(id), ...) or a capacity ≥ 39 bytes; witness i=j=k=10^7 (with patLen=chans=effectRows ≥ 10^7+1, chanShow[j]=true, chanCollapse[j]=false, any effect data) reaches the sink with no shown statement blocking it.

Same unbounded-sprintf mechanism into the 32-byte id buffer: with i=j=k=10^7 admitted by the unbounded song fields (lines 15, 63, 186), the format emits "00##PE" plus 8+1+8+1+8 digits = 30 chars for a non-negative data byte plus NUL = 31 (fits), but with operands of 9-10 digits (patLen/chans/effectRows up to INT_MAX, not excluded by any shown check) the expansion reaches 33-39 bytes past id[31]. Absent fix: bounded write (snprintf with sizeof(id)) or a capacity sized to the worst-case printf output; the guards on i/j/k again fail the Guard-Identity audit (wrong-target: pattern-size bounds, not buffer-capacity bounds).

assumptions: id at line 2 is a 32-byte stack array (`static char id[32]`).
printf-family standard semantics: %d of a non-negative int emits its decimal digits (up to 10 for int), %.2X emits 2 hex digits for a non-negative value, and the result is NUL-terminated.

e->song.patLen, e->song.chans (via chans), and e->song.pat[j].effectRows are entry-point song data with no upper bound shown in the fragment, so their residual range is the full int domain per Phase 1(a).
limitations: OOB reads of pat->data[i][...] (e.g., rows i up to 10^7 and column index 4+(k<<1)) cannot be confirmed: the data array's row and column capacities are not declared in the fragment.
patChanX[chans] at line 274 is a potential OOB write, but patChanX's capacity is not shown; chans has no shown bound, so it is demoted to a limitation.

fxColors[pat->data[i][index]] (line 200) and extFxColors[pat->data[i][index]-0xe0] (line 218) are potential OOB reads, but fxColors/extFxColors sizes and pat->data element signedness/range are not shown.
volColors[volColor] (line 162) depends on the unshown size of volColors; the clamps at lines 159-160 bound volColor to 0..127 only.
The %s operand of sprintf at line 87 (noteName return) has an unshown maximum length, so that call site's overflow is not independently confirmed.
A NULL patCache[j] dereference at line 71 would require a NULL-producing statement inside the fragment; none exists, so it is out of scope.
e->song.ins[pat->data[i][2]]->type (line 123) is guarded by the line 120 range check, but ins array size vs insLen is not shown; not scored as a finding.

evidence.reason: limit is an unconstrained uint16_t taken from read_u16(data, 2) at line 31 after only equality guards (len == 1 at L23, len == 4 at L26); the loop at L33-35 copies 4 bytes to data+4+4i with no check that len >= 4+4*limit. The absent fix is a range check such as 'if (len < 4 + (limit * 4)) return 4 + (limit * 4);' before the loop.

limitations: Whether an unshown caller ever invokes the handler with intermediate lengths (e.g. 2..19 for SET_PIXEL_FORMAT, or len < 4+4*limit for SET_ENCODINGS) is external to the fragment; the verdict rests on the residual ranges after the only shown constraints (equality checks), per the analysis rules.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations carry protective statements that survive the BREAK test: getaddrinfo/socket/setsockopt/bind/getsockname return codes are checked before their results are used, ptr is NULL-checked before every dereference on line 70, and the only memory writes are size-bounded (snprintf with sizeof(strport), net_address_get with INET6_ADDRSTRLEN). evidence.reason: getaddrinfo's failure return (a negative EAI code under the standard analyzed semantics) is fully excluded before servinfo is used; the guard tests the exact int value produced at line 21 with no intervening modification, so ret >= 0 implies a successful, valid result.

A successful getaddrinfo returns a non-NULL servinfo list whose ai_next chain is NULL-terminated, so the line 28 loop terminates.

limitations: A NULL cfg global or NULL port/log_service_name can only be supplied by an out-of-scope caller; no shown statement inside the fragment produces them, so they are not findings.
On non-glibc platforms that return positive EAI error codes, the ret < 0 checks would not catch getaddrinfo failures; this is an unshown-environment portability concern, not an in-fragment failure.
net_address_get's body is not shown; its protective behavior is inferred only from the explicit size argument and standard bounded-string semantics.

cfgaddr contents reaching the DPRINTF log call are data passed to a literal-format logging function; a newline-injection reading would depend on unshown log-consumer interpretation and is not confirmed here.

num_migrate retains its full int domain because the only shown gate on it (line 14) checks the return of xfrm_migrate_check, whose body is not shown and therefore is not credited with bounding num_migrate.

The OOB path requires xfrm_migrate_state_find to return non-NULL on each iteration; the fragment's success branch (lines 30-33) is its designed flow and nothing shown limits how many times it can be taken.

The witness depends on the success of XFRM_MAX_DEPTH+1 find/migrate calls on supplied entries; that is the fragment's normal operational path and is admitted by every shown guard, but the exact downstream corruption is not shown.

rc = MqttClient_DecodePacket(client, client->rx_buf,

MqttClient_RespList_Find returning non-zero sets *pendResp to a non-NULL found entry, per standard list-lookup semantics.

verdict.summary: All memory operations are bounded by in-fragment capacities: the 2*hash_len calloc (line 22) split at hash_len (line 26) gives passwd2_sum exactly hash_len bytes, the reads at lines 29/31 cap at that size, the digest write (line 51) and compare (line 56) use hash_len = digest_length(d), and the PBKDF2 layout (lines 39/41) satisfies keylen + PBKDF2_SALT_LEN = PBKDF2_LENGTH = hash_len. verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a failure set demonstrable from the shown code is protected: the num_segments scalar read (line 13) is gated by the NumElements() != 0 check (line 11), and every segment id is validated to [0, num_segments) before use (line 45). evidence.snippet:
OP_REQUIRES(context, num_segments_tensor.NumElements() != 0,
                errors::InvalidArgument("Number of segments cannot be empty."));
evidence.reason: Protective gate for the line 13 scalar read: it excludes NumElements() == 0 on every reaching path, so scalar<NUM_SEGMENTS_TYPE>()() reads element 0 only when the tensor capacity is >= 1, which is in-bounds. BREAK test passes on identity (same tensor, no intervening modification), boundary (admitted set >= 1 vs failure boundary 0), degenerate (empty tensor excluded), and reach (unconditional before the use).

Protective gate for the segment-id values consumed at line 59: for every index i < flat_segment_id.size() it confines flat_segment_id(i) to [0, num_segments), which keeps output_index = start_offset + flat_segment_id(i) * big_stride within [0, num_segments*big_stride - 1] for the sink writes at lines 61-63 and excludes negative or oversized ids (CWE-787/CWE-125 candidate blocked). The same value, same precision, reaches the sink unmodified (guard-identity OK) for all indices the sink loop provably uses; any index beyond flat_segment_id.size() would require unshown helper semantics and fails the BLOCK test, so it is recorded as a limitation rather than a finding.

num_segments_tensor.scalar<NUM_SEGMENTS_TYPE>()() reads the first element, which is in-bounds whenever NumElements() >= 1, as enforced at line 11.
Tensor::flat<T>() exposes a contiguous view whose size equals the tensor's element count; flat_segment_id and flat_input sizes are the element counts of inputs 1 and 0.

segment_dims >= 1 (line 15) implies the segment tensor has at least one dimension; combined with the dim-equality checks (lines 22-28) and the segment-id bounds loop, every subsequently used segment id index that is covered by the validation loop is a valid flat index.
limitations: The failure sets of the sink accesses at lines 59-63 depend on the unshown bodies of GetOutputShape, GetStrides, and GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets; the fragment provides no output-capacity or offset-size relation, so OOB read/write witnesses for output_flat and flat_input cannot be confirmed (and are not assumed safe either).

If GetFlattenedRelativeOffsets ever returned more elements than flat_segment_id.size(), the line 59 read of flat_segment_id(i) would be an out-of-bounds read and the line 45 validation would not cover those indices; this witness dies at the BLOCK test because the size relation is not derivable from the shown code.

The int-typed loop counters (lines 42, 57, 58) can wrap only for tensors or strides exceeding 2^31 (e.g., big_stride > INT_MAX from unshown GetStrides semantics); this is a scale/robustness concern with no derived surviving witness.

A signed negative num_segments is rejected by the line 45 bound check whenever the segment tensor is non-empty, and an empty segment tensor makes the sink loops vacuous; any malformed output shape would be caught by OP_REQUIRES_OK at line 34.

blobheader contains at least the five distinct members read here (totlen, version, min_version, hdrsize, flags), whose storage sums to at least 10 bytes, so sizeof(blobheader) > sizeof(bh) on any conforming layout.

Callee bodies (dm_i2c_read, i2c_read, i2c_get_cur_bus_chip) are unshown; only their call-site semantics were analyzed.

verdict.summary: In protocol_client_msg, the SET_ENCODINGS path runs a memcpy/read_s32 loop driven by an attacker-controlled uint16 limit without validating limit*4+4 against the received length len on the len!=1/len!=4 path, causing out-of-bounds write/read; the CUT_TEXT path likewise passes an unvalidated dlen payload length to client_cut_text when len>8.

evidence.reason: On the len != 1 && len != 4 path (e.g., len == 5), limit is read from network bytes at line 31 with full residual range 0..65535 and no comparison against len; line 33 enters the loop and line 35 writes 4 bytes at data+4+i*4 for i up to limit-1, exceeding the len-byte extent of data declared at line 1 (witness: len==5, limit==1 writes indices 5..7). The len==4 guard at line 26 executes only when len==4 and never constrains the else path (guard-reach drift). Absent fix: a check such as 'if (4 + (limit * 4) > len) return 4 + (limit * 4);' before the loop.

When len >= 9 (skipping the len == 8 block at lines 64-75), dlen is read from network bytes and passed unchanged into client_cut_text, which consumes dlen bytes from data+8; the 1MB cap at line 66 and the early return at line 73 execute only when len == 8, so for len == 9 with dlen > 1 the read reaches beyond the len-byte extent (witness: len==9, large dlen reads past index 8). Absent fix: a check such as 'if (len < 8 + dlen) return 8 + dlen;' before the call.

assumptions: data exposes exactly len valid bytes as declared by the parameter pair `uint8_t *data, size_t len` (line 1).
len >= 1 at every invocation, derived from the in-fragment re-arm `vnc_read_when(vs, protocol_client_msg, 1)` at line 145.
read_u8/read_u16/read_u32/read_s32 return the bytes at the shown offsets; their standard semantics are reads of offset..offset+width-1.
limitations: The physical allocation capacity of the input buffer behind data is not shown, so the memcpy crossing the heap allocation is evidenced via the len-declared extent rather than a quoted capacity.

If an unshown caller guaranteed invocations only with exactly the full message sizes, the intermediate-length witnesses would be unreachable; the fragment itself provides no such guarantee and its `else` branch at line 30 explicitly handles non-minimum lengths.

The partial-length fixed-offset reads (lines 16-20, 45-46, 52, 58, 88-89, 113, 117, 120, 124, 127) share the same missing len >= offset+width validation but are subsumed by the primary loop finding and not separately reported.

verdict.summary: In the moveable-entry branch of r_bin_ne_get_entrypoints, a file-supplied segment number (segnum) is checked only with 'segnum > 0' before indexing bin->segment_entries[segnum - 1], so any segnum above the header's SegCount indexes past the end of the segment_entries array (out-of-bounds heap read).

NE header fields and entry-table bytes (SegCount, EntryTableLength, bundle_type, segnum) are file-derived and attacker-controlled; no shown constraint limits SegCount below 255 or bounds segnum.

The r_list_get_n(segments, entry_cs - 1) call (line 22) can be an out-of-range index, but the callee's standard semantics return NULL and the result is consumed only under the 's? s->paddr: 0' ternary at line 23, so that sink is protected.
The 1-byte bundle_type read at line 38 depends on the unshown relationship between entry_table allocation size and the r_buf_size guard, so it is recorded as a limitation, not a second finding.

verdict.summary: Every memory operation is protected: the ternary at line 70 caps linebytes at DISP_LINE_LEN, the capacity of linebuf declared at line 67, before either read branch (lines 73/75), and both display loops index only j < linebytes <= DISP_LINE_LEN, so no unconstrained attacker-derived value reaches a dangerous operation.

A length up to UINT_MAX drives up to ~2^28 read+print iterations of the loop at lines 66-98 (resource-exhaustion/DoS robustness concern, CWE-770-style); total work is technically bounded by UINT_MAX, and this does not change the memory-safety verdict.

The u32 wrap of mw->total_samples at line 52 (CWE-190) is real for large sampleCount sums but has no shown in-fragment consumer, so it is not reported as a finding.
Direct returns of GF_OUT_OF_MEM after stsc/stco allocation failure (lines 41, 47) skip CleanWriters and can leak the current writer; resource-leak concern only.
Unchecked gf_list_add/gf_list_insert returns are allocation-failure-only and not memory-unsafe per std semantics.

verdict.summary: Unvalidated row_remapping element values flow into the slice-building loop: a row_remapping containing 0 and INT64_MAX yields min_old_row=0 and max_old_row=INT64_MAX, so 'max_old_row - row_start + 1' overflows the signed int64 arithmetic, slice_length becomes 0, row_start stops advancing, and the while loop never terminates (non-termination/DoS).

The guard at line 106 admits this pair, and line 116 then computes INT64_MAX - 0 + 1, which wraps to INT64_MIN; line 121 leaves row_start=INT64_MIN, and the next iteration computes a slice_length of 0, so row_start never changes and the loop at line 112 never exits (CWE-835), the root cause being the absent bound check on remapping values (no max_old_row < tensor_shape.dim_size(0) validation and no slice_length > 0 / row_start-advance guard) combined with the signed overflow (CWE-190).

assumptions: num_rows_, num_cols_, and max_rows_in_memory_ are kernel attributes passed to Compute (declared outside the fragment).
output_matrix has the declared capacity {num_rows_, num_cols_} (line 129).
OP_REQUIRES aborts Compute on a false condition, so the guard at lines 185-193 fully protects the write at line 194.
row_id_present and col_id_present are sized by the unshown helper RemapVectorToMap consistently with num_rows_/num_cols_ (consistent with their use at line 213).

The OOB write sink at line 194 is protected (OP_REQUIRES at lines 185-193: new_row/new_col bounded to [0,num_rows_)/[0,num_cols_)) and is not a finding; likewise the initializing_values access at line 219 is guarded at lines 214-218.
Potential int-vs-int64 loop counter mismatches (>2^31 elements) and the unshown internals of RemapVectorToMap/SliceTensorShape were not used as findings.

verdict.summary: dims.resize(rank) at line 32 sizes a vector allocation from the untrusted permutation-element count with no upper bound, so a declared perm_shape with a huge known dimension (input rank unknown, perm == nullptr) drives rank to an enormous value and crashes the process via std::bad_alloc.

assumptions: rank is non-negative on all three producer paths: RankKnown/Rank, ValueKnown/Value, and a concrete tensor's NumElements produce only non-negative values.
c->Dim(input, in_idx) is a bounds-checked accessor returning UnknownDim for out-of-range indices, so the admitted negative in_idx values do not cause memory unsafety.
When perm is a concrete tensor, its element count equals NumElements(perm_shape), so WithValue (line 36) keeps AsInt64 reads within bounds.
limitations: The int32_t/int loop counters (lines 49, 58) could drift past the int64_t rank bound only for rank > 2^31, which is preempted by the line 32 allocation failure on realistic memory; that OOB witness is dead.
The negative-index admission (line 51, in_idx in [-rank+1, -1]) is a shape-inference logic quirk, not a memory-safety or security-decision failure given bounds-checked Dim.
Bodies of input_tensor/WithRank/WithValue/AsInt64/Dim/NumElements are unshown; their behavior is attributed only to their standard semantics as documented here.

The finding is a crash/availability issue (CWE-400) rather than memory corruption, and practical exploitability depends on shape inference being reachable with declared large shapes, which the fragment does not restrict.

Before naddr is consumed at lines 85-86, naddr_len (initialized to sizeof(naddr) at line 7 and written by getsockname at line 73) must satisfy naddr_len <= sizeof(naddr) after the ret < 0 check at line 74; the excluded set {naddr_len > sizeof(naddr)} prevents any kernel-reported address longer than the union from reaching net_port_get/net_address_get, and the getsockname write itself is length-bounded by naddr_len.

A NULL port, log_service_name, or cfg supplied only by an unshown caller is a caller-contract violation, not an in-fragment flaw.
errno/strerror at lines 67/76/81 may be stale on the empty-servinfo degenerate path, a disclosure-quality concern only, with no memory-safety sink.

The discard of the njs_function_call status at line 71 ((void) cast on the reject call) is a semantic/robustness concern only (reject handler not delivered on internal failure); no memory-safety consequence is demonstrable in-fragment.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in the fragment are protected: main_mach0, prelink_range, obj, prelink_info, and pending_bin_files are NULL-checked before every use, and the only file-derived values (prelink range offset/size) reach a parser whose NULL failure is checked and whose RBuffer reads are bounds-checked. No vulnerable sink with an unconstrained value exists in the shown code.

evidence.reason: Unbounded sprintf writes at suffix = filename + Ustrlen(filename) (line 16); with filename at length big_buffer_size-1 (admitted by the string_nextinlist copy cap of big_buffer_size at line 10), suffix points one byte before the end of the big_buffer_size-capacity buffer and the minimum output '.0.' plus NUL (4 bytes) already writes 3 bytes past capacity; no length-vs-remaining-space guard exists anywhere before lines 25/30/41, so the absent fix is a bound check such as comparing Ustrlen(filename) + max suffix length against big_buffer_size (or building the name with a dynamic allocator) before each sprintf; mechanism is an out-of-bounds write.

Same unprotected in-place sprintf family: any list item of length >= big_buffer_size-2 leaves insufficient room for '.' + up-to-256 nodename chars + NUL at the suffix computed at line 16, exceeding the big_buffer_size capacity shown at line 10; no protective capacity check precedes it, so this sink is ABSENT with the same CWE-787 mechanism.

The shortest of the three unbounded suffixes still writes '.' + euid digits + NUL (>= 3 bytes) at the line-16 suffix position; with filename length big_buffer_size-1 it writes past the big_buffer_size capacity with no shown bound check, resolving ABSENT under CWE-787.

s is the result of expand_string(host_number_string) at line 390; the fragment itself shows expand_string returns NULL on failure (explicit 'if (s == NULL)' checks at lines 236, 250, 310), and the only preceding guard (line 387, host_number_string != NULL) constrains the argument, not the result, so a failed expansion (e.g., an unresolvable $variable) delivers NULL to Ustrtol unblocked; absent fix is an 'if (s == NULL)' check logging and dying before use; mechanism is a NULL-pointer dereference (CWE-476).

assumptions: big_buffer has capacity big_buffer_size; the shown call passes big_buffer_size as the copy cap to string_nextinlist at line 10, so a copied filename of length big_buffer_size-1 is representable.
expand_string returns NULL on expansion failure, evidenced within the fragment by the repeated 'if (s == NULL)' checks at lines 236, 250, and 310.
log_write with LOG_PANIC_DIE has die semantics, so the NULL-check-plus-PANIC_DIE sites (spool_directory, log_file_path, pid_file_path) are treated as protected.
limitations: Whether big_buffer is heap or stack allocated is not shown, so the overflow is classified as CWE-787 rather than CWE-122/121.
The exact origin of config_main_filelist (command line vs built-in default) is outside the fragment; it is treated as entry-point input per the provenance rules.
Exploitability and the privilege context of Exim are not derivable from the fragment alone; severity is assessed from the uncontrolled out-of-bounds write in the config parser.

The only guard, while (u >= 0) at line 30, admits every unsigned value including UINT_MAX, so no bound constrains the sink; the absent one-statement fix is a signed cast (while ((int)u >= 0)) or a monotonic u > 0 cleanup. The error branch is reachable from fragment values alone: an in-domain windows_size whose product with sizeof(double) overflows sets overflow_error = 1 at line 23-24, or gdMalloc returns NULL, at u = 0, and the witness (u == UINT_MAX) survives the BLOCK test because no shown statement excludes it before the free.

gdMalloc may return NULL (checked at lines 8, 18, 28) and gdFree of an out-of-bounds pointer corrupts heap memory.
UINT_MAX is out of bounds for the ContribRow array for every line_length representable as unsigned int.

verdict.summary: ZRLE_DECODE's dangerous operations are each protected: palette indices are masked to 0..127 against palette[128] (L65, L116), RLE run lengths are validated against the remaining tile area before any write (L88, L111), and the tile area is capped at 64x64 == buf capacity by the __rfbmin bounds (L12, L16, L8).

evidence.reason: The palette read in the packed-pixels path is fully constrained: L65 applies `& 127` to the byte-derived index, admitting only 0..127, which equals the valid index set of palette[128] at L21; the BREAK test passes on identity (mask in the same expression consumed at L66), boundary (max admitted 127 is the last valid index, 128 excluded), degenerate (byte=0xFF still yields ≤ 127), and reach (mask executes on every packed path before the sink).

The palette read in the palette-RLE path is bounded by L116 `index &= 127;` executed on every iteration before this sink, capping the attacker-controlled index to 0..127 against palette[128] at L21, so no out-of-range value survives to the read.

The plain-RLE write loop is protected by the L88 `if (end - ptr < len) throw` check executed before it on the same iteration, so len is forced to ≤ end-ptr and ptr can never pass end = buf + t.area() with t.area() ≤ 4096 capped by the L12/L16 __rfbmin bounds against buf[64*64] at L8.

assumptions: sizeof(PIXEL_T) == BPP/8, so the raw `readBytes(buf, t.area() * (BPP / 8))` at L43 matches the buf[4096] byte capacity.
READ_PIXEL, readU8, and readU32 throw on end-of-stream (rdr::InStream standard semantics), so stream-driven loops terminate.
__rfbmin returns the smaller argument; t.area() is width()*height() in int arithmetic.
Capacities are those declared in-fragment: palette[128] at L21 and buf[64*64] at L8.
limitations: pb->fillRect/imageRect (L29, L125) write into the framebuffer whose capacity and rect clipping are not shown; any out-of-bounds framebuffer write would require an unshown pb invariant or caller-supplied rect with r unvalidated by this fragment, so it is not a demonstrated in-fragment failure.
`int length = is->readU32()` at L5 can become negative, but ZlibInStream::setUnderlying's handling of a negative segment length is unshown; no memory-safety sink in the fragment consumes that value.

`len += b` at L85/L108 can overflow int after an extreme run of 0xFF bytes; the wrapped-negative result fails the `end - ptr < len` check and skips the write loop, so no memory overrun is demonstrated (UB noted only).

In packed and palette-RLE modes an index ≥ palSize reads a within-bounds but never-initialized palette slot, which may disclose stale stack data; this is an information-disclosure robustness concern, not a memory-safety violation, and is not the decisive direction.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation carries a protective statement that survives the BREAK test: the paste buffer is declared as NUMBUFLEN + MB_MAXBYTES (line 4), the end-code length check (lines 12-13) caps idx below NUMBUFLEN at every write because idx only grows while prefix-matching end, and the gap copy is guarded by ga_grow(gap, idx + 1) == OK with a NULL check on gap (line 55).

No CWE because the failure set is empty for all admitted values.

The guard constrains the same idx and gap at the same control point, so no failure set is reachable.

mb_char2bytes, per its standard Vim semantics, writes at most MB_MAXBYTES bytes into buf + idx and returns that byte count.

limitations: No unshown caller is assumed to enforce additional bounds; all safety arguments derive from statements in the fragment.
A NULL return from find_termcode is handled by the end == NULL branches (lines 24, 39), so no NULL-deref candidate exists inside the fragment.
If the fragment's pair counterpart differs by a single local statement (e.g., a smaller buffer or a missing end-length cap), that variant is not the code shown here and is not analyzed.

verdict.summary: pxa3xx_gcu_write truncates the size_t write length via `int words = count / 4`, so an attacker-chosen count makes `words` negative; line 17's one-sided `>=` bound admits all negatives, the copy size `words * 4` wraps small so copy_from_user succeeds, and `buffer->ptr[words]` writes past the buffer (OOB write).

evidence.reason: `words` is a signed int derived by truncating `count / 4` (line 9) from the attacker-controlled `size_t` count, reaching a negative residual range; the guard at line 17 only excludes `words >= PXA3XX_GCU_BATCH_WORDS` and admits every negative value, e.g. `count = 0x300000004` yields `words = -1073741823`, for which `words * 4` wraps to 4 so the earlier `copy_from_user` at line 37 succeeds and the error return at line 38 is skipped; the sink then writes 0x01000000 at `buffer->ptr[-1073741823]`, an out-of-bounds write below the buffer whose capacity is implied by the same BATCH_WORDS constant, with the absent fix being a negative-word check (`words < 0`) or making `words` unsigned so truncation stays positive and fails the line 17 bound (CWE-787).

assumptions: `count` is the syscall write() length and is fully attacker-controlled (entry-point input).
`PXA3XX_GCU_BATCH_WORDS` is a small positive constant used as the buffer's word-count bound, as implied by the line 17 check and the line 16 comment.
Kernel builds wrap signed overflow in two's complement, so `words * 4` with negative `words` yields the small non-negative size needed for `copy_from_user` to succeed.
limitations: The actual allocation size of `buffer->ptr` is not declared inside the fragment; the out-of-bounds nature relies on the BATCH_WORDS-derived capacity implied by the guard, and on the magnitude of the negative index exceeding any plausible capacity.

Negative `words` whose `words * 4` does not wrap to a small non-negative size cause `copy_from_user` to return nonzero and exit via `-EFAULT` before the sink; the confirmed witness uses the wrapped-size case.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in regmatch() carries a protective statement that survives the BREAK test: the inner loop NULL-guards scan, getmark_buf() is NULL-checked before use, the BACK case re-fetches backpos.ga_data after ga_grow() and FAIL-checks the grow, MULTIBYTECODE validates the operand length (< 2 rejected), input[-1] accesses are gated by start-of-line checks, reg_getline() results are NULL-checked where required, and regstack growth is capped by maxmempattern. No attacker-controlled value reaches an unprotected operation.

evidence.reason: NULL-check of the compiled-program pointer `scan` executes at the top of every inner-loop iteration before `regnext(scan)` (line 83), `OP(scan)` (line 85) and every `OPERAND(scan)` deref; a NULL `scan` is excluded on every path reaching those sinks (BREAK: identity, reach, degenerate all hold), so program-pointer NULL dereference (CWE-476) resolves PRESENT.

The NULL-producing `getmark_buf()` result is tested for NULL (and for `lnum <= 0`) before any `pos->lnum`/`pos->col` deref later in the RE_MARK branch; the check constrains the same pointer at the same precision with no intervening modification and lies on every path to the derefs, so the NULL-deref sink resolves PRESENT.

The array write `bp[i].bp_scan = scan` is protected twice: `ga_grow(&backpos, 1) == FAIL` is fail-closed (status = RA_FAIL), and `bp` is re-read from `backpos.ga_data` after growth so a stale pointer is never used; the admitted write index `i == ga_len` is exactly the newly guaranteed capacity slot, so the CWE-787/416 candidate resolves PRESENT.

Pattern-driven stack growth is capped against 'maxmempattern' before the STAR/PLUS/BEHIND pushes (same guard at line 1016), failing closed to RA_FAIL; combined with the interrupt checks (fast_breakcheck line 26, timeout lines 47–57) and the FAIL-checks on every other ga_grow/regstack_push, unbounded attacker-pattern resource consumption (CWE-770/1333) resolves PRESENT.

assumptions: rex.input points into the current NUL-terminated line (rex.line) and rex.lnum stays within 0..reg_maxline; line 88 dereferences *rex.input while matching, and reg_nextline()/reg_getline() maintain this invariant.

reg_getline() returns NULL only for an out-of-range line number; the unguarded uses at lines 158 and 1309 evaluate the current line or a saved position previously established within range by the engine.
The compiled regexp program is well-formed as produced by the compiler; malformed opcodes are handled by the default case (iemsg + RA_FAIL) rather than by memory access.
regstack/backpos are growable arrays managed by ga_grow/ga_free semantics (ga_grow returns FAIL, and ga_data is invalidated on realloc, hence the re-fetch at line 581).
limitations: Multibyte pointer reads near the end of a line (utf_ptr2char/mb_ptr2char at lines 101, 508–529, 639) cannot be judged as out-of-bounds without the allocation capacity of the rex.input line buffer, which is not shown in this fragment.

The unguarded reg_getline() results at lines 158 and 1309 are assumed in-range from engine state (current line / saved match positions); a NULL there would require an out-of-scope engine invariant violation.

BRCPLX/LONG pushes do not perform the p_mmp check, but their growth is bounded by pattern constants and safe ga_grow FAIL handling plus interrupts; this is a robustness/DoS nuance, not a confirmed memory-safety flaw.
No caller of regmatch() is shown; NULL supplied for tm/timed_out is handled by the explicit NULL checks at lines 47 and 52, and the timeout path writes through timed_out only after its NULL check.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations visible in the fragment carry protective statements: the negative-index reads at BOW/EOW are gated by rex.input > rex.line and rex.input == rex.line respectively; opcode decoding is gated by the scan == NULL check; the backpos write occurs only after ga_grow plus a re-fetch of ga_data; and the MULTIBYTECODE compare loop is gated by the len < 2 safety check. No admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: The negative-index read rex.input[-1] is only evaluated after rex.input > rex.line on the same short-circuit expression, admitting only rex.input >= line+1 (index >= 0); the value checked is the exact pointer consumed, with no intervening modification, so the guard survives the BREAK test and no OOB read of line[-1] is derivable.

reaching this read requires passing the line-231 guard 'if (rex.input == rex.line) status = RA_NOMATCH;', which excludes rex.input == line; together with the shown forward-only producers of rex.input (ADVANCE_REGINPUT, rex.line + col with col >= 0, rex.line + STRLEN(rex.line), MB_PTR_BACK), the admitted set is rex.input >= line+1 and rex.input[-1] >= line, so the access is in bounds; the guard checks the same pointer consumed by the sink.

This check executes at the top of the inner loop on every path before regnext(scan)/OP(scan) at lines 83/85, excluding scan == NULL (a value produced inside the fragment when a state pop or regnext returns NULL) from the opcode decode, so the NULL-deref failure set of the decode is fully constrained.

The write bp[i].bp_scan = scan at i == backpos.ga_len occurs only after ga_grow(&backpos, 1) succeeds (capacity >= ga_len + 1) and after ga_data is re-fetched, so neither an out-of-bounds write nor a use of a stale pointer freed by realloc can reach the sink; the grow/refetch pair neutralizes the failure set.

assumptions: ga_grow(..., n) has Vim's standard semantics: on OK it guarantees capacity for at least ga_len + n items and may reallocate ga_data; on FAIL it leaves the array unchanged.

All shown producers of rex.input keep rex.input >= rex.line (ADVANCE_REGINPUT, rex.input = rex.line + col with col >= 0, rex.input = rex.line + STRLEN(rex.line), and MB_PTR_BACK used only when rex.input != rex.line).

Case labels MOPEN+0..9, MCLOSE+0..9, ZOPEN+1..9, ZCLOSE+1..9, BACKREF+1..9, ZREF+1..9 and BRACE_COMPLEX+0..9 constrain the computed index no to 0..9; the corresponding arrays' sizes are declared outside the fragment.
limitations: Reads whose backing-object capacity is not declared or computed in the fragment — e.g., rex.input[i] for i < len in MULTIBYTECODE beyond a line NUL, rex.line + col after the line re-fetch in RE_MARK, and mb_head_off(line, ...) with a possibly NULL line in RS_BEHIND2 — cannot be confirmed as OOB from the shown statements and were not promoted to findings.
Code under #ifdef DEBUG and #ifdef FEAT_RELTIME is not credited as protective and could not affect the verdict.

The provenance of rex/regstack/backpos contents (validity of saved lnum/col positions, NSUBEXP array sizes) is maintained by unshown callers/engine state; any NULL therein is a limitation rather than an in-fragment finding.

verdict.summary: In tgs_build_reply, the return status of principal-construction helpers is discarded (_krb5_principalname2krb5_principal at lines 144/149/93, krb5_make_principal at 236/254); on failure the NULL-initialized sp/cp (line 17) or uninitialized p (line 70) is immediately dereferenced inside krb5_unparse_name, letting a crafted TGS request crash the KDC. The missing one-line fix is a return check (if (ret) goto out;) after each producer call.

evidence.reason: sp is NULL-initialized (line 17) and produced by _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal at line 144, whose return value is discarded; on helper failure (allocation/parse error) sp remains NULL and is dereferenced by krb5_unparse_name here, an unchecked construction-failure NULL dereference (CWE-476). The guard at lines 146-147 checks krb5_unparse_name's own return only after the dereference (check-then-use drift), and the missing fix is the one-line `if (ret) goto out;` after line 144.

cp is NULL-initialized (line 17) and produced by _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal at line 149 with the return discarded; on failure cp stays NULL and is dereferenced in krb5_unparse_name here with no intervening check — same missing `if (ret) goto out;` fix and the same NULL-deref mechanism (CWE-476); the guard at 151-152 runs only after the sink.

p is declared uninitialized (line 70) and _krb5_principalname2krb5_principal at line 93 has its return discarded; on failure p is indeterminate and is read by krb5_unparse_name here — uninitialized pointer use (CWE-457) with the missing fix `if (ret) goto out;` after line 93; the guard at lines 95-96 checks the sink's own return afterward and protects nothing.

assumptions: krb5_unparse_name dereferences its principal argument, so a NULL or indeterminate principal is invalid at the call.

_krb5_principalname2krb5_principal and krb5_make_principal are error-returning principal constructors that can fail; on failure an out parameter is left at its prior value (NULL for sp/cp, indeterminate for p).
Request fields (b->sname, b->realm, b->additional_tickets, b->etype) and TGT fields (tgt->cname/crealm) are entry-point network data; b->sname non-NULL is enforced at lines 138-141.
limitations: The helper bodies are unshown; the demonstrated failure trigger is their error return (allocation/parse failure), and a deterministic non-OOM trigger is not shown, which caps confidence.
The identical discarded-return pattern at lines 236-240 (capath branch) and 254-258 (need_referral branch) feeds krb5_unparse_name with a possibly-NULL sp but is not separately counted.
The etype loop (lines 306-318) and additional_tickets->val[0] (line 84) are properly bounded; no OOB candidate was found.
check_PAC receiving a NULL client on the HDB_ERR_NOT_FOUND_HERE path is not counted because the callee-internal dereference behavior is unshown.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in cx23888_ir_probe is guarded: the kzalloc result is NULL-checked before any dereference, kfifo_alloc failure frees state and returns, and sd->name is written only through size-bounded snprintf, so no admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: The kzalloc NULL-producer at line 8 is excluded on every reaching path by this guard before lines 12, 13, 19, 37, 41, and 45 dereference or free state, so no NULL dereference is possible; the admitted set contains only non-NULL state.

A non-zero kfifo_alloc return (failure) is handled by freeing state and returning, so every later use and the kfifo_free at line 45 operate only on an initialized fifo; no failing value reaches a fifo sink.

The snprintf destination is bounded by sizeof(sd->name), so the %s/888-ir payload cannot overflow sd->name regardless of dev->name length; the check-then-use and boundary BREAK steps pass because the bound is applied at the exact sink.

assumptions: dev is a non-NULL kernel probe parameter; plain parameters are treated as non-NULL because no shown statement can make it NULL.
kfifo_alloc returns 0 on success and non-zero on failure, per its standard semantics.
limitations: On v4l2_device_register_subdev failure (ret != 0, line 45 path) state is leaked because kfree(state) is absent; this is a one-time, non-attacker-repeatable resource leak (CWE-401 robustness concern), not a demonstrated memory-safety or exhaustion vulnerability.
An over-read in snprintf would require dev->name to lack NUL termination, a caller contract violation not shown in the fragment, so that candidate is demoted.
The return value after the register_subdev failure branch is not shown in the fragment, so any fail-open from returning success cannot be assessed within the shown statements.

verdict.summary: The MNG CLIP chunk handler iterates object ids from first_object to last_object (attacker-controlled 16-bit values) without bounding i below MNG_MAX_OBJECTS, unlike the sibling MOVE handler (lines 894-895), so the MngInfo object arrays are indexed out of bounds (up to 65535), yielding a heap out-of-bounds read of exists[]/frozen[] and a conditional out-of-bounds write to object_clip[].

evidence.reason: first_object/last_object are (p[0]<<8)|p[1] and (p[2]<<8)|p[3] in [0,65535] (lines 809-810) gated only by `length > 3` (line 807), and the loop at line 813 admits every i through last_object without any bounds check, while the fragment's own conventions bound these arrays to 0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1 (init loops at lines 114-118 and 326-327, and the MOVE guard `i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` at lines 894-895). For payload FF FF FF FF, i reaches 65535 and `mng_info->exists[i]` is an out-of-bounds heap read; the data offset test at line 821 is evaluated after the subscript and never bounds i. The absent fix is the MOVE-style `if ((i < 0) || (i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS)) continue;` inside the CLIP loop, so the unconstrained entry-point-derived index reaches the memory access (CWE-125).

When the out-of-bounds `exists[i]` read returns nonzero with `!frozen[i]`, the same unconstrained i (up to 65535) is written via `mng_info->object_clip[i]=mng_read_box(...)` for any length satisfying line 821 (`length-17 > 4`), producing a heap out-of-bounds write because i is never checked against MNG_MAX_OBJECTS before the subscript; the missing fix is the bounds guard present in the MOVE handler (lines 894-895) (CWE-787, secondary to the CWE-125 read).

assumptions: MNG_MAX_OBJECTS is the element count of the MngInfo object arrays, with valid indices 0..MNG_MAX_OBJECTS-1, inferred from the init loops at lines 114-118 and 326-327 and from the exclusive bound `i >= MNG_MAX_OBJECTS` in the MOVE handler at lines 894-895.
MNG_MAX_OBJECTS <= 65535, so the 16-bit first/last_object values can exceed the array bound (e.g., 0xFFFF); otherwise the MOVE guard at line 894 would be dead code.

Chunk payload bytes p[0..3] are attacker-controlled file data, and chunk is allocated with length+MagickPathExtent bytes (line 185) so logical overreads past `length` are not separate memory-safety failures.
limitations: DEFI chunk: the guard at line 384 admits object_id == MNG_MAX_OBJECTS after the clamp at line 392 and uses it to index exists/frozen/x_off/y_off/object_clip; whether that index is out of bounds depends on unshown MngInfo array sizing ([MNG_MAX_OBJECTS] vs [MNG_MAX_OBJECTS+1]); the comment at lines 386-389 suggests slot MNG_MAX_OBJECTS may be an intended sentinel, so this was not asserted as a finding.

PLTE: the allocation at lines 502-504 is not NULL-checked before the loop dereferences global_plte at line 508; this is OOM/environment-dependent only and treated as a robustness concern, not the decisive vulnerability.
DISC/SEEK passes i up to 65535 into the unshown MngInfoDiscardObject (line 868); the callee's internal bounds are unknown, so no failure can be demonstrated from the fragment alone.

LOOP/ENDL index loop_active/loop_count/loop_iteration with loop_level = chunk[0] in [0,255]; the sizes of those arrays are not shown, and MNG permits loop levels 0-255, so no in-fragment OOB is provable.

MAGN arithmetic and pixel write bounds depend on image->columns/rows originating from the unshown PNG reader, and the row/column sum formulas match the computed magnified dimensions; overflow paths require external dimension provenance, so they were not confirmed.
IHDR-process uses the DEFI-clamped object_id for exists[]/x_off[]/y_off[] accesses; it shares the DEFI capacity ambiguity.

verdict.summary: The parameters fname and backup are used directly as asprintf format operands with only a post-hoc allocation-status check and a NULL/empty guard respectively; neither constrains format-specifier content, so a value containing '%' is interpreted as format directives, a format-string injection (CWE-134).

evidence.reason: fname (const char*, residual range unconstrained by the fragment) reaches the asprintf format operand with only idstring as a variadic argument, and the sole shown check is the post-hoc -1 status test, so a fname such as "%n" is interpreted as format directives; the absent fix is a literal "%s" format with fname passed as an argument, or validation that fname contains no '%' (CWE-134).

backup is also passed as the asprintf format operand; the guard at line 8 excludes only NULL/empty strings, not format-specifier content, so a backup containing '%' is admitted and interpreted as format directives, an independent sink with the same absent fix — a literal "%s" format or '%'-content validation (CWE-134).

assumptions: asprintf follows standard semantics: its first argument is a printf-family format string and only the shown variadic argument idstring is supplied.
FatalError terminates the process on allocation/rename/remove failure, so the null-stat path after a failed asprintf is not treated as a NULL-dereference finding.
The fragment contains no loop, so Phase 3 iteration-bound analysis is vacuous.
limitations: No call site is shown for LogFilePrep, so exploitability of the format-string sinks depends on a caller supplying attacker-influenced fname/backup values; if callers always pass trusted literals, no trigger exists.
The block at lines 8-27 (stat/S_ISREG before rename, and remove with ENOENT tolerated) was reviewed and found to be status-correct with no independent finding.

verdict.summary: The bounds checks use '>' against the memslot counts, admitting slot_id equal to num_memslots and group_id equal to num_memslots_groups, so line 22 indexes mem_slots one element past the end and the out-of-bounds MemSlot is subsequently dereferenced.

evidence.reason: slot_id comes from memslot_get_id(info, addr) at line 15 with attacker-controlled addr, and the guard at line 16 ('slot_id > info->num_memslots') admits slot_id == info->num_memslots, which is one past the last valid index (0..num_memslots-1) of the num_memslots-element array dimension; line 22 therefore reads mem_slots[group_id][num_memslots] out of bounds, and the same '>' off-by-one at line 10 admits group_id == info->num_memslots_groups for the first dimension. The absent fix is the >= forms ('slot_id >= info->num_memslots', 'group_id >= info->num_memslots_groups'); the OOB MemSlot is then dereferenced at lines 25 and 35 (generation, address_delta), matching CWE-125.

assumptions: info->num_memslots and info->num_memslots_groups are element counts of the mem_slots dimensions, so valid indices are 0..count-1; this is read from the 'num_' field naming and their role as the array bounds in the shown guards.
memslot_get_id can yield the boundary count value for some addr, as the guard exists precisely because the helper's id output is unbounded relative to num_memslots.
limitations: The exact output range of memslot_get_id is not shown; the witness rests on the helper producing precisely the boundary value (off-by-one at the exact edge).
Negative slot_id/group_id values are also admitted by the '>' guards, but their production by memslot_get_id cannot be demonstrated from the fragment alone.

verdict.summary: Off-by-one bounds check in the fixed-file cancel path: `fd > ctx->nr_user_files` admits `fd == nr_user_files`, so an attacker-controlled fd equal to the fixed-file count reaches `io_fixed_file_slot(&ctx->file_table, fd)` and reads one slot past the valid fixed-file table (CWE-125 OOB read).

evidence.reason: Entry-point `fd` (cancel-op user input) is admitted by the line 11 check `fd > ctx->nr_user_files`, whose `>` operator leaves `fd == nr_user_files` in the admitted set `[0, nr_user_files]`; the table has `nr_user_files` valid slots (0..N-1), so index N is out of bounds. The line 13 `array_index_nospec` is a speculation-masking macro, not a bound-rejecting validation (expansion unshown, its contract presupposes a correct bounds check), so nothing on the path excludes the witness before the line 14 read. The absent one-statement fix is `if (unlikely(fd >= ctx->nr_user_files)) return -EBADF;` which would exclude `fd == nr_user_files`; its absence permits the off-by-one OOB read, and a garbage `file_ptr & FFS_MASK` at line 15 can additionally become a bogus `cd->file` used downstream.

assumptions: `ctx->nr_user_files` is the count of valid fixed-file table slots, so valid indices are 0..nr_user_files-1 — the fragment's own guard at line 11 uses it as that limit.
On the fixed-file branch, line 16's `if (!cd->file)` executes before `cd->file` reaches `__io_async_cancel`.
limitations: If `array_index_nospec`'s clamping semantics were credited, `fd == nr_user_files` would be transformed to index 0, so the OOB read would not retire and the defect would degenerate to wrong-target cancellation; it is not credited because it is a macro whose expansion is not shown and is documented as a speculation mitigation that presupposes a correct bounds check.
NULL `cd` / caller-provided `cd->file` on the non-fixed path (line 20) are supplied only by an unshown caller and were not treated as findings.
Exact heap layout and table-bucket rounding are not shown; the confirmed failure is the logical OOB index (fd == nr_user_files) on the N-slot table, independent of allocation rounding.

verdict.summary: Every src-side dangerous operation is guarded: the L9-11 NUL-stop bounds all *p accesses to the terminator position, the L25 `!last` guard excludes the terminator from the '/' restore, the L12 `*(p - 1)` read has a structurally empty failure set (p - 1 >= src always), and the stat() status is checked (L17). The only unguarded writes, *q at L20 and *r at L21, target dst, whose capacity is never declared or computed in the fragment, so no out-of-bounds witness is derivable from the shown code and no dangerous operation is confirmed.

evidence.reason: Guard bounding all *p accesses: while !last, p never exceeds the source terminator position src_len, so the *p = '\0' write at L16 (maximum index src_len, the NUL slot itself) and the *p read at L12 stay within src. BREAK test passes on identity (same p, no intervening modification on the reaching path), boundary (src_len is a valid index of the NUL-terminated buffer), degenerates (entry at the NUL sets last immediately), and reach (executes once per iteration on every path to the sinks).

Guard on the L28 restore write *p = '/': it executes only when *p was a genuine '/' before the terminator, admitting indices <= src_len - 1 and excluding the NUL position; BREAK passes on identity, boundary, degenerate (at the terminator last=true, so the write is skipped), and reach (L25 lies on every path to L28). This prevents corrupting the terminator and keeps the write strictly inside src.

Return-status handling for stat(): the == 0 comparison is checked before s.st_mode is consumed and before mkdir_attr runs, and the && short-circuit means s is never read on the failure path, excluding uninitialized use (CWE-457) and unchecked-status (CWE-754) candidates.

assumptions: src is a NUL-terminated C string whose terminator lies within its allocation; the L9-11 stop relies on and never dereferences past that terminator.
src_prefix_len is at most the position of src's terminator (an unshown caller contract); a larger value would make the entry-time *p read at L9 depend on an unshown capacity and caller bug.
dst's allocation capacity is not declared or computed anywhere in the fragment, so the dst-side writes cannot be sized.
limitations: The *q = '\0' (L20) and *r = '/' (L21) writes advance in lockstep with p and are never bounded against dst; the absent one-statement fix would be a q - dst capacity bound, but without a shown dst capacity the CWE-787 witness is not derivable from the fragment and is demoted per the OOB capacity rule.
If src_prefix_len exceeded strlen(src), the entry read *p at L9 would be out of bounds; this requires an unshown caller contract violation and an unshown src capacity, so it is not a finding.

mkdir_attr()'s failure status is not checked, but it is void and its success gating (stat()) is already validated; unchecked directory creation failure is a robustness concern, not a security decision visible in the fragment.
Overall dst safety depends on the unshown caller allocating dst at least dst_prefix_len + (strlen(src) - src_prefix_len) + 1 bytes; out-of-scope callers are not analyzed.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: the kzalloc result is NULL-checked before any dereference, and the rpmsg_ctrldev_register_device status is fully checked before the success return; no unconstrained value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: kzalloc may return NULL, and every later vch dereference (lines 13, 16-21) is protected by the line 9 `if (!vch)` guard, which excludes exactly NULL on every reaching path before the first use; the BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach.

The registration status is stored at line 23 and consumed at line 24 by `if (err)`, which excludes every nonzero value via `return ERR_PTR(err)` at line 26 and admits only err==0 to the success return; the guard constrains the same value with no intervening modification, so the call's full failure set is handled.

assumptions: kzalloc returns NULL on allocation failure, and that NULL is excluded by the line 9 check.
vdev and vrp->vdev are non-NULL per the virtio/rpmsg driver contract; no shown statement can make them NULL.
limitations: If rpmsg_ctrldev_register_device fails before taking a device reference that would trigger virtio_rpmsg_release_device, the error path leaks vch; this is a resource/robustness concern without a shown attacker trigger, not a memory-safety failure in the fragment.
A NULL vrp or vrp->vdev dereference at lines 19/21 would require an unshown caller to supply a NULL vdev->priv or vrp->vdev, which no shown statement can produce.
The caller's handling of the returned ERR_PTR/rpdev_ctrl is outside the fragment and was not analyzed.

verdict.summary: usb_get_intfdata(interface) at line 3 can return NULL (the fragment itself stores NULL into that datum at line 19), but no NULL check precedes the dereference of atusb->usb_dev at line 5, causing a NULL pointer dereference in the disconnect path.

evidence.reason: atusb is the unchecked result of usb_get_intfdata(interface) at line 3, whose domain includes NULL as demonstrated by usb_set_intfdata(interface, NULL) at line 19; NULL reaches the dereference of atusb->usb_dev here because no if (!atusb) return; guard (or equivalent) exists between lines 3 and 5 on the sole straight-line path, so the witness survives the BLOCK test — CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference.

assumptions: usb_get_intfdata returns the value previously stored by usb_set_intfdata for the interface, per standard USB API semantics.
NULL is a valid value of that stored datum, established verbatim by usb_set_intfdata(interface, NULL) at line 19.
limitations: A NULL usb_dev member with non-NULL atusb is not independently demonstrated by the fragment; the confirmed finding is the NULL atusb produced by the line 3 lookup.
The NULL-tolerance of usb_kill_urb/usb_free_urb was not relied on; downstream USB core lifecycle behavior is unshown.
The connectivity of the disconnect path (probe-failure flows) is outside the fragment, but the shown usb_set_intfdata(interface, NULL) suffices to demonstrate the NULL-producing state.

verdict.summary: All security-relevant operations carry protective statements that survive the BREAK test: payload reads are gated by an exact message-size check, both allocations are NULL-checked before use, mmap_size is computed in uint64 from uint16 operands so it cannot overflow, and the descriptor-initialization loops are bounded by the allocated per-queue regions.

evidence.reason: Sink resolves PRESENT: mmap_size (line 50) is the uint64 product of uint16 num_queues and the per-queue helper value, is passed verbatim to inflight_mem_alloc (line 51), and addr reaches this memset only after the `if (!addr)` error return (line 52) executes on every path, so addr is a mapping of exactly mmap_size bytes; maximum admitted size (65535 * per-queue size) does not exceed the mapped capacity and the multiplication cannot wrap in uint64.

evidence.snippet:
for (j = 0; j < queue_size; j++)
				inflight_packed->desc[j].next = j + 1;
evidence.reason: Sink resolves PRESENT: `j < queue_size` (line 81) bounds the flexible descriptor array index, and get_pervq_shm_size_packed/split(queue_size) (lines 46-48) provides per-queue capacity including header plus queue_size descriptors; outer bound `i < num_queues` (line 76) with step pervq_inflight_size (line 83) keeps every block within num_queues*pervq_inflight_size == mmap_size, so no admitted value reaches an out-of-region write.

Sink resolves PRESENT: the allocation's NULL result is checked at line 52 before any use, the size expression at line 50 cannot overflow uint64 (uint16 num_queues promoted against uint64 pervq_inflight_size), and the exact message-size check at line 13 gates the payload fields that feed the size.

assumptions: get_pervq_shm_size_packed/split(queue_size) returns, per its name semantics, the per-queue region size including the inflight header and queue_size descriptor entries.
inflight_mem_alloc maps exactly mmap_size bytes, and addr's NULL result is the only failure indicator it exposes.
ctx->fds has at least one slot (standard vhu_msg_context layout), so `ctx->fds[0] = fd` (line 71) is not out of bounds.
limitations: An arbitrarily large attacker-chosen mmap_size (e.g., num_queues=queue_size=65535) could exhaust memory (CWE-770/CWE-400) only if the mapping succeeds in an overcommit-capable environment; the line 52 NULL check converts allocation failure into an error return, so the DoS witness depends on unshown environmental facts and is demoted.
`desc[queue_size-1].next = queue_size` stores a descriptor index outside the 0..queue_size-1 ring range; ring-consistency effects are consumed outside this fragment, so no sink is demonstrable here.

verdict.summary: In the loop, the property id is read from the section buffer with CDF_GETUINT32(p, i << 1) before any bound check, so a file-derived sh.sh_properties that is large relative to the actual section length drives a read past the section end e (up to past the mapped stream), an unguarded out-of-bounds read.

limitations: cdf_get_property_info_pos is not shown; the witness assumes it can return a non-NULL q inside [p, e) for i=1 (e.g., q = p for a zero offset field). Its own internal checks could reject some crafted sections, and a hard crash beyond the mapping additionally requires the section end to lie within a few bytes of the mapped stream end.

verdict.summary: bgp_capability_msg_parse performs a fixed 4-byte memcpy from pnt+3 even when only 3 bytes of the capability remain (hdr->length can be 0..3), producing an out-of-bounds read of the packet buffer past end.

No loop constructs exist in the fragment; iteration-bound analysis is vacuous.

                            (paintType == 1) ? colorMode : splashModeMono8, true);
