The tile-draw loops iterate imgData.repeatX * imgData.repeatY times where both counters are attacker-controlled ints set from x1-x0 / y1-y0 (L78-79) or inflated to them (L104-107) with no upper bound — only L119 requires the (overflowable) product to exceed 4 — so e.g. x1-x0 = 1e9 with a legal bitmap admits ~1e9+ blitImage iterations per row pass, i.e., unbounded work driven by entry-point input, CWE-770.

assumptions: mat, ptm, bbox, xStep/yStep, x0..y1 are entry-point PDF-derived values; L24 ties xStep to width but imposes no positivity/magnitude bound.
Matrix::transform with m1.m[1]==m1.m[2]==0 (L55-56) maps kx = m1.m[0]*width, ky = m1.m[3]*height.
The 0x800000L product cap at L81 applies only to the else branch (L80-108); L119 constrains only zero dims and repeatX*repeatY > 4.
The L85-90 halving loop only shrinks kx/ky, so the L81 cap stays effective for the else-branch allocation.
limitations: Division by zero at L48 (ctm[0]==0 && ctm[1]==0) and L72 (kx==0) produce IEEE inf/NaN, which are dangerous only later via double->int casts whose UB behavior is compiler-dependent; kept as a demoted candidate.

Whether huge (or int-cast-overflowed negative) dimensions inside SplashBitmap lead to clean NULL data (caught at L129) or to wrapped allocations depends on the unshown constructor; primary confirmed impact is uncontrolled allocation/loop resource exhaustion (CWE-770).
Line 119's repeatX * repeatY int product can itself overflow; in the wrapped-to-<=4 direction it fails closed, so it is not a separate finding.
Membership in the vulnerable/fixed pair was not used as evidence (membership-identity ban); verdict rests solely on the shown guards and the BLOCK/BREAK tests.

verdict.summary: One-byte heap buffer overflow: for len==1, the post-loop statement name[i/2]='\0' writes index 1 into a 1-byte allocation, because i is left at 2 and i/2 is never bounded.

evidence.reason: Line 7 allocates exactly len bytes (capacity len), and lines 5-6 admit len in 1..400 including len==1. The line 18 loop with i+=2 leaves i=2 after len==1, so line 19 writes at index i/2=1, one byte past the 1-byte buffer — a heap out-of-bounds write. The fragment has no bound check on the final write index (e.g., excluding len==1 or allocating len+1). Mechanism: attacker-influenced length admitted by the guards reaches an unchecked write, CWE-787.

assumptions: cli_malloc(len) returns exactly len usable bytes per its standard semantics; the shown NULL check confirms the allocation can fail but not under-size.
fread(name, len, 1, f) succeeding implies len bytes were read into the len-byte buffer, keeping the read in-bounds.
len is a SIS string-length field (uint32_t) per the helper's role; any value in the admitted residual range 1..400 is permissible absent a shown caller constraint.
limitations: No call site is shown, so attacker ability to supply len==1 is inferred from the helper's length-field semantics rather than an in-fragment producer; the overflow itself is fully derivable in-fragment for any len==1 value.
Impact is a single NUL-byte overwrite, which limits severity despite the confirmed memory-safety violation.
fseek's return is unchecked, but any seek failure fails the subsequent checked fread and returns NULL, so no separate finding is made.

verdict.summary: All memory operations are bounded: len is restricted to [1,400] by an early return (line 5) and a clamp (line 6) executed on every reaching path, and every sink index (max read 399, max write 200) fits within the len+1 allocation.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement: the clamp restricts the uint32_t len to the admitted set 1..400 before allocation (line 7), fread (line 13), and the compaction loop (line 18) on every reaching path, with no intervening modification of len. The BREAK test passes: identity (same value/precision at sink), boundary (max read index 399 < capacity 401; max write index 200 <= 401; NUL at i/2 <= 200), degenerate (len=1 minimal case valid, len=400 valid), and reach (executes before every sink; the only prior exit is line 5 for len==0). No OOB (CWE-787/125), NULL deref (CWE-476), or uninitialized use (CWE-457) is reachable within the fragment.

Supporting protective statement: excludes the degenerate len==0 value before allocation and indexing, completing the residual range [1,400] established with the line 6 clamp; ensures the loop executes at least once with all indices in-bounds.

assumptions: cli_malloc returns NULL on allocation failure, and that failure is checked at lines 8-11 before any use of name.
fread(name, len, 1, f) returns 1 only when the full len bytes were read, so name[0..len-1] is initialized whenever execution proceeds past line 13.
len is uint32_t, and the line 5 and line 6 checks execute unconditionally on every path that reaches the memory sinks.
limitations: The fseek return (line 12) is unchecked; on failure fread may read from an unexpected offset, producing incorrect string content for the caller, but the read is still bounded to len <= 400 bytes within the 401-byte allocation, so no in-fragment memory-safety failure results.

No call site of getsistring is shown, so the provenance of ptr/len is not attributed; the clamp bounds len regardless of provenance, and ptr is used only as an fseek offset with no memory consequence.
Callee bodies (cli_malloc, fread) are analyzed only by their standard return semantics, as their implementations are not shown.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in cdf_read_property_info is fully constrained in-fragment: property-index writes are capped by i < sh.sh_properties against an allocation grown by sh.sh_properties plus each vector's nelements; the string length-word read at line 112 is guarded by the verbatim check `if (o4 + sizeof(uint32_t) > left) goto out;` (lines 109-110); the string payload store at lines 118-119 is guarded by `if (o4 + l > left) goto out;` (lines 114-115); vector counts are rejected when zero or over CDF_ELEMENT_LIMIT (line 60) with `left >= 8` enforced (line 55); helper results are NULL-checked (lines 43-44, 33-34, 100-101); and scalar copies fail closed through the `!cdf_copy_info(...)` return check with an end-pointer argument. No failing witness survives the BLOCK test, so no vulnerability is demonstrated.

evidence.reason: Protective statement for the string-length read `l = CDF_GETUINT32(q, slen)` at line 112: it admits only o4 + 4 <= left, i.e. q[o4..o4+3] is fully inside [q, e), so the length word read is bounded on every path; the guard tests the same o4 value, at the same size_t precision, immediately before the use, and survives the BREAK test (boundary o4+4 == left is an exact 4-byte fit; degenerate o4 > left fails closed).

Protective statement for the string payload store `inp[i].pi_str.s_buf = ... &q[o4]` at lines 118-119: it admits only o4 + l <= left, so q[o4..o4+l) stays within [q, e) for every attacker-supplied l (including l == 0, where s_buf is at most one-past-end and is only stored, not dereferenced in-fragment); it constrains the exact values consumed by the sink with no intervening modification and executes on every reaching path, surviving the BREAK test.

Protective statements for the vector-count read and the subsequent string loop: left >= 8 guarantees the count word q[1] is in-bounds, and nelements == 0 (which would make the string loop degenerate) is rejected along with values above CDF_ELEMENT_LIMIT, so the count admitted to the loop is 1..CDF_ELEMENT_LIMIT on every path.

assumptions: cdf_get_property_info_pos returns NULL unless the i-th id/type pair is fully inside [p, e), so the id read at line 45 and the q pointer used for all subsequent reads are in-bounds when it is non-NULL (line 43).

cdf_grow_info grows the array by its incr argument (line 32 grows by sh.sh_properties, line 99 by nelements), updates *maxcount, and returns NULL on failure; capacity after all grows therefore equals P + sum(nelements) over vectors, which exceeds every index written.

cdf_copy_info is a bounded copy taking an explicit end pointer e and returns a status; the shown `if (!cdf_copy_info(...)) goto unknown;` tests are fail-closed, so scalar copies (lines 78/85/92) cannot read past e.
CDF_PROP_LIMIT and CDF_ELEMENT_LIMIT are the visible caps applied at lines 30 and 60, so i and nelements cannot drive size_t arithmetic overflow in i << 1 or o4 computations.
limitations: DPRINTF (lines 121-124) is a debug-only macro whose expansion is not shown; if a CDF_DEBUG build enabled printf("%s", s_buf), a string of length l with no guaranteed NUL (notably l == 0 with s_buf == e) could cause an OOB read in the debug build, but no such consumer is active in the analyzed configuration.

The scalar-copy paths (CDF_SIGNED16/32/64 etc.) have no local o4+size left-check; their safety rests on cdf_copy_info's standard bounded-copy semantics with the e argument, which is callee behavior rather than a verbatim in-fragment guard.
No evaluation of downstream consumers of pi_str.s_buf/pi_str.s_len outside this function was possible; only in-fragment uses were analyzed.

evidence.reason: Loop bound admits i in [0, argc-1]; argv has argc entries from ExpandFilenames' success contract, so the max index argc-1 is in bounds; BREAK passes identity, boundary, degenerate (argc==0 yields zero iterations), and reach.
Return-status check executes on the only path that touches argv; on failure it branches out before any argv[i] use, so no partially-initialized or stack-backed argv content reaches the loop.
Excludes the NULL image list before CloneImageList/WriteImages on every path except the explicit 'null:' coder break at line 134, so a NULL list never reaches the write sink.

Depth cap executes before every push on both stacks (line 194 for braces), excluding nesting growth beyond MAX_STACK_DEPTH; the count loop it follows terminates on the NULL sentinel.

assumptions: argc is int, set to 1 at line 92, and on ExpandFilenames success describes an owned heap array of argc entries (standard callee semantics), making argv[0..argc-1] valid.

DestroyString, DestroyImageList, AppendImageToList, WriteImages, and RelinquishMagickMemory follow ImageMagick's NULL-safe/ownership semantics, so the cleanup and write paths cannot double-free or dereference NULL.
key[MagickPathExtent] is the declared capacity for the FormatLocaleString sink at line 139.
limitations: AcquireString('-1') at line 359 is passed to IsSceneGeometry at line 360 without a NULL check; this is an allocation-failure-only NULL with no in-fragment dereference, so it is a hardening concern, not a confirmed NULL-deref finding.
Null arg1n reaching the write/print/list branches depends on an unshown caller argument contract; a NULL produced only outside the fragment is not credited as a finding.
InterpretImageProperties receives the possibly-NULL _images at lines 35/42/278/291/317/337; its internal NULL handling is in an unshown callee and was not demoted or credited.
Safety of the read loop rests on the standard ExpandFilenames success contract (heap expanded list); an implementation that left argv at the stack address &arg1 is not assumed.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a confirmable in-fragment failure set is protected. The dereference JFS_IP(ipimap)->i_imap (line 17) is guarded by the `ipimap &&` NULL check, which survives the BREAK test (same value, no intervening write, NULL excluded on every path to the deref). verdict.summary: mkiss_close() frees ax->rbuff/ax->xbuff and free_netdev(ax->dev) after a wait that only covers refcount holders, while netif_stop_queue() is executed after that wait; a concurrent transmit can still be running and referencing the freed buffers/netdev, enabling a race-condition use-after-free.

evidence.reason: free_netdev(ax->dev) frees the net_device (and, since ax is netdev_priv(dev), ax itself) while the only synchronization shown, wait_for_completion on ax->refcnt (lines 17-18), covers refcount holders only; netif_stop_queue at line 23 executes after the wait and only stops new submissions without draining an in-flight transmit, so a transmit that began during the active-queue wait still reaches the freed object -> use-after-free (CWE-416), enabled by the race (CWE-362); the absent one-statement fix is executing netif_stop_queue(ax->dev) before refcount_dec_and_test at line 17 and synchronizing with the transmit path before these frees.

assumptions: ax is allocated as netdev_priv(dev), so free_netdev(ax->dev) at line 33 releases ax itself (fragment line 33 concedes no use after it, consistent with that layout).
The transmit path described in the comments (lines 20-21: a new transmit can scribble on our buffers) is the concurrent consumer of ax->rbuff/ax->xbuff/ax->dev and is not gated by ax->refcnt.
limitations: The failing transmit path is not shown in the fragment; the witness depends on a concurrent softirq transmit interleaving across the wait, which is a fragile-boundary race (confidence capped below 0.8).

If a given kernel's unregister_netdev() synchronously drains in-flight transmits before returning and none can restart, the window narrows to between the wait (line 18) and the frees (lines 28-33); the ordering flaw remains but the demonstrable corruption depends on the unshown stack behavior.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected: the NULL outcome of _g_path_get_relative_basename_safe is excluded by the line 10 base_name != NULL guard before g_file_get_child consumes it, and the extraction path is fail-closed via perform_extraction = FALSE on both the NULL-basename (lines 24-25) and NULL-file_list (lines 28-29) cases. base_name from _g_path_get_relative_basename_safe is not freed in the shown code (line 9 → line 11 use), which is a memory leak rather than a memory-safety or injection flaw in scope.

verdict.summary: In the pseudo-class path, colormap_index is allocated with MagickMax(image->colors+1, MaxMap) (exactly MaxMap elements when colors+1 <= MaxMap) yet the pixel-remap loop indexes it by ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(...)), whose maximum value is MaxMap, producing a one-past-the-end heap read.

evidence.reason: The remap loop reads colormap_index[ScaleQuantumToMap(GetPixelIndex(image,q))]; ScaleQuantumToMap's standard maximum is MaxMap, but the PseudoClass allocation at lines 26-27 is MagickMax(image->colors+1, MaxMap), holding only MaxMap elements (indices 0..MaxMap-1) whenever image->colors+1 <= MaxMap. In an 8-bit build a palette pixel with quantum index 255 maps to MaxMap=65535, so colormap_index[65535] reads one ssize_t past the 65535-element allocation (CWE-125). The guards at lines 31, 138/141, and 146 constrain allocation success and loop counters x/y only; none constrains the scaled index. The absent fix is a one-element-larger allocation (MaxMap+1) or a clamp of the ScaleQuantumToMap result.

assumptions: Standard ImageMagick constants apply: MaxMap = 65535, MaxColormapSize = MaxMap+1 = 65536.
ScaleQuantumToMap returns values in 0..MaxMap, reaching MaxMap at QuantumRange.

The witness requires an 8-bit (Q8) build where QuantumRange = 255 and a PseudoClass palette with >= 256 entries containing a pixel with stored index 255; such images are supplied by ordinary decoders (e.g., full 8-bit palette PNG/GIF).
limitations: In Q16/Q32 builds the S4 overflow does not manifest: stored indices are capped at colors-1, so ScaleQuantumToMap(colors-1) stays below MaxMap whenever the capacity drops to MaxMap.

The colors == 0 degenerate case at line 111 (colormap[0]=image->colormap[0] after a 0-size allocation) was not confirmed: it depends on malloc(0) returning non-NULL and on a PseudoClass image with an empty colormap, neither of which is demonstrable from the fragment alone.

The first-loop colormap writes (lines 82-87) were examined and rejected: the distinct-intensity count is bounded by the ScaleQuantumToMap domain (0..MaxMap), i.e. at most MaxColormapSize distinct entries, matching the AcquireImageColormap capacity at line 38.
Callers are assumed to pass an otherwise device-consistent Image; only the storage_class/colors combination needed for the witness is required.

verdict.summary: Every packet-derived read in bgp_capability_msg_parse is bounded before use: line 18 guarantees the 3-byte header fits, line 42 requires hdr->length >= sizeof(struct capability_mp_data), and line 51 requires pnt + hdr->length + 3 <= end, so the 4-byte memcpy at line 59 reads only inside [pnt, end); AFI/SAFI array indices are gated by the bgp_map_afi_safi_iana2int success check at lines 73-82. All dangerous operations resolve PRESENT.

The three guards execute on every reaching path with no intervening modification of pnt or hdr->length, so the operation resolves PRESENT.

afi and safi are produced only by bgp_map_afi_safi_iana2int (lines 73-74) on its zero/success return; the fragment continues on any nonzero return, so only internally valid AFI/SAFI values reach the peer->afc_recv/afc/afc_nego arrays. The indexed writes resolve PRESENT via the mapping-success gate.

assumptions: bgp_size_t length together with the buffer starting at pnt denotes at least length bytes of destination data (caller contract, not verifiable inside the fragment).
sizeof(struct capability_mp_data) is a small fixed constant and is exactly the size passed to memcpy at line 59.
bgp_map_afi_safi_iana2int returns nonzero for unknown IANA AFI/SAFI and sets the internal afi/safi outputs only on success.
limitations: A shortfall of the underlying allocation behind pnt relative to length would be a caller-side contract violation undetectable within this function.
bgp_map_afi_safi_iana2int's body is unshown; its success-gating semantics are inferred from the call site and the explicit continue on nonzero at lines 73-82.
All logging calls use literal format strings, so no format-string sink was inventoried.

verdict.summary: Every memory-safety sink in ins_bs (the two `*(ml_get_cursor() - 1)` reads, the `ptr[len - 1]` read/write, and the post-decrement `ml_get`/`ml_get_buf` line lookups) is preceded by an explicit guard whose admitted set excludes the failing value; no dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: The decoder loop dereferences one byte before the current line and fails at col == 0, but the same while condition (line 247) re-checks `curwin->w_cursor.col > 0` before every iteration's dereference, admitting only col >= 1 so index col-1 >= 0; the guard is identity-correct (same value, adjacent in the same && chain), boundary-exact (excludes only col == 0), and reaches every dereference, so this sink resolves PRESENT and no CWE-125 witness survives the BLOCK test.

The softtabstop branch dereferences `ml_get_cursor() - 1`, which fails at col == 0, but the guard `curwin->w_cursor.col > 0` on line 209 is evaluated left-to-right in the same short-circuit && chain before this read and admits only col >= 1; the guard's excluded set exactly covers the failure set, so the sink is PRESENT (no CWE-125/787).

`ptr[len - 1]` (read, and the write at line 128) fails at len == 0, but the guard `len > 0` in the same statement excludes len == 0 and admits len >= 1, giving index len-1 in [0, STRLEN-1]; identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach all pass, so the sink is PRESENT.

assumptions: Analysis uses the default build configuration without FEAT_RIGHTLEFT/FEAT_VARTABS, so the `#ifdef`-guard lines are compiled out.

colnr_T is unsigned, so `col == 0` is the only derivable failing value for the `ml_get_cursor() - 1` derefs; no shown statement can raise col above the line length (cursor mutations are editor-internal callees).
get_sw_value's standard semantics map an 'sw' of 0 to the tabstop, so the `want_vcol / ts` divisions cannot divide by zero on any reaching path.
limitations: In a FEAT_RIGHTLEFT build with revins_on TRUE the top guard's `!revins_on &&` disables the lnum == 1 && col == 0 early return, which could allow `--Insstart.lnum` to 0 before `ml_get`; reachability of that configuration (revins_on and Insstart.lnum == 1) is not derivable from the fragment, so it is recorded as a limitation, not a verified finding.
Callee bodies (ml_get, ins_bs_one, utfc_ptr2char, do_join) are unshown; they were analyzed only through their call-site arguments and standard semantics.
inserted_space_p NULL dereference was demoted: the fragment contains no NULL-producing statement for that parameter, and a NULL would have to be supplied by an unshown caller.

verdict.summary: Archive entry pathnames (and hardlink targets), which are attacker-controlled archive metadata, are joined verbatim into a GFile under extract_data->destination with no visible containment check, so extraction can create, replace, or hard-link files outside the destination directory.

evidence.snippet: ostream = (GOutputStream *) g_file_replace (file, NULL, FALSE, G_FILE_CREATE_REPLACE_DESTINATION, cancellable, &load_data->error);
evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled pathname (line 37) containing '..' survives the extraction-request check (line 38) and the leading-slash join (line 43), and _g_path_get_relative_basename (line 44, body unshown) cannot be credited with sanitization, so g_file_get_child yields a GFile outside extract_data->destination which g_file_replace opens with replace-destination, writing attacker-chosen bytes to an arbitrary path (CWE-22); the absent fix is a containment check such as g_file_has_prefix (file, extract_data->destination) or rejection of '..' components before line 44.

Attacker-controlled linkname (line 126) such as ../../etc/passwd is joined at line 134 and passed through the same unguarded g_file_get_child (line 135), so oldname (line 136) resolves outside the destination and link() creates a hard link to an arbitrary existing file (CWE-22); the NULL checks at line 139 protect only the arguments, not the path traversal, and no containment fix is present.

assumptions: pathname and linkname are attacker-controlled archive metadata read via archive_read_next_header (line 22) from an archive opened at line 21.
extract_data_get_extraction_requested (line 38) is a file-selection test that admits every pathname under default extract-all, so it does not constrain '..' components.
junk_paths is an extractor option whose FALSE default preserves path components; _g_path_get_relative_basename has unshown body and is not credited with any sanitization.
limitations: g_object_unref (parent) at line 117 with a possible NULL parent emits a GLib critical, not a crash, so it is not treated as a finding.
Writes that would flow through a previously extracted symlink target are not demonstrable within this fragment.
The exact containment-fix statement of the unshown counterpart is unknown and not needed for the verdict.

verdict.summary: Heap buffer overflow in Image::printIFDStructure: file-supplied count (line 37, uint32_t, no cap) is multiplied in 32-bit arithmetic at line 66, so size*count+pad+20 wraps to a tiny buffer capacity while io.read at line 73 writes count*size (up to 4GB) bytes into it.

evidence.reason: count is a file-supplied uint32_t with residual range 0..2^32-1 (only typeValid at line 41 gates it). For ASCII type (size=1, pad=1, lines 58-63, 57), count=0xFFFFFFFF makes the line-66 allocation (0xFFFFFFFF+21) mod 2^32 = 20 bytes while count*size wraps to 0xFFFFFFFF > 4, admitted by bOffsetIsPointer at line 68; io.read then writes up to 4GB into the ~20-byte heap buffer. The absent fix is a count cap or size_t promotion of size*count; the 32-bit wrap at line 66 (CWE-190) corrupts the capacity, yielding the CWE-787 heap buffer overflow at this copy sink.

Independent sink in the isPrintXMP branch: buf.pData_[count]=0 indexes with the raw file-supplied count (line 37). With BYTE type (size=1, pad=0) and count near 2^32, the line-66 capacity (count+20) mod 2^32 wraps to <= 20, so the write at index 0xFFFFFFFF is far out of bounds — the same CWE-190 wrap creating a CWE-787 heap buffer overflow.

assumptions: DataBuf buf(n) allocates a heap buffer of exactly n bytes as its capacity (line 66).
Both count and size are uint32_t, so size*count and size*count+pad+20 are evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wrap modulo 2^32 before any widening.
io.read(buf, n) writes up to n bytes from the file into buf per BasicIo standard semantics; the attacker controls the file contents/size.
typeValid admits ASCII (2) and BYTE (1) types, making size=1/pad=1 and size=1/pad=0 reachable.
limitations: The commented-out offset check at line 65 is not an executed protective statement; io.seek with an arbitrary offset could be a separate robustness concern but is not the decisive finding.
Resource-exhaustion sinks (new byte[count] at lines 121 and 137, up to 4GB) are a DoS candidate not needed for the verdict.
Ignored io.read/io.seek return statuses and partial reads are secondary status-handling concerns; the confirmed failure is the oversized copy at line 73.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation with a provable failure set is guarded: the retry path checks the io_setup_async_rw() status (lines 61-62) before dereferencing req->async_data, the iovec is NULLed after async capture (line 64) and kfree is NULL-guarded (lines 94-95), and the retry loop's condition (line 89) plus the pre-loop fall-through constraint keep io_size -= ret from underflowing. No unconstrained value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Return-status guard for io_setup_async_rw() (line 60): on every nonzero return the function exits before the req->async_data dereferences at lines 65/67/71 (`rw = req->async_data`, `iter = &rw->iter`, `rw->bytes_done += ret`), and on the zero return the helper's success contract supplies non-NULL async_data with no shown statement modifying it between check and use. BREAK passed: identity (same result gates the use), boundary (all failure values excluded), degenerate (ret2==0 is success, not failure), reach (check precedes every dereference on every reaching path).

evidence.reason: 1-bit index write into the per-row index cache of image->columns entries: the guard at line 467 (`for (x=0; x < ((ssize_t) image->columns-7); x+=8)`) admits x <= columns-8, so x+bit <= columns-1; the remainder path at 479 (`bit < (image->columns % 8)`) writes at most x+bit <= columns-1 (for columns=8k+r, max 8k+r-1). Degenerate columns=1..7 skip the main loop and the remainder writes indexes[0..columns-1]. Width>=1 is enforced on every path by the throw at 168-169, so no admitted index reaches the arrays' capacity; BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, and reach.

4-bit index write: the guard at line 511 (`for (x=0; x < ((ssize_t) image->columns-1); x+=2)`) admits x <= columns-2, so indexes+x+1 <= columns-1; the odd-column remainder (521-527) writes indexes[x++] with x <= columns-1 at that point, and the post-check at 528 does not index. Columns are forced >= 1 by 168-169 before this loop, so the largest write is exactly the last cache slot; no out-of-range value is admitted (BREAK: identity, boundary columns-1 < capacity, reach).

Colormap write loop is bounded by line 271 (`for (i=0; i < (ssize_t) image->colors; i++)`), so i <= colors-1; colors <= 256 because 178-180 caps number_colors at 1U<<bpp (bpp in {1,4,8}) and 218-219 replaces 0 with 1<<bpp; AcquireImageColormap (247) allocates exactly image->colors entries and its MagickFalse result throws. The companion *p++ reads consume at most 4*colors bytes, matching the 249-250 allocation (4*sizeof(*bmp_colormap) per color), and the blob fill is verified by the count equality check at 263-269 before the loop; all four BREAK tests pass.

Pixel-buffer fill reads length = bytes_per_line*image->rows (293) into the allocation of image->rows * MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) (299-300), so capacity >= length on every path; the per-case bytes_per_line reassignments used later (550, 596, 656, 696) are each <= the line-292 value, so row consumption stays within the same allocation. Allocation failure throws at 301-302 and a short read throws at 308-313 (count != (ssize_t) length), so neither an over-read of the file nor a write past the buffer is admitted.

32-bit pixel reads consume 4 bytes per pixel with bytes_per_line = 4*image->columns (696) per row against an allocation of rows*MagickMax(bpl_pre, columns+256) (299-300) where bpl_pre for 32-bit is also 4*columns (292); maximum byte offset reached is rows*4*columns-1, inside the capacity. Rows >= 1 is guaranteed by the height guard at 170-171, y runs rows-1..0 (697), and the allocation NULL check at 301-302 throws before p is derived; the BREAK boundary/identity/reach tests all pass.

assumptions: 64-bit size_t/ssize_t: the 32-bit signed width/height fields (153-154), validated bits_per_pixel (174-177), and height magnitude (206) keep bytes_per_line*rows <= ~2^64-2^33 (292-293), so no size wrap occurs.

GetVirtualMemoryBlob is non-NULL after a successful, checked AcquireVirtualMemory; ReadBlobLSB* return the documented 16/32-bit little-endian fields.
limitations: DecodeImage (line 325) is an unshown callee; it is analyzed only through its call (buffer rows*(columns+256) on the RLE path; expected = columns*rows; status checked at 327-332), so deeper callee behavior beyond that contract is out of scope.

The bitfield shift loops (391-451) can evaluate `mask << 32` (C undefined behavior) when a mask's highest bit sits at bit 0, but this has no memory-access sink in the fragment and is not counted as a vulnerability.

The ASCII read branch (lines 119-147) is reachable with an attacker-supplied .mesh/.sol file whose contents are entry-point input.

verdict.summary: Attacker-controlled `maxrlvls` (parsed from `optstr` via `atoi` at line 166) bounds the loop at lines 282-285 with no upper-cap check, so writes to the fixed-size arrays `tccp->prcwidthexpns[rlvlno]` and `tccp->prcheightexpns[rlvlno]` can index past the array elements, causing an out-of-bounds write. The loop condition `rlvlno < tccp->maxrlvls` (line 282) admits counts as large as INT_MAX (e.g., `maxrlvls=4096`), and the only maxrlvls check, `if (cp->tccp.maxrlvls < 1)` (line 376), excludes only values below 1 and executes after the writes, so it neither blocks the path nor bounds the count. The absent one-statement fix is an upper-bound check (e.g., `maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS -> error`) before line 282. The resulting writes past the fixed-size `prcwidthexpns` array's element capacity constitute an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787).

Same unbounded `maxrlvls`-controlled loop (line 282) writes index `rlvlno` into the fixed-size array `prcheightexpns`; no guard anywhere in the fragment admits only in-range counts, and the minimum-only check at line 376 runs after the write, so attacker count `maxrlvls >= capacity+1` overflows this array too (CWE-787).

assumptions: `tccp->prcwidthexpns` and `tccp->prcheightexpns` are fixed-size member arrays of `jpc_enc_tccp_t` with a finite element count (the shown code never increases their capacity), so an unbounded write count necessarily exceeds that count.
limitations: The exact array capacity (e.g., `JPC_MAXRLVLS` from the struct definition) is not declared or computed inside the shown fragment, so the OOB claim rests on the unbounded attacker-controlled write count rather than a quoted capacity line.

The `maxrlvls >= 65536` case can also make the `uint_fast16_t rlvlno` counter wrap or run indefinitely (CWE-835), but this depends on the platform width of `uint_fast16_t` and is not the decisive mechanism.

Unsigned-wrapping arithmetic (`hsteplcm *=`, `imgareatlx *=`, `refgrdwidth +`, `numhtiles * numvtiles`) was demoted to a limitation because no in-fragment memory sink consumes the wrapped results; the tile-grid-offset validation at lines 303-306 and nonzero tile checks at lines 291-300 protect the divisions shown here.

verdict.summary: ismt_access consumes the unvalidated u8 block length data->block[0] (domain 0..255) on the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA write path: with block[0]==255, `dma_size = data->block[0] + 1` (line 119) wraps the u8 to 0, and `dma_size - 1` underflows to SIZE_MAX at the memcpy at line 124, producing an enormous out-of-bounds copy; the length clamp present for I2C_SMBUS_I2C_BLOCK_DATA (lines 153-154) is absent on this path and on the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL path (line 145).

evidence.reason: On the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA write path, data->block[0] keeps its full u8 residual range 0..255 (no shown check bounds it); for block[0]==255, `dma_size = data->block[0] + 1` at line 119 wraps (int)256 into u8 0, and `dma_size - 1` promotes 0 to int -1, converted to size_t as SIZE_MAX, so this memcpy copies ~2^64 bytes from &data->block[1] to &dma_buffer[1], a massive out-of-bounds read/write. The clamp `if (data->block[0] > I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX) data->block[0] = I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX;` (lines 153-154) is the exact fix form and is absent before this case's length computation, so the u8 wraparound (CWE-190) at line 119 is not excluded on this path.

On the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL path, data->block[0] is unconstrained at u8 domain 0..255 and is passed directly as the memcpy length; block[0]==255 yields a 255-byte copy from &data->block[1] to &dma_buffer[1], and no validation or clamp (the form shown at lines 153-154) precedes it, leaving an oversized copy from the full residual range — same missing-validation family as the primary finding; the missing one-statement fix is the max-length clamp before this case.

assumptions: data->block[0] is a u8 field with declared domain 0..255, and no shown statement constrains it on the I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_DATA or I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_PROC_CALL paths.

I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX is the standard SMBus block maximum (32); the clamp at lines 153-154 admits data->block[0] in [1, I2C_SMBUS_BLOCK_MAX], which prevents the u8 wraparound on the I2C_BLOCK_DATA path.

Standard C semantics: u8 255 + 1 evaluates as int 256 and truncates to 0 when assigned to u8 dma_size; `dma_size - 1` with dma_size==0 evaluates as int -1 and converts to SIZE_MAX at memcpy's size_t parameter.
limitations: Capacities of priv->buffer (via PTR_ALIGN at line 13) and of the union block array are not declared in the fragment, so the downstream OOB may not be capacity-confirmed as CWE-787/CWE-125; the confirmed mechanism is the in-fragment u8 wraparound producing the SIZE_MAX copy size (CWE-190).
Any pre-validation of block[0] performed by the i2c core or i2c-dev caller is not visible in the fragment and was not assumed in either direction.

verdict.summary: In cp_create, the resolution-level write loop indexes tccp->prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns with rlvlno under the trip bound tccp->maxrlvls, which is set from an unvalidated atoi() of attacker-supplied option text. The only early guard (line 167) rejects maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS and admits every negative value; the maxrlvls < 1 check runs after the loop. A negative maxrlvls promotes to a huge unsigned bound in the mixed-sign comparison at line 286, driving out-of-bounds heap writes.

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled tccp->maxrlvls (atoi of the option value, line 166) reaches the loop bound at line 286 with residual range [INT_MIN, JPC_MAXRLVLS]: guard 167 excludes only maxrlvls > JPC_MAXRLVLS, and guard 380 (maxrlvls < 1) is evaluated after the loop, so it cannot protect this write (evaluated-after-use drift). A negative value such as -1 promotes, in rlvlno < tccp->maxrlvls (uint_fast16_t vs int), to a huge unsigned trip count, so rlvlno indexes prcwidthexpns far beyond its finite per-level capacity anchored only by JPC_MAXRLVLS; heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) via signed-to-unsigned bound conversion (CWE-195). Absent fix: a maxrlvls < 1 (or >= 1) rejection immediately before line 286.

Same mechanism as line 287: the identical loop bound admits negative maxrlvls through guard 167, the negative value converts to a huge unsigned bound in the comparison at line 286, and rlvlno writes past the end of prcheightexpns — heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) triggered by the unchecked signed bound from line 166, with the needed lower-bound check missing before the loop.

assumptions: uint_fast16_t is assumed to have rank >= int (e.g., unsigned long on glibc LP64), so the signed negative maxrlvls converts to a huge unsigned trip count in the comparison at line 286; on platforms where uint_fast16_t is 16-bit the loop is skipped and the late check at line 380 would catch the value.

prcwidthexpns and prcheightexpns are finite per-resolution-level arrays whose capacity is tied to JPC_MAXRLVLS, the only bound enforced on maxrlvls (guard at line 167); the struct capacity itself is not declared in the shown fragment.
limitations: The exact element count of prcwidthexpns/prcheightexpns is not shown (struct definition out of scope); the finding rests on the unbounded trip count exceeding any finite array.
jpc_atoaf failure leaves ilyrrates/numilyrrates potentially inconsistent, but the callee's partial-state contract is unshown, so that status-handling candidate is demoted.
Unsigned-wrap arithmetic on imgareatlx/refgrdwidth/numtiles is stored and consumed only by code outside the fragment; no dangerous in-fragment consumer was demonstrated.
Potential NULL dereference of jas_taginfo_nonull(jas_taginfos_lookup(...))->id has no in-fragment NULL producer and is not a finding.

verdict.summary: The file-deletion operation in drop_table is gated only by a debug-only DBUG_ASSERT; in release builds a non-temporary table's files reach maria_delete_table_files unconstrained, without the required runtime authorization check.

evidence.reason: The file-deletion sink at line 5 executes unconditionally: the only protective statement, the temporary-table invariant at line 3 (DBUG_ASSERT(!file || file->s->temporary);), is an assert-class check compiled out in normal builds and never constrains the delete. `name` and `file` are unconstrained at this point, so a drop_table call with a non-NULL, non-temporary file — the exact state the assert excludes — reaches the sink unblocked and deletes live table files. The absent one-statement fix is a runtime guard such as `if (file && !file->s->temporary) return;` (or input validation of `name`) before the call; a file-destruction operation reached without the required authorization check is CWE-863.

assumptions: Normal/release builds compile out DBUG_ASSERT, so line 3 performs no check at runtime.
Line 3 encodes the intended invariant that drop_table must only destroy files for temporary tables.
limitations: Path traversal or arbitrary-file deletion via a crafted `name` is not confirmed because `name` has no shown call site (internal-helper parameter, unconstrained-domain-only).
A NULL `name` or NULL `file->s` dereference inside maria_delete_table_files is not confirmed because no in-fragment producer supplies NULL.
The discarded ha_close() return status (line 4) has no visible security consumer, so it is not treated as an independent finding.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation is protected: output writes are bounded by the len<=occ gate (line 143) and the codep&&tp>op loop bound (line 170); table pointers are bounded by the free_entp and oldcodep in-table checks (lines 106-119); the post-CLEAR code is bounded to 0..255 (line 90); the main-path code index (line 101) is masked by nbitsmask with nbits capped at BITS_MAX (lines 124-128, 125-126), which the shown table sizing (lines 107/115, 128) keeps inside the table. No admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Protective gate for all string-output copies: it excludes every stream-derived string length len=codep->length that exceeds the remaining output count occ (the same value consumed at line 162), routing those cases to the restart logic, so every write at lines 157-159 and 169 stays within [op0, op0+occ0-1]; passes the BREAK test on identity (no modification between check and use), boundary (len <= occ <= occ0), degenerate (occ >= 1 via the outer while), and reach.

Second protective bound on the reversal-copy do-while: iteration stops when the chain ends (codep NULL) or when tp reaches op, and combined with line 143 (len <= occ) the highest written address is op+len-1, inside the occ0-byte buffer; BREAK test passes on all four axes.

Excludes an out-of-table free_entp before the table write at line 113, so the code-table entry creation cannot write past the CSIZE-entry table; the companion check at lines 114-119 excludes an out-of-table or NULL oldcodep before the derefs at lines 120-121.

Bounds the code admitted after a CODE_CLEAR sequence to [0, CODE_CLEAR] (literals) before `*op++ = (char)code` and `oldcodep = sp->dec_codetab + code` at lines 96-98, closing the clear-path table index; EOI is already handled at line 88.

assumptions: op0/occ0 is the output buffer of capacity occ0; occ starts equal to occ0 and only decreases in the shown code.
NextCode (standard libtiff macro semantics, body unshown) masks the stream code with nbitsmask, so code is bounded by MAXCODE(nbits).

The shown nbits cap (lines 125-126) and table sizing (free_entp < CSIZE at line 107, maxcodep = dec_codetab + nbitsmask at line 128) are consistent only if MAXCODE(BITS_MAX) < CSIZE, which keeps line 101's index inside the table.
The restart invariant dec_restart < codep->length is preserved in-fragment (dec_restart set to occ only when codep->length > occ at lines 143/154; incremented at line 38 only while residue > occ).
limitations: The main path lacks an explicit `code >= CSIZE` guard before `codep = sp->dec_codetab + code` (line 101); under the shown masking/cap invariants it is vacuous, so no witness survives the BLOCK test, but it is noted as defense-in-depth absent.

Negative or zero occ0, or dec_restart >= codep->length, would drive the do-while loops at lines 46/58 into unbounded backward writes, but no shown producer can derive those states (caller contract and internal state maintain occ >= 1 and residue >= 1); demoted to unshown-caller/state concerns.
Initialization values of sp->dec_oldcodep and the exact CSIZE/BITS_MAX literals are not shown in the fragment; the guards at lines 106-119 and 90 cover NULL/out-of-range cases under the shown logic.
The `assert(occ >= len)` at line 171 and `assert(sp != NULL)` at line 15 are debug-only and were not credited as protective statements.

verdict.summary: The zip entry filename is used to build the extraction target and open a write stream without any rejection of '..' or absolute-path components, so a crafted archive can write files or create symlinks outside the target directory (zip-slip).

evidence.reason: Attacker-controlled entryPath (zei->entry.filename) is admitted by the line 11 non-empty check and the line 16 trailing-slash check, then concatenated into targetFile at line 14; a filename such as "../../escape.txt" or "/tmp/escape.txt" resolves outside targetDirectory, and this line 46 FileOutputStream opens it for writing (line 51 writes the entry contents), yielding arbitrary file creation/overwrite outside the extraction root. No shown guard rejects '..' or absolute paths and there is no containment check (e.g., isAChildOf) before the write; the absent one-statement fix is traversal validation on entryPath/targetFile. Mechanism: path traversal (zip-slip) → CWE-22.

On the isSymbolicLink path the same unvalidated targetFile escapes targetDirectory when entryPath contains '..' or is absolute, so the fragment creates a symlink at an attacker-chosen location outside the extraction root, with originalFilePath taken verbatim from the entry stream. This sink resolves ABSENT under the same missing traversal check → CWE-22.

assumptions: zei->entry.filename is populated from zip-archive data and is therefore attacker-controlled entry-point input.

File::getChildFile concatenates/builds the child path and does not reject '..' or absolute child paths; '..' resolution is performed at file open, so the escaped path is written outside targetDirectory.
On the non-Windows build, backslashes in entryPath are normalized to '/' but any '..' segments are preserved.
limitations: entries.getUnchecked(index) at line 3 is a potential OOB read, but index is a parameter with no shown call site or in-fragment producer of an out-of-range value (Phase 1 category c), so it is demoted.

File::createSymbolicLink(targetFile, originalFilePath, true) also permits arbitrary absolute symlink targets from entry data; no in-fragment write-through demonstrates a separate failure, so it is folded into the traversal finding.
No memory-safety failure is demonstrated for readEntireStreamAsString; the confirmed mechanism is CWE-22 traversal.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in composite_setup is protected by in-fragment guards: w_length is clamped to USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ (OS-desc path re-clamped to USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ), each memcpy/memset length is min()/min_t()-bounded (18, 6, and 1024 respectively), and all interface-array indexing is gated by intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES. No admitted value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement: on IN paths it assigns w_length = USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ for any w_length > USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ, excluding all values above the ep0 buffer constant, and on OUT paths it bypasses all sinks (goto done). Every later copy and reply length derived from w_length is therefore at most the buffer-size constant; BREAK test passes (identity: same w_length variable; boundary: 64 not exceeded; degenerate: w_length=0 yields safe 0-length copies; reach: every processing path passes through this block).

evidence.snippet:
value = min(w_length, (u16) sizeof cdev->desc);
			memcpy(req->buf, &cdev->desc, value);
evidence.reason: memcpy length is bounded by min(w_length, sizeof cdev->desc) (18 bytes) on line 69, executed immediately before the copy on the same value with no intervening modification; excluded set is value > 18, well below the ep0 buffer capacity, so the copy cannot overrun.

evidence.snippet:
value = min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len);
				memcpy(req->buf, config->descriptors[0], value);
evidence.reason: Copy length is bounded by min_t(int, w_length, otg_desc_len), where otg_desc_len is exactly sizeof(struct usb_otg20_descriptor) or sizeof(struct usb_otg_descriptor) (lines 117-123), i.e. at most 6 bytes; the copy-length side is fully constrained with no admitted failing value.

evidence.snippet:
w_length = min_t(u16, w_length, USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ);
			memset(buf, 0, w_length);
evidence.reason: memset length is capped by min_t(u16, w_length, USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ) on line 285, excluding any w_length above the named OS-descriptor buffer constant before the zeroing of buf on line 286; BREAK test: same value, no drift, admitted maximum matches the buffer constant exactly (1024 bytes into a 1024-byte buffer is in-bounds).

Interface-array indexing is gated by intf >= MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES, excluding every index >= capacity before the use at line 164; intf (line 8, w_index & 0xFF, range 0..255) is not modified between the check and the use, so the guard fully constrains the sink. Identical guards protect the uses at lines 193, 229, 252, and 360.

assumptions: USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ is the capacity of req->buf (cdev->req) and USB_COMP_EP0_OS_DESC_BUFSIZ is the capacity of cdev->os_desc_req->buf; these equal-size allocations are standard in this file but not visible in the fragment.
MAX_CONFIG_INTERFACES is the declared size of cdev->config->interface and os_desc_cfg->interface arrays, which is what the >= comparisons are written against.
limitations: OTG case (lines 108-126): list_first_entry(&cdev->configs, ...) never returns NULL, so the line 114 if (!config) is dead for the empty-list case and config->descriptors[0] could be an invalid pointer; demoted because 'configs list empty' and 'descriptors[0] NULL' depend on unshown producers/environment, failing the BLOCK test.

DEVICE OS-desc case (line 302) lacks the explicit if (value >= 0) present in the INTERFACE case before min_t; a negative fill_ext_compat return wraps large in u16 but min_t still yields w_length <= 1024 and buf was zeroed at line 286, so no OOB or disclosure occurs - a status-handling robustness concern only.

Bodies of get_string(), config_desc(), bos_desc(), fill_ext_compat(), fill_ext_prop(), and the f->*/c->setup callbacks are unshown; their internal writes are analyzed only through call-site arguments and shown min() clamps.
NULL producers for cdev (get_gadget_data), gadget->ep0, and cdev->os_desc_req are not visible in the fragment, so NULL-deref candidates there are out of scope.

verdict.summary: unlzw() pushes decoded LZW-string bytes onto de_stack via *--stackp (lines 136/142/145) with no bound check that stackp stays within the buffer; a crafted stream whose prefix chain approaches the dictionary size (bounded in-fragment only by maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits), up to ~2^BITS entries) writes below de_stack's start.

evidence.reason: The chain-expansion loop writes one byte per prefix-chain node with *--stackp and no check that stackp has not fallen below de_stack. code reaches this sink from input() at line 93 and from tab_prefixof(code) descent at line 143; because free_ent grows while (code = free_ent) < maxmaxcode at lines 174-178 with maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) at line 31 and maxbits <= BITS at line 33, a chain can reach ~2^BITS nodes, while the stack buffer has only its (standard) fixed capacity. Guards at 114-115 and 140 constrain code values, not the push count, and the clamp at lines 151/153 bounds only the later memcpy reads, so the loop can push past de_stack's start. The one-statement fix that would neutralize this — a bound check such as 'if (stackp < de_stack) gzip_error("corrupt input.");' before the push — is absent; the surviving witness is a crafted stream whose prefixes (including code == free_ent KwKwK expansions, lines 114-137) drive stackp below de_stack: out-of-bounds write, CWE-787.

The final push after the chain loop adds one more *--stackp write beyond the chain depth already emitted; it shares the identical unbounded-decrement mechanism and the identical absent stackp-bound fix, so the deepest structurally longest chain overflows de_stack by at least one byte (CWE-787).

assumptions: maxmaxcode = MAXCODE(maxbits) at line 31, combined with the line 33 maxbits <= BITS rejection, bounds the LZW dictionary size and hence the maximum prefix-chain depth at ~2^BITS.
de_stack is a fixed-size buffer (standard gzip/UNIX LZW semantics for de_stack) whose capacity is below the worst-case chain depth; its declaration is not shown in this fragment.
input(), tab_prefixof(), and tab_suffixof() are taken at their standard macro semantics (bit-masked code read; indexed table access).
limitations: de_stack's capacity is not declared or computed inside the fragment, so the overflow witness relies on the standard gzip de_stack size rather than an in-fragment capacity; this caps confidence below the top band.
The outbuf paths (lines 99, 151-171) were verified bounded and resolve PRESENT; write_buf() return values are discarded (lines 129/161/184) but that is not treated as a security-relevant finding.
The DEBUG-only block (lines 116-127) is not credited as protection because it is compiled out; the dict table writes (lines 175-176) are guarded by the line 174 maxmaxcode check and resolve PRESENT.

verdict.summary: sctp_setsockopt_auth_key bounds authkey->sca_keylength against the total option length optlen (line 24), but sctp_auth_set_key (line 35) consumes sca_keylength bytes from the flexible key array starting sizeof(struct sctp_authkey) bytes into the optlen-sized kmalloc buffer (line 15); optlen = sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)+1 with sca_keylength == optlen passes every shown guard and triggers a heap out-of-bounds read of up to sizeof(struct sctp_authkey) bytes.

evidence.reason: optlen is entry-point input with residual range [sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)+1, INT_MAX] after line 12, and authkey->sca_keylength is attacker-controlled after copy_from_user (line 19); the guard at line 24 rejects only sca_keylength > optlen, so its admitted set [0, optlen] intersects the copy's failure set (sca_keylength > optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)) at sca_keylength == optlen, which over-reads up to sizeof(struct sctp_authkey) bytes past the optlen-capacity buffer because the callee reads from sca_key at the header offset; the witness (optlen = sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)+1, sca_keylength = optlen, sca_assoc_id = 0 or a resolved association) passes the line 30 guard and survives the BLOCK test, so the absent one-statement fix is 'sca_keylength > optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey)', and the confirmed mechanism is a heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: struct sctp_authkey places the variable-length key sca_key immediately after the fixed header fields (sca_keylength, sca_hmac_id, sca_assoc_id), so key bytes start at offset sizeof(struct sctp_authkey) within the optlen-byte buffer allocated at line 15.

sctp_auth_set_key stores the supplied key by copying authkey->sca_keylength bytes from authkey->sca_key (standard call-site semantics; its body is not shown), and accepts both the endpoint mode (asoc == NULL with sca_assoc_id == 0) and association mode used by this caller.
limitations: The exact header size (u8 vs u16 keylength field) is not derivable from the fragment, but the header is at least 1 byte, so the over-read window (optlen - sizeof(struct sctp_authkey), optlen] is non-empty for every reachable optlen; with a u8 keylength the window is optlen in [header+1, 255].
The unbounded kmalloc size optlen (line 15) with its NULL check is treated as a resource-use concern, not a confirmed memory-safety finding here.
A NULL asoc passed to sctp_auth_set_key is not flagged because the fragment never dereferences asoc and the endpoint-key contract is visible; any callee-side dereference is outside the shown code.
An internal re-validation inside sctp_auth_set_key is not assumed because the shown fragment is the only configurable guard and callee internals are not shown.

verdict.summary: In the GLOB_TILDE user-name unescaping, an unbounded copy loop writes into 'newp' whose capacity is only 'end_name - dirname' (lines 470-474), so a pattern such as "~u\s/subdir/pat" with GLOB_TILDE and escaping enabled overruns the buffer by up to the length of 'dirname', an out-of-bounds write (heap or alloca).

evidence.reason: Unbounded unescape copy: entry-point 'pattern' reaches dirname="~u\s/subdir" (capacity at lines 470-474 is 'end_name - dirname' = 4) after the tilde checks at 315-319 and unescape selection at 454-463; the loop at 487 executes until the dirname NUL and writes one byte per source char, copying 11 bytes plus the final NUL into a 4-byte buffer, with no guard constraining the destination offset 'p' (the line 487 loop condition is source-side, a wrong-target drift), so the failing value is admitted by every guard on the path. The absent fix is bounding the copy at 'end_name' or sizing 'newp' for the full unescaped length. Primary CWE-787 heap/stack out-of-bounds write.

The terminating NUL write lands past the 'end_name - dirname' allocation for the same witness (e.g. dirname "~a\b/c" advances p to newp[4] with capacity 4); it is the final write of the same unconstrained unescape copy and lacks the same end_name bound, an independent one-past write of the same CWE-787 mechanism.

assumptions: Analysis is for the non-Windows configuration (the user-name unescape branch is inside #ifndef WINDOWS32, lines 448-583).
GLOB_TILDE is a bit within __GLOB_FLAGS, so the line 16 flag-mask check admits flags = GLOB_TILDE with GLOB_NOESCAPE clear.
pattern is an external entry-point argument; no shown constraint limits its length or content.
limitations: Pair identity (which one-statement fix the counterpart carries) is not used; the failing sink is demonstrated solely from the shown statements.

Other inventoried sinks are guarded and did not contribute to the verdict: gl_offs overflow check at 41, dirname copy at 259-268, brace onealt sizing at 91-144, home-dir concat at 416-432, user-dir construction at 549-566, and the 'newcount+2' realloc bounds.
assert(next != NULL) at 169 is compiled out in normal builds and is not credited as protective.

verdict.summary: ha_maria::drop_table discards the return status of ha_close() and of maria_delete_table_files(), so a failed/partially-completed close or deletion is silently ignored and the destructive file deletion at line 5 executes unconditionally; the missing return-status check is the absent fix.

evidence.reason: The destructive file deletion runs unconditionally even though the preceding ha_close() status (line 4) is discarded with (void), and its own error return is also discarded, so a close/drop failure is fail-open and unobservable; the absent fix is a return-status check (e.g., abort or propagate the error) placed before this deletion -- unchecked security-relevant status, CWE-754.

The int error status of ha_close() is explicitly cast to void and never checked, so the failure range of the close result is admitted and its security-relevant consequence (deleting the table files at line 5 despite a failed close) is not prevented; a return-status check on this value is absent -- unchecked exceptional condition, CWE-754.

assumptions: ha_close() and maria_delete_table_files() return int error statuses per standard handler semantics, which is why the code applies (void) casts.
limitations: NULL dereference of file->s at line 3 was considered and rejected: no shown statement can produce NULL for the file member, so there is no in-fragment witness.
Path traversal / arbitrary file deletion via name was considered and rejected: name has no shown call site and path construction occurs in an unshown callee (provenance class c).
The DBUG_ASSERT at line 3 is not credited as a protective statement because it is compiled out under NDEBUG.
The actual ha_close() failure is an exceptional path, not attacker-controlled, so confidence is capped at 0.6 rather than higher.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment is protected: the kvzalloc result is NULL-checked on all paths before dereference, the CQE-initialization loop is strictly bounded by the WQ entry count, the pas fill exactly fits the allocated inlen tail computed from the same npages, and the vector2eqn/create_cq results are checked before their outputs are used. No unconstrained value reaches an unprotected sink.

evidence.reason: Dereference of the kvzalloc result at line 33: the NULL check `if (!in)` at lines 34-37 executes on every path reaching this use and excludes NULL (blocking the NULL-deref/write candidate); the same `in` object is consumed with no intervening reassignment, so the guard-identity audit passes (class: none).

CQE write indexed by i: the loop guard `i < mlx5_cqwq_get_size(&conn->cq.wq)` at line 26 admits only i in [0, size-1] while the WQ created at lines 21-22 contains exactly `size` 64-byte entries, so the strict `<` bound fully protects the write (no off-by-one at i == size).

Frag-array fill: with standard semantics it writes exactly buf->npages 8-byte entries, and inlen at lines 31-32 = MLX5_ST_SZ_BYTES(create_cq_in) + 8*npages, so the allocated tail (pas offset <= ST_SZ_BYTES being the last field) is at least npages*8 bytes; the same npages value feeds both the allocation and the fill, giving an exact fit.

Use of eqn produced by mlx5_vector2eqn at line 39: the return-status check `if (err) goto err_cqwq;` at lines 40-41 excludes the failure state before eqn is consumed here and irqn at line 68, so the unchecked-result candidate is resolved PRESENT.

assumptions: mlx5_cqwq_create allocates the WQ with exactly mlx5_cqwq_get_size() 64-byte entries per the standard semantics of these helpers.
mlx5_fill_page_frag_array writes exactly buf->npages 8-byte entries per its standard semantics.
pas is the trailing field of create_cq_in at byte offset at most MLX5_ST_SZ_BYTES(create_cq_in) per the standard mlx5_ifc layout.
Mlx5_core_create_cq/vector2eqn/cqwq_create return negative errno on failure and fill their outputs only on success.
limitations: On the mlx5_vector2eqn error path (lines 40-41) the allocated `in` buffer is not freed before `goto err_cqwq` (only line 55 frees it): a real CWE-401-class memory leak, but it is outside this analysis's dangerous-operation classes (memory safety/injection/crypto/logic-status) and no attacker-driven resource exhaustion is demonstrable in-fragment, so it is recorded here rather than as a verdict input.
cq_size has no shown call site (provenance class c); roundup_pow_of_two(0) or a negative value has no in-fragment consequence at a sink, so it cannot support a finding.
conn->cq.wq_ctrl.db.db and fdev->conn_res.uar are assumed non-NULL because no statement in the fragment can make them NULL; any NULL supplied by an unshown caller is out of scope.
Callee bodies are unshown; only their standard semantics (noted above) were attributed to them.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations shown in GmfOpenMesh carry in-fragment protection: strcpy(msh->FilNam, FilNam) is preceded by the line-39 check (strlen(FilNam) + 7 >= GmfStrSiz) that admits only strings of length at most GmfStrSiz-8, so the copy writes at most GmfStrSiz-7 bytes; both fscanf "%100s" reads cap the token at 100 chars plus NUL inside the GmfStrSiz str buffer. The only dereferences lacking a guard (*PtrVer/*PtrDim) have no NULL producer inside the fragment and depend on an unshown caller, so they are recorded as limitations, not findings.

BREAK test passes on identity (same value, no intervening change), boundary (write < capacity), degenerate (empty name writes 1 byte), and reach (guard is unconditional on every path to line 42); no strcpy overflow witness survives the BLOCK test.
