PRESENT: same %100s width bound as line 127; at most 101 bytes written into str[GmfStrSiz] (GmfStrSiz = 256), and the loop condition plus the EOF longjmp (lines 141, 143) prevent any out-of-bounds or uninitialized read of str. BREAK boundary check: 101 <= GmfStrSiz, so no failing value is admitted.

assumptions: msh->FilNam has capacity GmfStrSiz, consistent with the boundary chosen by the in-fragment guard at line 39 (the libMeshb GmfMshSct declares char FilNam[GmfStrSiz]).
GmfStrSiz is 256 (libMeshb definition), so the %100s writes of at most 101 bytes fit within str[GmfStrSiz] with a large margin.
Caller contract: non-NULL FilNam and valid int* varargs (PtrVer/PtrDim) for GmfRead mode, and int varargs for GmfWrite mode.
limitations: The dereferences (*PtrVer) = msh->ver and (*PtrDim) = msh->dim at lines 152-153 are unguarded, but PtrVer/PtrDim come from va_arg with no NULL-producing statement inside the fragment; NULL supplied only by an unshown caller is out of scope per the reverse-protection rules.
A NULL FilNam would fault inside strlen at line 39, but no in-fragment producer can create it.

Bodies of ScaWrd, safe_fread, safe_fscanf, RecWrd, GmfSetKwd, GetPos, and ScaKwdTab are not shown; they are analyzed only via their names and shown call sites (safe/standard semantics) and are not the basis of the verdict.
The membership of the vulnerable/fixed pair was not inferred from code appearance; the verdict rests solely on the in-fragment protective statements.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations are protected by in-fragment guards: mdl_ticket is NULL-checked after open_table_get_mdl_lock() before its later dereference; share is NULL-checked after tdc_acquire_share(); the freshly allocated table and table_list->db.str are checked before use; the memcmp is gated by an exact length equality; and the open_tables list head is checked before dereference. No witness survives the BLOCK test at any sink.

evidence.reason: The only shown producer of a NULL mdl_ticket (open_table_get_mdl_lock returning success without a ticket) is neutralized: the `|| mdl_ticket == NULL` guard forces return TRUE before the ticket is later dereferenced at mdl_ticket->get_deadlock_weight() (line 343) and assigned to table->mdl_ticket (line 421); identity holds since mdl_ticket is not reassigned between check and use, and the guard executes on every path reaching those uses from the MDL-acquiring branch.

tdc_acquire_share (line 246) may return NULL (its result is the only producer in scope); this guard returns TRUE on NULL, and the retry_share loop re-executes it for each iteration, so every later dereference of share (share->is_view line 278, share->tdc line 318, share->crashed line 399) has a non-NULL operand.

The memcmp reads key_length bytes, but the exact operator `==` constrains key_length to equal table_cache_key.length, so the cached buffer is at least that long by contract and key holds exactly the length get_table_def_key returned (line 55); both operands are provably large enough, so the memory read has no failing value.

The fresh-table path's NULL producer (my_malloc, which returns NULL on OOM) is checked and branches to err_lock before table is dereferenced at table->mdl_ticket (421), table->init (424), table->vcol_fix_expr (438) and table->s->table_type (458); the cached and pre-locked paths use non-NULL tables selected by the best_table guard (line 113).

assumptions: open_table_get_mdl_lock() returns TRUE on failure and can leave the ticket NULL, which is exactly what the `|| mdl_ticket == NULL` guard (209-211) excludes.
get_table_def_key() returns the byte length of the key buffer/key string it produced; tdc_acquire_share() may return NULL unless re-checked.
The open_tables linked list is NULL-terminated, so the loop at lines 69-112 terminates.
limitations: table->file (dereferenced at lines 373 and 434, the latter assert-only) and share->tdc (line 318) are not proven non-NULL inside the fragment; they rest on unshown callee behavior, and no in-fragment statement can make them NULL, so they are demoted to limitations.

On the MYSQL_OPEN_HAS_MDL_LOCK path, table_list->mdl_request.ticket (line 224) has no shown NULL producer inside the fragment; a NULL there would require an out-of-scope caller violating the flag contract.
table_list->alias.str has no in-fragment NULL producer; NULL aliases would only arise from an unshown caller.
DBUG_ASSERT/DBUG_ASSERT statements are not credited as protective statements.

verdict.summary: ZipFile::uncompressEntry reads entries.getUnchecked(index) with no bounds check on the int parameter index; a negative or oversized index performs an out-of-bounds read and the resulting pointer is dereferenced at zei->entry.filename.

evidence.reason: Parameter `index` (int, full domain, no shown validation) flows unmodified to the unchecked accessor `entries.getUnchecked (index)` (standard callee semantics: raw `elements[index]` with no bounds check); the reverse protection scan over lines 1-3 finds no guard constraining `index`, so the degenerate witness `index = -1` — outside any container's valid range `[0, size)` regardless of the unshown size — is admitted and performs an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125), with the out-of-range pointer dereferenced at `zei->entry.filename`; the absent fix is a bounds check before line 3, e.g. `if (! isPositiveAndBelow (index, entries.size())) return Result::fail(...)`, or a checked accessor with a null fallback.

assumptions: `entries` is a finite container whose valid indices are `[0, size)` with non-negative size, per the standard semantics of the `getUnchecked` accessor name; the shown fragment contains no statement contradicting this.
`entries.getUnchecked` performs no bounds validation; its standard semantics are raw element access.
limitations: `index` has no shown call site, so its provenance is only the unconstrained parameter domain; a caller honoring the API contract would pass a valid index.
A NULL `zei` from array contents is not a finding because no NULL producer is visible in the fragment.
`createStreamForEntry (index)`'s body is unshown; only its NULL-return path is checked here.
Path traversal (line 12) and symlink-parent (line 30) candidates were demoted: both sinks carry shown protective checks that survive the BREAK test.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation whose failure set is demonstrable in the fragment carries a protective statement: the SplashBitmap allocation is guarded by the zero/repeat-size return (line 115) and the deterministic-size cap (line 81), and any allocation failure is excluded by the getDataPtr() null check (line 125) before bitmap is consumed at line 132.

evidence.snippet:
bitmap = new SplashBitmap(surface_width, surface_height, 1,
                            (paintType == 1) ? colorMode : splashModeMono8, true);
evidence.reason: The only shown memory-construction sink, `new SplashBitmap(surface_width, surface_height, ...)`, receives dimensions that every reaching path first constrains: line 115 (`if (surface_width == 0 || surface_height == 0 || repeatX * repeatY <= 4)`) excludes zero dimensions with the exact values later consumed (no intervening assignment to surface_width/height), and the else branch's line 81 cap (`(unsigned long) surface_width * surface_height > 0x800000L`) bounds the pixel product at 0x800000 before allocation. Any allocation failure is additionally converted to an early return by the line 125 `getDataPtr() == nullptr` check, so no admitted value reaches an unprotected allocation with a shown failure set.

This is the first consumption of the freshly allocated `bitmap`, and the fragment's own NULL producer (a failed SplashBitmap allocation) is fully excluded on every path by the unconditional `if (bitmap->getDataPtr() == nullptr) { ... return false; }` guard at lines 125-131, which checks the same object with no intervening modification; the reverse protection scan finds no path that reaches line 132 with null data, so no NULL dereference resolves ABSENT.

assumptions: PDF-derived inputs (bbox, mat, ptm, x0/y0/x1/y1, xStep/yStep, the CTM from state->getCTM()) are attacker-controlled, per the entry-point provenance in Phase 1.
The line 36 `std::isfinite` check ensures the CTM entries entering the matrix math are finite.
SplashBitmap allocation failure is observable via getDataPtr() == nullptr, which the fragment itself tests at line 125.
Splash::blitImage and Splash::drawImage are raster operations with internal clipping; their row/index math is not part of the shown fragment.
limitations: Double division by zero at line 48 (`/ ctm[0]` when ctm[0]==0 in the else arm), at lines 64-65 (when surface_width==0 or x1==x0), and at line 174 is IEEE-defined (inf/NaN), not a memory fault; a further chain to int-cast UB and unshown SplashBitmap internals is not demonstrable from the fragment alone.

repeatX/repeatY (x1-x0 / y1-y0) have no upper cap, so the tile loops at lines 187-193 can perform a very large number of clipped blits for a huge tiling region; this is a resource-exhaustion/DoS concern that terminates within the int range and does not violate any shown capacity, so it is demoted to a limitation.

Integer overflow in `result_width = tBitmap->getWidth() * imgData.repeatX` (line 166) feeds drawImage at line 196; the sink's internal handling is unshown, so no memory-safety failure is confirmable at the shown-code level.

verdict.summary: Every attacker-influenced size or index in ReadCINImage is constrained by a shown protective statement before use: the 4-byte magic buffer is consumed only after count==4 is confirmed, user_length is capped by GetBlobSize before allocation, image_offset is bounded below and the skip loop aborts on EOF, and columns*rows/8 is capped by blob size before SetImageExtent; the pixel row loop breaks on a NULL row or a partial read, so no unconstrained value reaches a dangerous operation.

evidence.reason: The 4-byte magick buffer (line 66) is consumed by LocaleNCompare at line 69 and by the endian test at lines 72-73 only after the short-circuit guard confirms count==4; a short read (count!=4) throws, so no uninitialized or partial buffer content reaches the compare/endian reads. Protective statement: count != 4 excluded set {0..3}, admitted {4} equals the exact read size.

user_length (32-bit, line 82) is capped to GetBlobSize(image) by the guard at line 333 before the allocation at line 335, and the allocation failure path is NULL-checked at line 337; the admitted set [0, blobSize] fully bounds the allocation and the subsequent ReadBlob at lines 339-340, so no unchecked file-derived size reaches an allocation or copy.

columns and rows (from 32-bit file fields at lines 345-346) are bounded by the guard before SetImageExtent at line 365 and the row loop at line 386; the 64-bit product of two <=2^32-1 operands cannot overflow, and the admitted set columns*rows/8 <= blobSize constrains the pixel cache and total raster reads proportionally to actual file data.

The row sink ImportQuantumPixels at lines 397-398 is reached only when QueueAuthenticPixels returned a row and after the full length-byte read succeeded; the NULL check (line 392) and the short-read check (line 395) break on every failure path, so a truncated blob or failed cache row can never feed an image conversion with insufficient data.

image_offset is constrained to [712, 2^32-1] before it is used as the skip-loop target (line 354); combined with the EOF break at lines 359-361 and the position re-check at lines 363-364, a truncated file or corruptibly small offset throws before any image-data processing, so the 32-bit offset cannot drive an unbounded or undersized read.

assumptions: cin.image.channel has at least 8 elements so indices 0..7 from the header loop at line 130 are in bounds; the 8-channel CIN layout is the only capacity consistent with the loop bound shown.
size_t/MagickSizeType is 64-bit, so columns*rows with both operands <= 2^32-1 (from ReadBlobLong) cannot overflow the guard at line 352.

GetBytesPerRow(columns,channels,depth,MagickTrue) computes rows of at most columns*channels bytes (depth<=255, and 8-bit depth yields columns*3 or columns*1), which never exceeds the 32-bit-quantum pixel buffer obtained via SetQuantumPad/GetQuantumPixels.
limitations: The quantum pixel buffer size, SetImageExtent, and ImportQuantumPixels bodies are not shown; their internal bounds are not quotable protective statements, so row-buffer sufficiency rests on the standard semantics analyzed at the call site rather than a verbatim in-fragment check.

Return counts for fixed-size header-field ReadBlob calls are discarded, but the destinations are fixed declared arrays and CopyMagickString is length-capped, so no unbounded write is derivable in-fragment.
The copy-paste in the chromaticity block (green primary written to red_primary.x, line 172) is a data-correctness defect, not a memory-safety or security decision, and is not counted.

Resource exhaustion by forcing allocations proportional to (up to 8x) file size is bounded by the shown blob-size checks and is not a memory-safety failure; memory-limit enforcement inside SetImageExtent is unshown.

verdict.summary: The shown bmexec_trans is protected: len is constrained to 1..size before any pointer/tp[-1] use (L11), every final-sweep read is guarded by the while condition d <= ep - tp (L72), memchr_kwset NULL results are checked (L16, L55), and tp is re-bounded after the memchr path (L58). The only reads without a verbatim local guard (mid-iteration and the L71 entry read) require delta-table entries exceeding the pattern length, which the fragment cannot produce and standard kwset construction excludes; that invariant is not shown, so it can neither be credited nor used to build a surviving witness.

evidence.reason: Protective bound check: it excludes len > size before L21 (tp = text + len), so every initial-region tp[-1] read (L31, and by induction the L28-loop position invariant) computes an index in [len-1, size-1], in-bounds. BREAK test passes: identity (same len, no intervening modification), boundary (len == size yields index size-1, the last valid byte), degenerate (len may not be 0 on this path because of L9), reach (executes before any read on every path).

Protective guard for the final-sweep read at L74 (d = d1[U((tp += d)[-1])]): admitted set is 0 <= d <= ep - tp, which forces the read index (tp + d) - 1 <= ep - 1 = size - 1. BREAK test passes: identity (d and tp are unchanged between the condition and the read), boundary (d == ep - tp reads byte size-1), degenerate (d == 0 reads tp-1 with tp >= text+2 from L21/L11), reach (evaluated before every body iteration, including the first).

Protective NULL-status check on memchr_kwset's return (L54): it excludes tp == NULL on every reaching path before tp++ (L57) and the subsequent L58/L71 use, preventing a NULL-based dereference in the deepest skip block. Combined with the ternary NULL check at L16 for the len == 1 branch, all memchr_kwset failure paths are closed.

assumptions: size is the exact byte length of the text buffer, so text + size is one-past-end and index size-1 is the last valid byte.
kwset->mind is non-negative; len == 0 is returned early at L9 and the len == 1 case is handled separately at L13-17, so the main path has 2 <= len <= size.
U(...) maps a char to an unsigned char (0..255), matching the table index domain, and memchr_kwset has standard memchr semantics (returns NULL when not found).
limitations: The Boyer-Moore delta invariant d1[c] <= len (produced by unshown kwset construction) is not visible in the fragment: the mid-iteration reads (L32/L36-37/L41-42/L46) and the L71 entry read before the while guard would be out-of-bounds only if a delta entry exceeded len. The required large-delta witness cannot be derived from the fragment alone and contradicts standard kwset construction, so the BLOCK test rejects it; it is recorded here rather than as a finding.
The length argument text + size - tp at L54 is positive only under that same delta invariant; an over-read there likewise lacks a derivable witness.
bm_delta2_search's body is unshown; only its call-site arguments and return convention (true = match found) are analyzed.
No verdict can be based on which member of a vulnerable/fixed pair this fragment resembles; the result rests solely on the verbatim guards above.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in open_table() is reached only behind a shown protective statement: the memcmp of key_length bytes is gated by the length-equality test (line 71); share is NULL-checked (line 248) before every dereference; mdl_ticket is NULL-checked (line 211) on the path where the in-fragment helper can produce it; the new TABLE allocation is NULL-checked (line 388); and the locked-tables walk (lines 69-112) performs no indexed access. The only unguarded ticket/string paths depend on caller-supplied non-NULL values, which is a limitation, not an in-fragment failure.

evidence.reason: The equality guard constrains the exact value fed to memcmp: key_length bytes are copied only when table->s->table_cache_key.length == key_length, so the table-side operand is read only within its declared length; identity holds (no write to key_length between 71 and 72), the boundary admits only copy length == buffer length, a degenerate 0-length key gives a zero-byte compare, and the test executes on the same path immediately before the sink. The key-side operand is produced by get_table_def_key with that same key_length, so no capacity shortfall is demonstrable.

Protective return/NULL check for mdl_ticket before its only dereference at line 348: a helper failure or a NULL ticket short-circuits to DBUG_RETURN(TRUE), so no NULL ticket producible on the in-fragment helper path reaches tdc_wait_for_old_version; identity holds (mdl_ticket is not reassigned between 211 and 348). The else-branch assignment at line 224 could only carry a NULL supplied by an unshown caller, which the NULL-deref class rule excludes as a limitation.

Excludes NULL share before every subsequent share dereference (279, 323, 404) and before tdc_release_share(share) at 472: tdc_acquire_share's result is re-checked after each retry_share iteration, and every goto err_lock target is reached only after this check, so NULL share is excluded on every reaching path with no intervening reassignment.

Excludes NULL table from my_malloc before the later dereferences on the new-table path (table->mdl_ticket= at 426, table->init at 429, table->next= at 431); a NULL table instead transfers to err_lock. Together with the if(table) branch at 375 and the best_table NULL check at 113, every path reaching table dereferences carries a non-NULL table.

assumptions: LEX_STRING str fields (table_cache_key, alias, db, table_name) are NUL-terminated and hold at least length bytes, so reading length bytes stays within the buffer.
get_table_def_key fills key with exactly key_length bytes (key-side operand of the memcmp).
open_table_get_mdl_lock sets *mdl_ticket on success, and tdc_acquire_share sets the out TABLE parameter.
thd->open_tables is a NULL-terminated linked list, so the loop at lines 69-112 terminates on NULL.
limitations: On the MYSQL_OPEN_HAS_MDL_LOCK path, mdl_ticket is taken from table_list->mdl_request.ticket (line 224) and dereferenced at line 348 without a NULL check; a NULL there would require an unshown caller, so it is not an in-fragment-producible witness for CWE-476.
table_list->table_name.str (line 346) and table_list->alias.str have no NULL checks; NULL values are only caller-supplied and not producible by the shown code.
table->file is only DBUG_ASSERTed (lines 377, 439) before use; a NULL file is not producible by shown code, and asserts do not count as protective statements.
The global-read-lock decision at line 188 depends on can_acquire_protection() semantics that are not shown, so its fail-open/fail-closed behavior cannot be evaluated from the fragment.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations whose failure sets are derivable from the shown code are protected by verbatim guards that survive the BREAK test (outbuf copy clamp at L154 with L152, first-code validation at L98-99, maxbits bound at L33-38, read status check at L72-74); residual OOB candidates on de_stack/tab_prefix/tab_suffix/inbuf depend on capacities not declared in the fragment and are demoted to limitations.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement for the outbuf copy sinks (L157 in the flush loop, L170 in the else branch bounded by L152): it caps the copy length so outpos+i never exceeds OUTBUFSIZ, keeping the write span within [0,OUTBUFSIZ); the BREAK test passes on identity (same i/outpos consumed by the memcpy), boundary (largest admitted i = OUTBUFSIZ-outpos gives last index OUTBUFSIZ-1), degenerate (i==0 no-op), and reach (executes on every path to L157).

The first decoded code is validated to 0..255 before being stored into oldcode at L100 on the only path that reaches that write (initial oldcode==-1, L43, never re-set), excluding every code >= 256 that could poison later prefix-table state; the guard constrains the same code value with no intervening modification, and outpos is provably 0 on that path, so no out-of-bounds write is derivable.

Bounds the entry-derived maxbits (after `maxbits &= BIT_MASK` at L30) to BITS and returns ERROR before MAXCODE(maxbits), n_bits, and bitmask are used by any table access or bit read, so the derived maxmaxcode and all free_ent-based indices stay within the shown BITS-limited domain; read status is separately checked at L72-74 (rsize == -1 -> read_error).

assumptions: OUTBUFSIZ/INBUFSIZ are genuine positive buffer-size constants, as the fragment's own guards (L152, L154, L160) and read call (L71) treat them.
read_buffer returns at most INBUFSIZ bytes, 0 at EOF, and -1 on error (standard name semantics, matching the L72-74 check).
gzip_error terminates the decode (fatal-error semantics), which is why paths through L133-135 are dead after it.
limitations: Capacities of de_stack, tab_prefix/tab_suffix, and inbuf are not declared in the fragment, so the *--stackp pushes (L137/L143/L146), tab writes (L177-178), and inbuf ops (L65/L71/L94) cannot be confirmed as overflows in either direction.
The outbuf[outpos++] write at L100 executes only once with outpos==0, so no OOB witness can be constructed even without treating OUTBUFSIZ as known.
code_int signedness is not shown; the init loop L52-54 is treated as terminating 256 iterations, and the infinite-loop reading (unsigned code != -1 never true) is not confirmable.
DEBUG-only block L117-128 and Tracev/WARN macros are compiled out or non-protective and were credited nowhere.

verdict.summary: All bitmap word accesses in hfsplus_block_allocate stay inside the kmap'd page: every curr read/write is gated by `while (curr < end)` with end capped at pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32, the requested run is capped by `len = min(size - start, len)` after `if (start >= size)`, and the page walk breaks on `if (offset >= size)`. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: Every word write (lines 91, 98) and the partial-word write at line 120 execute only while curr < end, and end is constructed at lines 23/25/61/63/108 to be at most pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 words, so all indexed accesses (curr <= pptr + 127) are inside the 128-word kmap'd page; BREAK test passes on identity (same curr/end at check and use), boundary (<), degenerate (offset/size extremes still in-page), and reach (all paths to the sinks pass through this gate or the equivalent initial-word construction at line 19).

Combined with `if (start >= size)` at line 71 (admitted set start < size, so size - start >= 1 in u32 and no wraparound), this caps the allocation run to the bits remaining in the bitmap, so the write loops (lines 87, 98, 120) can never set bits past size or run an unchecked number of iterations; the len == 0 degenerate case is also excluded at lines 11-12 and 82/85.

Guards the page-advance path: the next `read_mapping_page(mapping, offset / PAGE_CACHE_BITS, NULL)` at lines 57-58 executes only when offset < size, so the page index never advances past the bitmap region and the loop at 40-64 terminates; this bounds every subsequent page's curr/end within one kmap'd page.

assumptions: PAGE_CACHE_BITS is one page of bits, so PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 word pointers fit exactly within the kmap'd page (128 words for a 4K page); end is at most pptr + PAGE_CACHE_BITS/32 on every shown branch.
len is nonzero and < or = remaining bitmap bits after `if (!len) return size` (line 11) and `len = min(size - start, len)` (line 76) with start < size enforced at line 71.
limitations: kmap(page) at lines 18/59/106 is applied without checking read_mapping_page's error result; a failing read (I/O error or out-of-range index supplied by a caller violating the offset < size contract) would dereference an ERR_PTR, but no failure producer is shown inside the fragment and offset's unshown caller constrains resulting I/O behavior, so this is an environment/caller-contract dependent concern, not a demonstrated finding.
First page read at line 17 has no in-fragment bound against size; it is safe only under the unshown caller convention offset < size.
*max/free_blocks accounting (lines 123-124) is u32 arithmetic with no memory-safety consequence in the fragment; a wrong count would be a robustness/logic issue only.

verdict.summary: The signed-overflow accumulation 'min += minnext * mincount;' (line 1038) is protected by an unconditional pre-add guard (lines 1032-1036) that FAILs compilation whenever minnext*mincount would overflow SSize_t or min + that product would overflow, so no admitted value reaches the sink. All other dangerous operations either carry a protective statement (e.g., SvGROW sizing before repeatcpy) or lack any in-fragment declared capacity to breach, and are not confirmable findings.

evidence.reason: The sink 'min += minnext * mincount;' (line 1038) consumes entry-point-derived SSize_t values mincount/minnext with no shown upper bound, but the immediately preceding guard (lines 1032-1036) excludes exactly its failure set: if minnext > 0 and mincount >= SSize_t_MAX/minnext the product would overflow (FAIL), and otherwise min >= SSize_t_MAX - minnext*mincount excludes a sum overflow, with the guard evaluating the same unmodified values on every path before the add (Guard-Identity Audit passes; BREAK test passes on identity, boundary, degenerate minnext==0, and reach). The BLOCK test finds no surviving witness because any overflow-producing combination trips FAIL at line 1035, terminating compilation. This is a protective bound check, not a vulnerability; CWE-190/787 overflow corruption is neutralized.

assumptions: SSize_t is the signed size type such that SSize_t_MAX is its positive limit, so the guard's division and subtraction comparisons are meaningful arithmetic on the same types used by the sink.
minnext/mincount are treated as non-negative length/count magnitudes per their use as minimum pattern lengths and quantifier counts.
SV buffer management (SvGROW/sv_catpvn) guarantees that a pre-grown buffer of size (mincount*l)+1 safely holds the repeatcpy write ending at offset mincount*l.
limitations: Indices derived from GOSUB/OPEN node arguments, e.g. RExC_open_parens[paren] (lines 630-631), RExC_recurse[ARG2L(scan)] (line 629), and the study_chunk_recursed bitmap (lines 663, 678-684), have no capacity declared or computed inside the fragment; RExC_total_parens (line 61) appears only as a debug-block loop bound in code compiled out in normal builds, so no in-fragment capacity can be exceeded and these are demoted (CWE-787 not confirmable).

The delta accumulation at lines 1045-1046 and the pos_delta expression at lines 1267/1270-1271 have no shown in-fragment memory consumer or capacity on which a failing witness could land; on 64-bit SSize_t the operands stay bounded by the quantifier limits.
assert() statements (lines 120, 834, 903, 1182, 1201) are debug-only and were not credited as protective statements.
The positive-lookahead branch under PERL_ENABLE_POSITIVE_ASSERTION_STUDY (lines ~1135+) is guarded by assert(0) and is not part of the normal analyzed configuration.

verdict.summary: Every text-access operation is bounded in-fragment: len <= size at line 11, the skip-loop margin ep = text+size-11*len at line 28 caps the 10 delta1 advances so tp never exceeds text+size-len, the advance heuristic at line 51 plus the NULL check at line 55 gate the memchr fallback, and the final loop's reads are per-step gated by 'while (d <= ep - tp)' at line 70.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective bound for the final-loop reads: it admits only d <= size-(tp-text), so after 'tp += d' the read '(tp += d)[-1]' at line 72 indexes at most ep-1 = text+size-1, the largest valid index; d=0 is re-read in bounds and d>remaining exits before reading. Guard is on every path to line 72 with no intervening mutation (identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach all pass BREAK).

evidence.snippet: for (ep = text + size - 11 * len; tp <= ep; )
evidence.reason: Caps the unrolled skip loop: with delta1 values <= len (standard kwset/BMH semantics), the body makes at most 10 advances so tp <= ep+10*len = text+size-len, keeping every 'tp[-1]' read at lines 31-46 in bounds and making line 54's 'text + size - tp >= len >= 1', so the memchr length cannot underflow to a huge size_t.

NULL check on the memchr_kwset result placed before every use: it runs before 'tp++' at line 57 and before the bm_delta2_search call at line 61 on all reaching paths, so a no-match NULL result is returned from rather than dereferenced (blocks the NULL/wild-pointer-read witness).

Excludes len > size before 'tp = text + len' (line 21) and every initial offset read: since len==0 and len==1 were already returned at lines 10 and 16, proceeding has 2 <= len <= size, so 'tp[-1]' at line 69 indexes len-1 <= size-1, guaranteed in bounds.

assumptions: kwset->delta is a Boyer-Moore-Horspool delta1 table with values in [0, len] (0 for the rightmost pattern character, len for characters absent from the minimal word); this underpins the skip-loop margin at line 28.
kwset->target holds the len-byte minimal word, so sp = kwset->target + len is the required one-past-end pointer for bm_delta2_search.
bm_delta2_search operates within [*tpp, ep], returns true only on a verified match, and otherwise advances *tpp so the calling loops terminate.
int is 32-bit: if 12*len (line 26) or 11*len (line 28) overflows, the skip loop is not entered and the guarded final loop handles the tail, so the overflow path stays safe.
limitations: No call sites are shown, so kwset invariants (delta range, target capacity) are external; the skip-loop margin would be insufficient only if delta1 could exceed len, which contradicts standard kwset semantics and was rejected.
A theoretical non-termination at d==0 with tp==ep depends on the unshown bm_delta2_search body not advancing; the callee's standard contract assumes advancement, so it was not counted as a finding.
The memchr size argument at line 54 is safe only via the line 28 margin plus the delta1<=len assumption; both are recorded above.

verdict.summary: The only dangerous operations whose failure sets are derivable from the fragment (SSize_t overflow of the min accumulator at line 1025 and of the final RExC_maxlen write) carry saturating guards that survive the BREAK test; the remaining candidate sinks (RExC_recurse/RExC_open_parens indexing, delta/SvGROW multiplication wraps, NULL data deref) cannot be confirmed because their capacities, magnitudes, or NULL-producing paths are not present in the fragment.

evidence.reason: Decisive protective statement: it constrains the exact SSize_t values (minnext, mincount, min) consumed by the sink at line 1025, admitting only products with minnext==0 or mincount < SSize_t_MAX/minnext, and requiring min < SSize_t_MAX - minnext*mincount before the addition, so min += minnext*mincount cannot wrap (CWE-190 failure set is empty); it executes on every CURLY path before the sink and survives the BREAK test.

Protected sink: min is accumulated only after the guard at 1019-1023 verifies both the product and the sum bounds on the identical values with no intervening modification, so no admitted value reaches an unprotected overflow operation.

assumptions: mincount/maxcount are non-negative (they derive from ARG1/ARG2 quantifier counts and the fixed 1/REG_INFTY assignments of the PLUS/STAR paths).

limitations: A non-EFAULT seccomp_rule_add() failure arises from a library/environmental condition (e.g. -ENOMEM, arch-dependent -EINVAL), not directly from sandboxed-application input; this is therefore a fail-open security-control/status-handling weakness rather than a directly attacker-controlled memory-safety defect, reflected in the confidence and severity.

The same admitted witness (RTCP length word 00 01, length=8) reaches this second read at buffer offset 13 after the underflow at line 24 disables line 25's protection, exceeding the 8-byte capacity tracked by the length parameter; the missing fix is the same converted-length or minimum-length check applied before line 29 (CWE-125).

assumptions: hdr->rtcp_common.length is a 16-bit network-order field, as shown by the pj_ntohs conversion at line 24; sizeof(pjmedia_rtcp_fb_common) is 12 bytes, consistent with the +12 offset at line 25 and sizeof(*hdr) at line 28.
The analyzed host is little-endian; on a strictly big-endian host, the raw guard at line 18 would reject the witness.
PJ_ASSERT_RETURN at lines 11-12 is an assertion-family macro whose body is not shown and is not credited as a protective statement per the do-not-credit policy.
limitations: If PJ_ASSERT_RETURN were treated as executing in the analyzed configuration, its length >= sizeof(...) check at line 12 would return before the OOB read; the finding relies on the policy that such macros are not protective.

The oversized (rpsi->rpsi_bit_len + 7)/8 length stored by pj_strset at line 45 would only cause harm in a downstream consumer; pj_strset itself performs no dereference, so it is not counted as an in-fragment sink.
Header-field reads at lines 15 and 18 with length < 4 are also only assertion-protected; they were not used as the primary witness.

verdict.summary: In the outer RLE loop, `from` is advanced past the last byte and then dereferenced on line 14 before the `from == end` check executes, producing a one-past-the-end byte read.

evidence.reason: With step == 1, when the loop processes the last element (from == end - 1, admitted by line 10), line 13 advances from to end; line 14 then evaluates `*from` before the `from == end` operand, dereferencing one-past-the-end — an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The `from == end` check is evaluated after the dereference and cannot constrain it; the absent fix is an early `from == end ||` (or equivalent pre-dereference boundary check), and the witness is not blocked at any shown statement.

assumptions: `end` is an exclusive one-past-the-end boundary per the fragment's own `from < end` loop conditions.
`step == 1` is a valid value of the unconstrained `int step` parameter; the primary witness uses it.
`byte` is treated as an unsigned byte type so the 0xc0 comparisons are well-defined.
limitations: Callers and the buffer's actual allocation are not shown; the OOB access is relative to the fragment's own `end` boundary convention.
Additional paths (step > 1 jumping past end, step <= 0) were not needed for the verdict and are not evaluated.
No downstream corruption or disclosure impact is modeled; only the demonstrated one-byte OOB read.

verdict.summary: entry_count is bounded before the local-entry loop by the division check at lines 14-15 (admitted 0..floor(size/16|12), exactly matching each entry's 16/12-byte consumption); every bitstream read is preceded by a fail-closed ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE remaining-size guard; both allocations are NULL-checked. No file-derived count reaches a dangerous operation without a protective statement, so no witness survives the BLOCK test.

assumptions: ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, n) is GPAC's standard check-and-decrement guard: if ptr->size < n it returns GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE, otherwise subtracts n; each invocation's argument matches the bytes read at the immediately following statement (lines 6, 22, 25, 28, 34, 41, 44, 48, 53, 57).

ptr->size is the remaining unread byte count of the afra box at entry; ptr->local_access_entries and ptr->global_access_entries are valid lists; gf_bs_read_* provide internally bounded reads (returning 0 at end-of-stream) and gf_malloc returns NULL on failure.
The global-entry loop (line 36) lacks an upfront count check, but each iteration's reads are capped by the per-iteration size guards, bounding iterations and allocations to O(remaining size).
limitations: The expansion of the ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE macro is not shown; if it were only a decrement without a bounds return, reads could run past the box section (though gf_bs_read_* are internally bounded and entry_count is still capped by line 14).
global_entry_count (line 35) has no pre-loop division check analogous to entry_count's; this is a defense-in-depth gap only because the per-iteration size guards fail closed before each read.
gf_list_insert/GF_List internals are unshown and assumed safe for an insert index equal to the current list count.

verdict.summary: The parse-failure path is safe: result->Unref() (line 15) is followed by result.release() (line 16) on the same path, severing unique_ptr ownership before scope exit and preventing a double-delete of the freed resource; the CreateResource status is checked (lines 26-28), propagating every code except the intentionally tolerated ALREADY_EXISTS.

evidence.snippet: result.release();  // Needed due to the `->Unref` above, to prevent UAF
evidence.reason: The dangerous operation is the combination of result->Unref() (line 15), which frees the RefCounted resource when its refcount reaches zero, with the scope-exit ~unique_ptr that would otherwise `delete` the same raw pointer (double-free/UAF). Line 16 neutralizes it on the only reaching path (the if-body at lines 13-20): release() discards the raw pointer without accessing the pointee, so the destructor deletes nullptr. BREAK test passes: identity (same unique_ptr and pointer), boundary (not a bound check; ownership removal eliminates the second delete entirely), degenerate (valid even after Unref already freed the object), reach (unconditional before scope exit). This is the decisive protective statement for the NOT-VULNERABLE verdict.

assumptions: BoostedTreesEnsembleResource is RefCounted and `new` produces refcount 1, so the failing-path Unref() drops it to 0 and frees the object; the unique_ptr default deleter would otherwise `delete` the same pointer at scope exit.
C++ `new` throws rather than returning NULL, so `result` is non-null when used.
CreateResource's ALREADY_EXISTS code is an intended idempotent-create outcome, and every other status is propagated by OP_REQUIRES_OK (fail-closed).
limitations: The shape/capacity of the tensors consumed by scalar<int64>()() (line 5) and scalar<tstring>()() (line 14) is not declared or validated inside the fragment (no NumElements or capacity line shown), so an empty-tensor OOB read cannot be confirmed under the OOB rules requiring an in-fragment capacity.

Whether CreateResource (line 25) disposes of the transferred pointer on non-OK or ALREADY_EXISTS statuses is callee behavior not visible in the fragment; no in-fragment leak or double-free is demonstrable.

verdict.summary: Heap out-of-bounds read in string_scan_range: for a scan range of 1-3 bytes (to <= 3), the ut64 expression `to - 4` in the guard at line 77 underflows to a huge value, admitting needle=0, and r_read_le32 then reads 4 bytes from a buffer allocated with only len bytes at line 27.

evidence.reason: r_read_le32 reads exactly 4 bytes from buf + (needle - from); buf's capacity is len = to - from (calloc at line 27) with 1 <= len <= ST32_MAX admitted by line 23. For from=0, to=3 (len=3), the guard `needle < to - 4` at line 77 evaluates 3 - 4 in ut64 and wraps to a huge value, so needle=0 passes it; the 4-byte read then extends one byte past the 3-byte buffer. The guard fails the boundary/degenerate leg of the BREAK test, and no later statement blocks the witness (BLOCK test passes); the absent one-statement fix is an underflow-safe comparison such as `if (needle + 4 < to)` or `if (to - needle >= 4)` before the read. This is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

assumptions: buf capacity equals the len passed to calloc at line 27, with 1 <= len <= ST32_MAX enforced at line 23.
r_read_le32 performs a fixed 4-byte read per its standard semantics.
The witness takes the environment path where RABIN2_CHARSET is unset (lines 43-68 skipped) and is_breaked is NULL or returns false (lines 70, 73).
limitations: from/to are internal-helper parameters with no shown call site; the witness uses values (from=0, to=3) that every shown check admits, but reaching the bug requires the actual caller to supply a range smaller than 4 bytes.

The RABIN2_CHARSET branch (lines 44-68) was not counted as a separate finding: outlen = len * 4 can overflow int for len > 2^30, but r_charset_encode_str's handling of a negative outlen is not part of the shown fragment or standard semantics.
r_utf16le_decode / r_utf32le_decode (lines 132/137) are assumed to respect their length argument; any OOB inside those helpers is not demonstrated in the fragment.

verdict.summary: Every entry-point-derived value reaching the EXIF value-building and copy sinks is constrained by shown guards: format/components validation (L617-623), multiplication-overflow guard (L625-626), IFD q-bounds (L610-611), dir_offset+number_bytes <= length checks (L638-643), p-range gates (L652-653, L731-732), SIZE_MAX-guarded number_bytes+1 allocations with NULL checks, and the MaxTextExtent length clamps (L40-41, L66-67) in both value-formatting macros. No witness survives the BLOCK test.

evidence.reason: Protective clamp in EXIFMultipleValues: FormatLocaleString returns the would-be length, so without this cap the next iteration's size argument MaxTextExtent-length could underflow and the stack buffer[MaxTextExtent] write would escape; the clamp forces length in [0, MaxTextExtent-1], making every following write stay inside the buffer. Survives BREAK (identity, boundary, degenerate, reach).

Identical protective clamp in EXIFMultipleFractions; same excluded set ({length > MaxTextExtent-1}) applied on every iteration of the fraction-formatting loop, preventing size-argument underflow into the 2-integer fraction formatter.

Offsets the p-pointer only while dir_offset+number_bytes <= length, so any value read / copied across number_bytes bytes at p (BYTE, UNDEFINED, STRING, and all EXIFMultiple* format reads) cannot cross exif+length; combined with L638-641 this is the reaching-path bound that makes the later p-gates effective.

Explicit STRING-format gate requiring p+number_bytes <= exif+length before the copy loop reads p[i], i < number_bytes, and before the allocation number_bytes+1 is written through value[number_bytes]='\0'.

assumptions: ReadPropertyByte/UnsignedShort/SignedShort/UnsignedLong/SignedLong consume their fixed byte widths and are only reached after the shown length checks guarantee the bytes are inside the profile buffer (length>=16 at L549-550, dir/offset gates).
components is a signed 32-bit value (<= 2^31-1) and max tag_bytes[format]=8, so number_bytes <= 2^34 on 64-bit size_t; the L625-626 guard fully prevents multiplication wrap.

FormatLocaleString bounds its output by the size argument (snprintf semantics), which is why the length clamps (L40-41, L66-67) are sufficient; AcquireString follows ImageMagick's contract of allocating at least MagickPathExtent, keeping the L783/792/796/799 key writes in bounds.
limitations: The capacity of key (result of AcquireString(property)) is not declared or computed in the fragment, so the FormatLocaleString(key,MaxTextExtent,...) writes (L783, L792, L796, L799) cannot be confirmed as an OOB under the in-fragment-capacity rule; under a naive strdup assumption they would be a candidate, but under AcquireString's allocation floor they are bounded.
NewSplayTree's return value is not NULL-checked before GetValueFromSplayTree/AddValueToSplayTree (L576, L612-614); without a shown in-fragment failure path this is not confirmable and is demoted.
Unaligned float/double dereferences (L720, L725) are style/UB concerns with no shown bounds impact, not classified as a vulnerability here.
No inference was made from which member of the pair the fragment appears to be; the verdict rests only on the Phase 2-4 guard and BLOCK/BREAK analyses.

verdict.summary: All dangerous operations in the fragment are protected: argv indexing is bounded by the crun_assert_n_args check at line 17, the args array is allocated with argc+1 entries (line 42) so the loop and NULL terminator at lines 43-45 stay in bounds, and strtoll at line 30 is guarded by the getenv NULL check at line 28. Remaining concerns (argc overflow, LISTEN_FDS value overflow, cap/cap_size coupling) are not demonstrable within the shown code.

evidence.reason: argv[first_arg] read (also read at line 92) is protected by line 17: crun_assert_n_args (argc - first_arg, exec_options.process ? 1 : 2, -1) enforces argc - first_arg >= 1 on every path before this use, so with argp_parse's standard first_arg in [0, argc] the index is at most argc-1. Guard identity holds (same int value, unmodified), boundary (first_arg == argc-1) is admitted and in-range, and reach is satisfied; no unattacked residual value reaches the read.

Writes into process->args are bounded by the capacity declared at line 42, xmalloc0 ((argc + 1) * sizeof (*process->args)), giving indices 0..argc; the loop at line 43 admits i up to argc-first_arg-1 and the NULL terminator writes index argc-first_arg, which is <= argc since first_arg >= 0 (argp semantics). The argv read reaches at most index argc-1. BREAK test passes at the exact boundary and under degenerate first_arg == 0.

The getenv result fed to strtoll is guarded by the NULL check at line 28 (if (getenv ("LISTEN_FDS"))); no environment mutation appears between the guard and use, so the admitted set excludes NULL and the guard identity, boundary, degenerate, and reach tests all pass. strtoll's numeric result is not consumed by any fragment-demonstrable sink.

assumptions: crun_assert_n_args (n, min, -1) terminates the program when n < min, per its standard assert-n-args semantics (crun_fail-style exit); it is a runtime check, not a debug-only/NDEBUG-compiled assertion.
argp_parse (glibc standard semantics) sets first_arg to an index in [0, argc] and, for exec_options string-array fields (cap, env), keeps the count and storage consistent.
xmalloc0 and xstrdup abort on allocation failure and never return NULL.
argv contains argc valid entries followed by argv[argc] == NULL (C standard).
limitations: The capabilities block (lines 59-77): a cap_size > 0 value with exec_options.cap == NULL or shorter than cap_size would be an OOB read in dup_array, but no shown producer can derive that inconsistent pair; it depends on unshown argp_parse/run_argp option-table behavior, so the witness fails the BLOCK test.

Potential int overflow in (argc + 1) * sizeof at line 42 and in preserve_fds += listen_fds at line 31 would require argc near INT_MAX or a crafted LISTEN_FDS value; the former terminates in xmalloc0 before any write and the latter is consumed only by the unshown callee at line 92, so neither is a fragment-demonstrable memory-safety flaw (robustness/DoS concern only).

If crun_assert_n_args were a no-op contradicting its name, argv[first_arg] could read argv[argc] (a valid NULL pointer) and pass NULL into the unshown init_libcrun_context/libcrun_container_exec_with_options; rejected as a witness because it requires an unshown callee to violate its documented semantics.

process->args_len is set to argc (line 41) while only argc - first_arg entries plus a NULL terminator are populated; any downstream consumer iterating args_len full range is outside the fragment and was not evaluated.

verdict.summary: rsi_init_usb_interface NULL-checks both allocations before use (rsi_dev at line 8, tx_buffer at line 24), treats both helper return values as errors with cleanup, and initializes status on every error path; no dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: kzalloc at line 7 can return NULL; the check at line 8 executes before the first dereference of rsi_dev (line 11) on every reaching path and excludes NULL, resolving the NULL-deref candidate PRESENT. The BREAK test passes: same pointer, no intervening modification, no degenerate admitted value, and the early return covers all paths.

kmalloc at line 23 can return NULL; the check at line 24 excludes NULL before any use of tx_buffer, and fail_rx (which kfree's tx_buffer at line 53) is reachable only after this check passes. The BREAK test passes, resolving that candidate PRESENT.

The return of rsi_usb_init_rx is fully checked: any non-zero result assigns status = -ENOMEM (line 31) and jumps to fail_rx, which frees tx_buffer before freeing rsi_dev. Similarly, rsi_find_bulk_in_and_out_endpoints is checked at line 15 with status = -EINVAL (line 16). No security-relevant status is discarded, and status is initialized on every path to return at line 58.

assumptions: pfunction is a non-NULL struct usb_interface supplied by the USB core, consistent with the plain-parameter rule; interface_to_usbdev and usb_set_intfdata require it.
rsi_find_bulk_in_and_out_endpoints and rsi_usb_init_rx follow the kernel convention of returning 0 on success and non-zero on failure, as evidenced by their boolean use in the fragment.
kzalloc/kmalloc may return NULL and kfree(NULL) is safe, matching the allocations and error paths shown.
limitations: adapter->rsi_dev remains set after fail_eps frees rsi_dev (lines 55-56); any later use would require an unshown caller and is out of scope for this fragment.
The body of rsi_usb_init_rx is not shown, so internal leaks or partial-state issues are not verifiable here.
No NULL guard appears before the uses of pfunction (lines 12, 15, 20-21), but a NULL pfunction can only be supplied by an unshown caller, which is a limitation rather than a confirmed finding.

verdict.summary: elo_probe() acquires a USB device reference with usb_get_dev() but the err_free error path only calls kfree(priv); the matching usb_put_dev() is absent, so any hid_parse()/hid_hw_start() failure leaks the reference and prevents device teardown.

evidence.reason: The reference acquired by usb_get_dev() at line 16 is never released: both error paths (goto err_free at lines 23 and 29, taken when hid_parse() or hid_hw_start() returns nonzero) reach line 39, which frees only the container priv, and the fragment contains no usb_put_dev() call; the absent one-statement fix is usb_put_dev(udev) (or usb_put_dev(priv->usbdev)) before kfree(priv), so a failing probe leaks one usb_device kref per attempt (CWE-772, missing release of resource after effective lifetime).

assumptions: usb_get_dev() increments the usb_device kref and requires a matching usb_put_dev() (standard kref semantics); the successful path stores priv in hdev via hid_set_drvdata() at line 18, with the matching release expected in an unshown remove callback.
hid_is_usb(hdev) at line 7 implies hdev->dev.parent is a struct usb_interface, so the cast at line 15 is not treated as a NULL/type-confusion finding.
limitations: The safety of to_usb_interface(hdev->dev.parent) at line 15 relies on the kernel invariant that USB HID devices have a usb_interface parent; no in-fragment producer can make that pointer NULL, so no CWE-476 finding is reported.

The leak's impact (resource exhaustion / failure to free the usb_device) requires repeated failed probes, e.g., replugging a device whose descriptors force hid_parse() or hid_hw_start() to fail; each failure leaks one reference.
The discarded queue_delayed_work() return at line 34 is standard work scheduling and is not treated as a security-relevant unchecked status.

verdict.summary: The LSTMBlockCell Compute kernel passes the rank-1 peephole weight tensors (wci, wcf, wco) to the LSTMBlockCellFprop functor without validating their lengths against cell_size. A caller can supply a rank-1 wci/wcf/wco with dim_size(0) < cell_size (or 0); with peephole enabled the functor reads these vectors at indices [0, cell_size), producing an out-of-bounds read.

evidence.snippet:
functor::LSTMBlockCellFprop<Device, T, USE_CUBLAS, gate_layout>(
        batch_size, input_size, cell_size)(
        ctx, device, forget_bias_, cell_clip_, use_peephole_,
        x_tensor->matrix<T>(), cs_prev_tensor->matrix<T>(),
        h_prev_tensor->matrix<T>(), w_tensor->matrix<T>(), wci_tensor->vec<T>(),
        wcf_tensor->vec<T>(), wco_tensor->vec<T>(), b_tensor->vec<T>(),
        xh_tensor.matrix<T>(), i_tensor->matrix<T>(), cs_tensor->matrix<T>(),
        f_tensor->matrix<T>(), o_tensor->matrix<T>(), ci_tensor->matrix<T>(),
        co_tensor->matrix<T>(), gates_tensor.matrix<T>(),
        h_tensor->matrix<T>());
evidence.reason: wci/wcf/wco are entry-point tensors whose only shown constraint is the rank check dims()==1 (lines 130, 134, 138), which admits every 1-D length k including k < cell_size; cell_size is taken from cs_prev_tensor->dim_size(1) (line 28). No dim_size(0) == cell_size check exists, so an attacker-supplied short wci (e.g. k = cell_size - 1 or 0) passes all guards and reaches the functor call at lines 177-178, where LSTM peephole semantics index the vectors up to cell_size, causing an out-of-bounds read beyond the k-element buffer (CWE-125). The missing fix is an OP_REQUIRES equality check of each peephole vector's dim_size(0) against cell_size before the call.

assumptions: use_peephole_ is an attacker-configurable op attribute as shown in the call at line 175; with it true the functor consumes the peephole vectors.

LSTMBlockCellFprop standard forward-pass semantics read the peephole weight vectors elementwise with vectors of length cell_size, per the call-site arguments (cell_size and the unvalidated vec() views).
limitations: The exact indexing statement is inside the unshown functor body; the finding is anchored at the call site that forwards the unvalidated views, which lowers confidence.
If use_peephole_ is false the peephole vectors may be unused; that configuration does not reach the failing read.

Integer-overflow candidates on TensorShape({batch_size, cell_size * 4}) and TensorShape({batch_size, input_size + cell_size}) were demoted: overflow requires implausible dims (~2^61 elements) that no real tensor can back.
The typo in the wcf rank-check message referencing wci_tensor->dims() (line 136) is cosmetic and non-security.

verdict.summary: The fragment contains no memory, injection, or unchecked-status sink: the sole security-relevant operation is the avc_has_perm call at lines 3-5, whose access-decision status is returned directly, and no shown value can reach an unprotected operation.

evidence.reason: The only security-relevant operation is the authorization call at lines 3-5. Its subject and target are u32 SIDs (task_sid_subj(parent), task_sid_obj(current)), so no NULL dereference path exists; the check executes unconditionally on the sole straight-line path, and the returned status is propagated immediately as the function's return value at line 5, leaving no unchecked security-relevant return and no admitted superset. No producer inside the fragment generates a failing value, so no witness survives the BLOCK test; the operation resolves PRESENT.

assumptions: avc_has_perm returns an access-decision status that the fragment propagates directly as its own return value.
limitations: A NULL parent would require an unshown caller to violate the hook contract; no NULL-producing statement is shown, so the NULL-deref candidate was demoted per the reverse-protection-scan rule.
Whether task_sid_subj/task_sid_obj are the semantically correct SID-helper choices for this hook is not derivable from the shown fragment, so no wrong-target authorization finding is asserted.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment is protected: the dereference of the callback-returned list at line 43 is fully gated by `if (rettv.v_type == VAR_LIST)` (line 40), which excludes every non-list return type before `vval.v_list` is extracted, and the `dict_alloc_lock` failure is checked at line 23 before any dict use. No dangerous operation admits an unconstrained value.

evidence.reason: The dereference at line 43 is reachable only when `call_callback` returns OK (line 38) and `rettv.v_type == VAR_LIST` (line 40). The type-equality guard is the immediate, exclusive gate before the union field `vval.v_list` is assigned at line 42 and dereferenced at line 43, with no intervening statement able to modify `rettv`, so the guard constrains the exact value the sink consumes (identity pass) and admits only values carrying a valid list pointer (boundary/degenerate pass, reach pass). `qftf_list`'s NULL initializations at lines 4 and 37 are overwritten on this path, so no shown NULL producer reaches the sink; the named absent fix (a type check before extracting `vval.v_list`) is present verbatim at line 40.

assumptions: `call_callback` fills `rettv` with a well-formed Vimscript typval on OK and a VAR_LIST typval always carries a valid non-NULL `v_list` pointer (standard callee semantics); the union field is therefore safe to dereference exactly when line 40 admits it.
`qfl`, `qf_winid`, `start_idx`, `end_idx` are ordinary parameters; the fragment provides no way to make `qfl` NULL, so its dereferences at lines 14/30 rely only on the caller's contract.
The list returned by the callback is kept alive because `lv_refcount` is incremented at line 43 before `clear_tv(&rettv)` at line 45.
limitations: A NULL `qfl` supplied only by an out-of-scope caller would crash at lines 14/30; no NULL producer exists in the fragment, so this is recorded as a limitation, not a finding.
If `call_callback` could return OK with `v_type == VAR_LIST` and `v_list == NULL` (contrary to its standard semantics), line 43 would be a NULL dereference; no such producer is shown in the fragment.
The `IS_QF_LIST` macro expansion is not shown; it only feeds a dict number value at line 28 and is not itself a sink.
`clear_tv` and `dict_unref` bodies are unshown; their return values are ignored by design and no shown statement uses freed memory after them.

verdict.summary: When num_spans == 1, the do-while body executes once and unconditionally reads spans[1], one element past the supplied 1-element span array (out-of-bounds read).

evidence.reason: spans has exactly num_spans elements; the only count guard, line 9 'if (num_spans == 0)', admits num_spans == 1, and the do-while (lines 14-90) with post-test 'while (--num_spans > 1)' executes its body once for that count, reading spans[1] (index 1) against a 1-element array. No statement on the path excludes count 1, so the residual range [1, UINT_MAX] reaches the index-1 access; the absent fix is a guard requiring num_spans >= 2 (or equivalent single-span handling) before the spans[1] read. Mechanism: out-of-bounds read of one span past the array, CWE-125.

assumptions: spans points to an array of exactly num_spans elements, as implied by the parameter name and the fragment's own spans[0] dereference at line 12.
The early return at lines 9-10 is the only count validation in the function.
limitations: The capacity of r->_buf is not declared in the fragment, so the coverage-buffer writes at lines 83-85 cannot be confirmed as out-of-bounds.
pixman_image_composite32 destination/width arguments carry no shown capacity, so no failure is derivable for those calls.
External caller provenance of spans is unshown (internal-helper parameter with no call site), but the finding is derived wholly from the fragment's own admitted count of 1.

verdict.summary: OP_ARGARY (line 677) and OP_BLKPUSH (lines 1177/1181) read one mrb_value past the end of the captured environment stack: the guards at lines 644 and 1171 admit MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, but the keyword read requires length >= m1+r+m2+3 because stack = e->stack + 1.

evidence.reason: Operand fields m1/r/m2/kd (lines 625-628) are unconstrained bytecode values; for lv>0, uvenv (642) is non-NULL (643) and stack = e->stack+1 (646), so stack[m1+r+m2+1] = e->stack[m1+r+m2+2]. The only guard, line 644 `if (MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+1) goto L_NOSUPER;`, admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) == m1+r+m2+2, while the access convention shown at lines 260-261 (e->stack[b] valid iff b < MRB_ENV_LEN(e)) requires len >= m1+r+m2+3 for this index. With kd=1 and len == m1+r+m2+2 the read dereferences e->stack[len], one slot past the env stack: off-by-one out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). The absent fix is the one-larger bound `MRB_ENV_LEN(e) <= m1+r+m2+2` at line 644.

Same off-by-one pattern: OP_BLKPUSH decodes m1/r/m2/kd (lines 1160-1163), sets stack = e->stack+1 (1175), and the guard at lines 1170-1171 admits MRB_ENV_LEN(e) >= m1+r+m2+2. With kd=1 the read stack[m1+r+m2+1] = e->stack[m1+r+m2+2] (also evaluated at line 1177) requires len >= m1+r+m2+3 by the convention of lines 260-261, so len == m1+r+m2+2 reads one slot past the environment stack: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125). verdict.summary: In get_visual_text, *lenp is derived from unconstrained column differences (lines 24/29) and only guarded below by `if (*lenp > 0)` (line 33); no shown statement clamps it to the line length, so `(*pp)[*lenp - 1]` and `*pp + (*lenp - 1)` can read past the NUL terminator, a heap out-of-bounds read.

The surviving witness is a single fragile boundary (count exactly INT_MAX with yanklen == 1), and its practical impact is a clean allocation failure plus int-overflow UB, not memory corruption; confidence is kept at 0.6 for that reason.

conn->structured_replies is reachable in the same connection: the client first sends NBD_OPT_STRUCTURED_REPLY with optlen==0, which sets it true (lines 330-359).

The client is fixed-newstyle (sets NBD_FLAG_FIXED_NEWSTYLE) and the server TLS guard at lines 60-65 is not tripped (tls != 2, or TLS already negotiated), so the SET/LIST_META_CONTEXT branch is reachable.

limitations: check_export_name (line 403) and check_string (line 460) bodies are unshown; if check_export_name independently enforced len <= optlen-8, the meta-context path would be bounded by that callee and this witness would not fire — per the callee rules that bound is not derivable from the fragment and is therefore not credited.

The strndup sink's OOB past a small allocation additionally depends on the uninitialized byte data[optlen] being non-NUL; the memcpy sink at line 426 (guard wrap) does not depend on heap contents once reached and is the decisive witness.

verdict.summary: Every dangerous operation in the fragment is protected by a verbatim guard that survives the BREAK test: the non-timeseries division at line 62 is preceded by the `numRecords <= 100` bail at line 14 (excluded set numRecords <= 100, so the divisor is >= 5.05); the timeseries division at line 124 and the `*bucketUnpacker` dereferences at lines 131/143 are preceded by the `!(bucketUnpacker && numRecords)` bail at line 91; the random-cursor null and plan-executor status results are checked at lines 35 and 162 before their uses. evidence.reason: This bail guard protects the division at line 62: the `numRecords <= 100` term means every non-timeseries path that reaches `sampleSize / (numRecords * kMaxSampleRatioForRandCursor)` has numRecords >= 101, making the double divisor `numRecords * 0.05` >= 5.05 (never zero or NaN-producing); numRecords is not modified between line 14 and line 62, so the guard-identity audit passes.

On every timeseries path reaching the ratio division at line 124 and the `*bucketUnpacker` dereferences at lines 131 and 143, this guard returns early unless numRecords is non-zero (excluding the zero-divisor case for the denominator `kCoefficient * numRecords * gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount`) and bucketUnpacker is engaged (excluding disengaged-optional dereference); the guard precedes all three uses with no intervening modification.

The status returned by `plan_executor_factory::make` (line 154) is checked with `isOK()` before `execStatus.getValue()` is used at line 169; the failure path returns `execStatus.getStatus()` at line 163, so no unchecked failure status reaches the returned executor value.

assumptions: gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount is a positive server constant; its declaration is not shown, so the fragment itself only guarantees a non-zero numRecords factor in the timeseries denominator.
coll, expCtx, and CollectionShardingState::get results are treated as valid non-NULL pointers because the fragment contains no in-fragment NULL producer for them.
limitations: If gTimeseriesBucketMaxCount were <= 0 with a non-zero numRecords, the floating-point division at line 124 could produce NaN in that unshown configuration; the value is a server parameter, not attacker-controlled, and no producer or type for it is shown in the fragment.
A negative sampleSize or negative numRecords on the timeseries path yields a sign-flipped or clamped ratio, but reaches no memory-safety, injection, or NULL operation inside the fragment.
The behavior of the downstream TrialStage/SampleFromTimeseriesBucket/UnpackTimeseriesBucket stages is unshown, so any impact of an extreme ratio there is out of scope.

verdict.summary: dnsc_load_local_data computes rrlen as a size_t sum but stores it in uint16_t (line 19). The only guard (line 40) caps provider_name length at 0xffff0000 (32-bit scale), so a config-supplied provider name can make rrlen wrap modulo 65536 to 0. Then rrlen - 1 promotes to int -1 and converts to SIZE_MAX as snprintf's size argument (line 55), causing an unbounded heap write into a 0-byte malloc buffer (CWE-787), rooted in the 16-bit size truncation (CWE-190).

evidence.reason: provider_name length is entry-point config data with residual range P < 0xffff0000 (guard at line 40, operator >=, threshold far above the uint16_t sink), and rrlen (uint16_t, line 19) is assigned P + strlen(ttl_class_type) + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2 at lines 45-49, truncating modulo 65536; for any sizeof(struct SignedCert) >= 1 there is a P in [0,65536) with the sum ≡ 0 (mod 65536), so rrlen becomes 0 and malloc(0) (line 50) succeeds on glibc; at line 55 rrlen - 1 is int -1 and converts to SIZE_MAX as snprintf's size, writing the format string and provider name past the 0-byte heap object (CWE-787), caused by the size wraparound (CWE-190). The guard fails the BREAK test on precision/boundary (it constrains a 32-bit length, not the 16-bit truncated size) and the absent fix is size_t rrlen or a check that keeps rrlen >= 2 (rejecting strlen(provider_name) >= 0x10000 - 17 - 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert)); the witness survives the BLOCK test because no statement between lines 40 and 55 excludes the wrapped value.

assumptions: sizeof(struct SignedCert) >= 1, so for any actual size a provider-name length in [0, 65536) exists with P + 17 + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) ≡ 0 (mod 65536)
glibc-style malloc(0) returns a non-NULL pointer; on implementations where it returns NULL, the early return at lines 51-53 blocks this particular write witness
dnscenv->provider_name is a config-supplied (entry-point) NUL-terminated string
the missing semicolon after `continue` at line 43 is treated as a rendering artifact of an otherwise valid fragment
limitations: unchecked strdup() results at lines 6 and 71 could flow as NULL into cfg_str2list_insert/cfg_strlist_insert on OOM, but the callee bodies are unshown, so a NULL dereference is not confirmable from the fragment
signed_certs/signed_certs_count and rotated_certs/rotated_certs_count capacities are not shown, so no out-of-bounds claim is made for the loops at lines 15 and 23
on malloc(0) == NULL platforms the line-55 write is blocked by the early return; the rrlen truncation defect itself remains, but no memory-safety witness would be demonstrable on such implementations

if (((unsigned long)Bitmap_Head.biWidth) > (unsigned int)0x7fffffff / Bitmap_Head.biBitCnt ||

unsigned long overflowTest = Bitmap_Head.biWidth * Bitmap_Head.biBitCnt;
  if (overflowTest / Bitmap_Head.biWidth != Bitmap_Head.biBitCnt) {
evidence.reason: Second overflow validation for the width*bitdepth product that rowbytes (line 321) and ReadImage (lines 341-345) consume; in unsigned arithmetic r/w == b holds if and only if w*b did not wrap, so any wrapped value is diverted to cleanup before reaching the size computations, and the division is safe because biWidth is nonzero (line 267).

Cap on the palette-entry count passed to ReadColorMap at line 334: ColormapSize is computed at line 253 as unsigned 32-bit arithmetic (non-negative) or overwritten at line 258 with 1<<biBitCnt (<= 256), and the cap admits at most 256 entries, exactly matching ColorMap[256][3] declared at line 7 with last index 255; no intervening assignment changes the value before the sink, so the boundary holds.

ReadColorMap and ReadImage honor the sizes passed to them (standard size-parameter semantics); their bodies are not shown.

verdict.summary: uint16_t rrlen truncates the computed allocation size (lines 40-44); a provider name of length 65536 - (strlen(ttl_class_type) + 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) + 2) makes rrlen == 0, the unchecked malloc(0) result reaches snprintf whose size operand rrlen - 1 wraps to SIZE_MAX, causing a heap buffer overflow at line 50.

A witness uses signed_certs_count >= 1 with the first certificate not rotated; nothing in the fragment constrains or forbids this.
sizeof(struct SignedCert) >= 1, so the 4*sizeof(struct SignedCert) term is positive.
limitations: The same 16-bit truncation can also underflow the size operands at the snprintf calls on lines 54, 56, and 65; they share the same root cause and are not counted as independent findings.

memcpy(&serial, cert->serial, sizeof serial) at line 29 assumes the serial member is at least 4 bytes; its layout is not shown, so a serial OOB read cannot be confirmed.
strdup() results at lines 6-7 and 66 are not NULL-checked; no in-fragment failure path can prove NULL reaches the insert functions.

TabPageIdxs is indexed per screen column and the fragment's own access convention bounds valid indices by Columns (line 275: mouse_col < Columns); its literal allocation is not declared in the fragment.

The click-path guard (line 275) admits negative mouse_col, but no shown producer inside the fragment can drive mouse_col negative, so no separate lower-bound finding is confirmed.

Internal sinks (do_put, goto_tabpage, stuffcharReadbuff, findmatch) receive only values already guarded in the fragment and their bodies are unshown; no NULL producer exists for oap or cursor pointers, so no NULL-deref or injection finding is confirmed.

verdict.summary: The directory-entry name length is fully constrained before the buffer writes: line 71's `dire->size >= SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN` guard admits only 0..SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1, so memcpy's `dire->size + 1` and the NUL at `dire->size + 1` stay within the declared SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN+1 name region, and dirs indexing is covered by the realloc growth invariant.

dire->size is an unsigned 16-bit field, so the guard's admitted range is 0..SQUASHFS_NAME_LEN-1 (no negative values admitted).

limitations: The capacity of directory_table is not declared in the fragment, so out-of-bounds reads at lines 52, 66, and 76 from directory_table + bytes cannot be confirmed and are demoted.
